tieu_de: Sun Spectrum Projection /
tom_tat: The Buddha's universal light is the light of Buddha's wisdom, shining to all sentient beings. It is to illuminate the minds of sentient beings, to destroy all greed, anger and ignorance. It is to illuminate darkness into light, to eliminate eighty-four...
noi_dung:
Sun Spectrum Projection /

The Buddha's universal light is the light of Buddha's wisdom, shining to all sentient beings. It is to illuminate the minds of sentient beings, to destroy all greed, anger and ignorance. It is to illuminate darkness into light, to eliminate eighty-four thousand habits and bad habits. When we study Buddhism, we eliminate greed, anger, and ignorance and no longer have attachments. Why can't we see Buddha's light? We study Buddha's teachings to open our wisdom, so isn't that the light of Buddha? If the more we study, the more confused we become and do not understand the true teachings of Buddha, it is because we do not want to eliminate our habits. Don't ask, why does Buddha's light not shine? Without opening your own wisdom, greed, anger and ignorance remain intact, refusing to change at all, so even if the Buddha light wants to shine, there is no place to shine.

This is not whether the Buddha light shines or not. It is shining without shining, not shining but shining, which means: when the light of one's own wisdom appears, the Buddha's light shines. If the light of our wisdom does not appear, the Buddha light will not shine.

Buddha light is like an electric company. As in our house, we are equipped with an electrical system including electric wires, electric lights, all connected together. But if we don't press the power button, the light bulb will not light up and the room will still be dark. Why? Because the electricity is not flowing, it has no effect. Therefore we need to press the electric button. Once you press the button, the light will immediately illuminate dark places. The minds of us sentient beings are like buttons. If we press the button to open our mind, Buddha light will shine in. If the door of the mind is not open, even if the Buddha's light shines, it will not shine. This example is shallow, but its argument is the same. Ladies and Gentlemen! Quickly open the door of your mind to receive the light of Buddha's wisdom. So you are illuminated by the Buddha's light.

Lecture on July 4, 1980

Kim Son Pagoda, Gold Mountain Monastery

tieu_de: Key to Enlightenment /
tom_tat: How do people become enlightened? Enlightenment is like opening a lock. The lock is used to lock the door of the house, preventing you from entering or leaving. So you must have a key to open the door. Otherwise, you will be…
noi_dung:
Key to Enlightenment /

How do people become enlightened? Enlightenment is like opening a lock. The lock is used to lock the door of the house, preventing you from entering or leaving. So you must have a key to open the door. Otherwise, you will be locked in your house forever. So where is this key? It's right in your body, it's easy to find. So how to find it? While you are meditating, reciting Buddha's name, and reciting Mantras, that is when you are looking for the key. So when will I find it? This matter must be determined by your level of practice. If one is diligent, one can find it very quickly. And if someone is lazy, they will never find it, not only in this life, but also in the next life will not find it. This principle is also very simple.

If your mind is locked, that locked mind is ignorance, it can make your pure and bright mind turn into a dark, polluted mind. When the situation comes, if you don't have the wisdom to judge and distinguish between good and evil, you will do crazy, crazy things. But if you practice effectively, you will break through ignorance. That means finding the key, the locked mind will naturally open. After the luminous wisdom appears, no matter what you encounter, you will have no troubles.

What is ignorance? Simply put, it is dark and dark, everything is unknown. Because people who do not understand the truth lock their minds, they cannot become enlightened. In the Tang Dynasty, during the Emperor Zong Dynasty, there was a eunuch named Ngu Trieu An. The eunuch asked the National Teacher: "What is ignorance?" The national teacher said: "You are just a petty general, so what right do you have to ask about Buddha Dharma?" Upon hearing that, the eunuch immediately became angry. The national teacher then laughed and said: "That means ignorance, right?" That's why it is said: "The fire of ignorance can destroy the entire forest of merit."

People have enough conditions to become enlightened today because they have practiced many good deeds in many previous lives, so in this life they can achieve it. If they had not practiced many good deeds in the past, they would not have been able to become enlightened in this life. You all want enlightenment, right? First of all, you must know how to prepare to practice, only then can you have hope of enlightenment.

Why did Shakyamuni Buddha become a Buddha in this life? Because He "cultivated blessings and wisdom in three periods, and hundreds of eons of perfect appearance," means that He cultivated blessings and wisdom for three great Aṅgha periods, cultivated thirty-two forms of merit, and cultivated eighty beauties in a hundred great eons. Therefore, he sat under the Bodhi tree, and in the middle of the night, he looked up at the bright stars and became enlightened. If he had not practiced in his previous lives, he would not have been able to become a Buddha in this life.

Lecture on July 12, 1980

Who recites Buddha's name?

Now is the time for us to discuss. So if anyone has any problem, just raise it so everyone can research and discuss together. Someone asked about the question "Who recites Buddha's name"? As the Vajra Sutra says: "If you don't want to stay, you will give birth to a strange mind." So if there is a place, that means staying, but if there is no place to stay, it means not thinking good, not thinking evil, it is right there that you apply effort. If we pay attention to a place and then think about whether it's good or not, that's an attachment. Practicing practice means cultivating to the point where there is no more attachment, no attachment to anything, even the body forgets. You don't even have a body, so what else are you attached to?

When meditating, we should not think about anything, but just remember "Who recites Buddha's name?" Who is reciting Buddha's name? That is, find this "Who". Once you find "Who", then it is time for enlightenment. If you can't find it, you have to search for it for a day, for ten days, you have to search for it, for a hundred days, you have to search for it, for a thousand days, you have to search for it, for ten thousand days, you have to search for it, one year, ten years, a hundred years, a thousand years, ten thousand years, just to find it. Until I find it, that's it.

Don't expect it too quickly, because this is not like smoking opium, where once you smoke it, you'll be addicted. It's not that easy! Because if it's easy, it's a deceitful method. The true way of cultivating is to put effort into it yourself. We shouldn't have the same idea as the farmer. Because he wanted to help the rice grow quickly, he pulled the rice plants a little higher so that they could grow quickly too.

a little more. That is a wrong thought!

The question "Who recites Buddha's name?" can cut off all delusions and desires, and kill all ten great armies of demons. This word "Ai" is the precious sword of Vajra King, it cuts everything cleanly, until there is no place left to cling to. "Everything that has a form is an illusion. If anyone sees that all forms are non-forms, he can see the Tathagata." If there is still an attachment, it is the human mind, the mind of sentient beings. If there is no attachment, then it is the path of the mind. When we sit in meditation without thinking about this word "Who", false thoughts will arise so enlightenment cannot be achieved. Using this first line when meditating is using poison for poison, using false thoughts to control false thoughts, and also using one false thought to tame many false thoughts. We use it forever until the mountains and waters end and there is no longer any way to go, then it is at that place of turning around that we will be enlightened.

Lecture on September 9, 1980

tieu_de: No Accept All /
tom_tat: In this world, whether good or bad, they teach people enlightenment. Being good teaches us enlightenment from a good place; being bad teaches us enlightenment from a bad place. Both good and bad can make us enlightened. If we could…
noi_dung:
No Accept All /

In this world, whether good or bad, they teach people enlightenment. Being good teaches us enlightenment from a good place; being bad teaches us enlightenment from a bad place. Both good and bad can make us enlightened. If we can be enlightened from both good and bad, there will be no problem. If we are not enlightened in the good, we will be attached to this good. If we are not enlightened in the bad, we will cling to the bad. Regardless of whether it is a good attachment or a bad attachment, it is still an attachment. Once we have such an attachment, we will not be able to achieve spiritual karma. We must see through both the good and the bad. If we encounter favorable or unfavorable circumstances, we can handle them peacefully, then we will not be swayed by the situation.

In the Diamond Sutra it is said:

“There is absolutely no dharma,

Like a dream, a shadow,

Like an electric heron.

The eagle's actions are like a shop."

This means that all conditioned dharmas in the world are like dreams and are not real. It's like a bubble floating on water, it's not real. Just like a shadow, it's there but you can't grasp it. Also like dew drops, like lightning, in the blink of an eye it disappears, so observing like that is truly insightful. After understanding, you need to let go. If we don't let go and keep clinging to this and that, we will not achieve freedom. Whether it is favorable or unfavorable circumstances, we should let go of everything. Even if we don't have any attachments, then we can achieve freedom.

Lecture on September 10, 1980

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas in its early years.

Science:

Blessings or Misfortunes - Gifts or Poisonous Cups of Tea

Science absolutely cannot bring a life of true peace and salvation to humanity both spiritually and materially. Not everyone accepts this type of argument. Why? Because people are attached to delusion and cannot be enlightened. If you want to propose this type of argument, of course it will fail, because many people will not agree with this way of speaking. Compared to other things, science and technology have a stronger allure. Many people know clearly that science has problems, but they still support and praise science. In this world, whatever is beneficial must be harmful. Anything that has great benefits means it also has equal harm.

See, cancer is spreading all over the world. That's because science invents new things every day, producing many types of toxins that pollute the atmosphere. As a result, humanity inhales these toxic gases and becomes infected with cancer. Are scientists not aware of that situation? It's not because they don't know, it's just because they don't want to think carefully, and don't want to accept that kind of reasoning. And today, the world has fallen into a state of being infected to the bone, with no cure. Although there is no cure, we should do as much as we know, and use all our strength to save the storm that has come. It's not that we want to oppose scientists, but we should also know to clearly understand this truth. As with all things, wherever there is benefit, there will be harm. For example, if someone has reached the moon, then what will they do when they get there? Suppose the government decides to hide an atomic bomb on the moon, in preparation for global destruction of humanity. Or one day, these bombs will explode, destroying the moon, etc.

If the world doesn't even have a moon, then what kind of world will it be? This is just an example, but we should understand its meaning.

In short, the more science advances, the more humanity's lives are in danger. Progress is like progress. In the past, science had not yet developed but humanity lived happily and freely. Like when the sun rises, you go to work, when the sun sets, you go home and rest, keeping yourself in peace. Today, while science is thriving, humanity is infected with countless strange and incurable diseases. Thus, invisible science has created accidents. We should know that: in life there is good and there is bad, there is good and there is harm, there is success and there is failure, and all things are relative, nothing is absolute.

Lecture on October 6, 1980

Money

Today I will give a special Dharma lecture. What Dharma? It is the Dharma of MONEY. Why is money an unclean object? Please try and see! Money is the dirtiest thing in the world. Because when people count money, most people often salivate to count. Saliva contains countless germs and bacteria. I don't know how many times the money has been through people's saliva, nor do I know how many disease-causing germs are in it. It can be seen that the more times money is counted, the dirtier it becomes. But on the contrary, there are still people who love money more than their lives. That's knowing it's dirty and trying to commit it. There are some people who, because of their greed for money, even sacrifice their own lives without regret. That's enough to prove the magic power of money.

When the Chinese created words, they were very careful and spent a lot of effort to achieve it. Normally, there are six types of words: Figurative, Just Su, Hieroglyphic, Hieroglyphic, Chuan Mantra and Pseudo-ta (impersonation to borrow language). Each word cannot leave the scope of these six categories. Like the word money ( ) belongs to Hoi Yù. Money consists of the letter needle ( ) and two marks ( ).

There is a verse about money as follows:

Second, the painting is filled with high murderous aura,

Humanity and humanity suffer hardship;

Ability to utilize the transcendent three realms,

Unsuitable for use and harshness.

The general idea of ​​the verse says: People use metal to cast money. The two labels are two people fighting for money, both sides compete for the winner, causing murderous aura to soar into the clouds. Many people create so many troubles because of money. People who know how to use money can use it to do many meritorious things, benefit others, benefit themselves, and can escape the Three Realms and avoid having to endure birth and death. People who do not know how to use money will use it to create many evil karma, so they will fall into the three evil paths and will never be liberated. We should know that money is harmful to people and should not be greedy for it.

Why do we become monks and practice Buddhism? Because we want to see wealth and form as non-existent, we are not attached to wealth, nor are we attached to form. Next, for each of my own gestures and actions, I reflect back the light at every moment, keeping my mind from letting it run out. Through long days and months, when our mind is as pure as a mirror, we will clearly understand good and evil. Only then can we escape the three worlds and birth and death. That is the basic ambition of a monk. If we can't let go of wealth, if we can't let go of beauty, then we've failed our desire to become a monk.

People in the world sacrifice their lives to make money, and think of every way to save money for their children. But they do not know that leaving money to their children and grandchildren means bringing disaster to them. On the contrary, if they don't leave any money behind, there won't be any trouble. It's called: "Children are better than their father, what's the point of saving them? If they have children who aren't as good as their father, what's the point of saving them?" Sons and daughters have more ability than their fathers. If you leave money to them, they will have no place to use it. On the contrary, if sons and daughters do not have the ability like their fathers, if you leave money to them, it means teaching them not to work to make a living, but to only like to roam around, get drunk on gambling, be promiscuous and drink alcohol, and hang out at the Tan floor and So shop all day. Isn't that harming your children and grandchildren? Therefore, I advise people who have money to do many meritorious deeds and save humanity, then they will gain immeasurable merit.

We are monastics, not only should we not be greedy for material wealth, but we should not even think about it with false thoughts. When we walk, stand, lie down, or sit, we should control our delusions. How to control? There is only one method: reciting Buddha's name or reciting Mantras. If you say one less word, you can recite one more Buddha's word. Reciting until there is a feeling of enlightenment can lead to enlightenment and wisdom. Therefore, it is said: "Defeat the thoughts of the first death, the Dharma body will be activated" which means: Kill the false thoughts so that the Dharma body can come alive. Therefore, cultivators should control themselves at all times. So it is said: "Remember impermanence, be careful and don't let go." We should use these two verses to be alert, we will naturally awaken again. I hope everyone will strictly maintain the precepts, that's what I always hope for!

These are two very reasonable sayings: "Lung cocks are real, thang oa is close. Wild cranes are unkind to the world." Meaning: Even though the chicken in the cage has food and water to drink, when it grows fat, it is killed and put into a pot of boiling water to make human food. Therefore, it is said: "Thang oa nhan" means the pot of boiling water next to it. Although the wild crane does not have grain to eat, the sky is high and the earth is wide, it can roam freely in the universe, not being restrained, not attached to anything, how free and free it is! We, as monastics, should take heaven and earth as our tent and the four seas as our home, and should not have a private residence. If we have a temple, there will be times when we get attached and then go searching for something, which is contrary to the Buddha Dharma. So even small mistakes can lead to huge consequences. That is also the meaning of the sentence: One error goes a thousand miles.

A Zen master once said: "Last year I was poor, I still had land to stick to; this year I'm poor, I don't even have an awl!" How free and liberating his thoughts are! It's inconceivably magical. We should follow the example of this Zen master, who did not seek anything other than an alms bowl and three robes. Money is something outside the body, it is not brought to birth, it is not taken away at death. Therefore, if we have money, we should do many meritorious deeds, such as printing a small book to propagate the Buddha Dharma, the merit is immeasurable, compared to building a pagoda and tower for ourselves.

A wise person does not have attachments and does not engage in polluted behavior. What is pollution? That is, greed for wealth and love of beauty. If you don't give up money, you won't be able to eliminate pollution; If form is not considered empty, it cannot be completely cleansed of defilements. If you don't want to be polluted, there is only one way to destroy the two gates of "talent and beauty". Instantly, all over the dharma world, everywhere is our residence. We as cultivators should remember that the key lies in the two gates of "talent and physical appearance." If we can break them, we will not be attached to anything. People have an ironic saying: "Monks don't like money - but the more the better!"

We monastics should reflect and review to see if we have such thoughts? If so, you should change it, if not, try to avoid it. We hope that everyone will be vigilant and self-reliant, and should learn from Zen Master Bach Truong's advice: "A day without work is a day without food." If everyone can do that, people will no longer sarcastically say: Those who become monks are rice beetles.

The monastics at Kim Son Pagoda know that money is an impure object, so some people follow the precepts and do not keep money. That means their hands do not touch money, they have absolutely no interaction with money. Let me tell you a true story. I have a disciple who is the only child of a millionaire. Not only did this uncle not want his father's property, but when his father introduced him to a girlfriend, he also refused. Then he decided to go to Kim Son pagoda to become a monk. That's why I gave him the Dharma name Hang Khong.

One day, my father called and asked: "Do you need money? I can send it to you." But he refused to accept money from his father. That action is truly worthy of the reputation, the greatest stupidity. He kept the precept not to touch money or fame, and it was indeed appropriate, because he was not penniless. People who are not greedy for wealth and form will not be polluted. If anyone behaves like that, they will definitely achieve success.

Lecture on October 10, 1980

tieu_de: At Nha - Buddha Nature /
tom_tat: Prajna is Buddha Nature, Buddha Nature is Prajna. To speak of Great Prajna means to speak of Great Buddha Nature. To say Great Buddha Nature is to say Great Prajna. Although the names are not the same, the meaning is the same. Why say that? Because Prajna is wisdom…
noi_dung:
At Nha - Buddha Nature /

Prajna is Buddha Nature, Buddha Nature is Prajna. To speak of Great Prajna means to speak of Great Buddha Nature. To say Great Buddha Nature is to say Great Prajna. Although the names are not the same, the meaning is the same. Why say that? Because Prajna is wisdom, and wisdom is great enlightenment. If you can achieve great enlightenment, then you have wisdom. If you do not attain great enlightenment, then you do not have wisdom. Great enlightenment is great Buddha nature. Buddha is Sanskrit, translated as enlightenment, self-realization, enlightenment of others and perfect enlightenment. Therefore, it is said that Buddha Nature is Prajna. There are three types of Prajna: Prajna of Literature, Prajna of Contemplation, and Real Form of Prajna. I now briefly explain as follows:

The Prajnaparamita Text: This is not the type of Prajnaparamita text taught in worldly schools, but the Prajnaparamita Text in the world, which makes you develop the mind of Bodhi, practice the Bodhi path, attain Bodhi and is also the Prajnaparamita Text in the scriptures.

Prajna Contemplation: From Prajnaparamita Contemplation will arise Prajna Contemplation. For example, when you read the sutras, when faced with the four words "Nha Thi Van" (I heard like this), you wonder: What is "Nha Thi"? What is "Fall Literature"? So you have a mind to contemplate and consider clearly. After reading "Thu Thi Van Van," you should take the text to find the meaning, find the meaning in it. That is called Prajna Contemplation.

The True Form of Prajna: That is, when there is Contemplation

Prajna, you will know that this "Thus" is the essence of the Dharma and "Nha Van" means "I hear the essence of the Dharma." This is because of your contemplation that you can achieve the True Form and realize that the Dharma is as it is, and the Dharma is the original emptiness. Emptiness is the True Form of Prajna.

Those who understand these three types of Prajna will also know the Three Human Buddha Natures. The Three Causes of Buddha Nature are the Cause and Effect of Buddha Nature, the Cause and Effect of Buddha Nature, and the Right Cause of Buddha Nature.

Prajnaparamita is the cause and effect of Buddha Nature. Using writing as a supporting condition, helps you know these three types of Buddha Nature and also know that Buddha Nature is Prajna, and Prajna is Buddha Nature. Because of that, you will develop your merit and good roots to attain the True Form.

Contemplating Prajna is the Willow of Humanity and Buddha Nature. For example, a light illuminates the room so you can see what is in the room. For example, in the room there is the Avatamsaka Sutra, a Buddha statue, a Buddha altar, and the names of eighty-eight Buddhas, you can see and know them all. That is because the light shines, making all things clearly visible. Therefore, we should use such lamps to illuminate our own inner room. When you have the power of contemplation, you begin to generate the functions of the Buddha Nature. If you do not have the power of Prajna Contemplation, you will not clearly know the Buddha Nature. You also don't know your inner room: There are Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who are teaching and transforming living beings; There is a Pratyekabuddha who is practicing according to the Dharma of the Twelve Causes and Conditions; There is Thanh Van who is practicing the Four Noble Truths; There are countless gods who are receiving wonderful and wonderful bliss; There are countless sentient beings who are going crazy; There are countless Asuras who are struggling; There are countless animals in the cycle of birth and death, being born and then dying, dying and then being born again; There are countless hungry ghosts stealing food; There are countless sentient beings in hell who are suffering torture in mountains of knives and oil pans. All of these realms are inseparable from your mind, they are all interconnected with your mind. Hell has eighteen major hells and five hundred small hells. Which hell you want to go to is up to you. If you have the power of Prajna Insight, you will clearly understand the causes and conditions of the Ten Dharma Realms. Once we have a clear understanding, of course we should choose good deeds to do, and give up bad deeds. Only then will we not fall into hell.

The True Form of Prajna is the Right Humanity and Buddha Nature, also the Buddha Nature of the first meaning of emptiness. Due to contemplation, we achieve the True Character and realize the True Character.

How can we be born into the Buddha realm? Buddha is enlightenment, that is, enlightenment. Those who can be enlightened are Buddhas, those who cannot be enlightened are sentient beings. Therefore it is said: "A thought of enlightenment is a thought of Buddha, a thought of enlightenment is a thought of Buddha. A thought of confusion is a thought of sentient beings, a thought of delusion is a thought of sentient beings. The time of enlightenment is the time of Buddha, the time of delusion is the time of sentient beings." If you know that your actions are crazy, then that is Buddha. If you don't know that your actions are crazy, then that's a sentient being. Therefore, it is said that the limit between Buddha and sentient beings is between enlightenment and delusion. Whether you want to be a Buddha or a sentient being depends on your choice.

How to be born into the Bodhisattva realm? Simply put, anyone who often thinks about the benefit of sentient beings is a Bodhisattva, and someone who often thinks about their own benefit is a devil. Bodhisattva only knows others but does not know himself. While the devil only knows himself and does not know others. These two components are very contradictory. Bodhisattvas know there are sentient beings to save, but have not yet reached the stage where there are no sentient beings to save. When you reach the Buddha realm, there are no more sentient beings to save. Why? Because all sentient beings have been saved, and there are no more sentient beings left to save. That means there is but also no form of sentient beings, because Buddha does not care about form. That is called scanning all dharmas, leaving all appearances. Sweep all dharmas, like using a broom to sweep away all worldly dharmas. Leaving all appearances means there are no more appearances. If you practice according to the Dharma of the Six Paramitas, you will be born in the Bodhisattva realm.

How to be born in the Pratyekabuddha realm? It is you who contemplate the Twelve Causes and Conditions: Ignorance is conditioned by action, action is conditioned by consciousness; until birth, old age, and death. Ignorance ranks first among the twelve dharmas of Dependent Origination. Where does ignorance come from? It comes from the three poisons of greed, anger, and ignorance. Where there is ignorance, there is action. Where there are actions, there is consciousness, etc. If we can find the root of ignorance and cut off all ignorance, then birth and death will no longer exist. How to cut it off? That is, we need to practice the three trainings: Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom. Only then can we cut off the roots of the three poisons and turn ignorance into wisdom. When we have wisdom, we will understand what is good and what is evil. Thus our mind will be clear, bright and pure. Once ignorance has been destroyed, the Dharmakaya will appear, that is, Pratyekabuddha.

How to be born into the Thanh Van realm? You should practice the Four Noble Truths, that is, find the cause of suffering. The root of suffering is from within the mistaken view and thinking, that is, views and thoughts. Therefore, we must use the Thirty-Seven Path Supports to destroy those two "or"s. View or has eighty-eight parts, fourth or has eighty-one parts. Only when we have destroyed those two good things of the three worlds can we attain the four fruits of Arhatship, which means no birth and no death. Above are the four dharma realms belonging to the Holy realm.

How to be born in heaven? You should practice the Five Precepts and Ten Virtues, which is to practice purifying the three karmas of body, speech, and mind. The ten good deeds are: Do three good things with your body: do not kill, do not steal, and do not commit adultery. The mouth has four good things: no false speech, no false language, no evil speech, and no double-tongue. The mind has three good things: no greed, no anger, and no ignorance. Whoever has these merits will be born in heaven. But they can only be born in the Dia Cu Thien heaven, that is, the Four Heavenly Kings Heaven and the Dao Loi Heaven, but cannot be born in Khong Cu Thien, which are realms such as the Da Ma Heaven, the Tu Suat Heaven, the Hoa Lac Heaven, the Tha Hoa Heaven, and the Tha Hoa Free Heaven. Unless people diligently practice meditation, they can gradually advance higher. From the eighteen Heavens of the Form Realm, one rises to the Heaven of Non-Perception and Non-Perception of the Formless Realm, which is the supreme heaven of the twenty-eight heavens in the Three Realms. If they continue diligently practicing meditation, they will go beyond the Three Realms, escape the part of birth and death and attain Arhatship.

How to be born into the human world? If you

Maybe the evil acts, but the good ones obey, that is, don't do evil deeds, so do good deeds and you will not lose your human body. Those who practice in their previous lives with both blessings and wisdom will be born into a wealthy family, everything will go smoothly, they will be healthier, they will live longer and have a good and dignified appearance. And if those who do not practice blessings and wisdom in their previous lives, will be born into poverty, have a lifetime of trouble, have many illnesses, die prematurely, and have an ugly appearance. It's all due to the law of cause and effect, which is an immutable, unchanging law. Doing good will be rewarded with blessings, doing evil will be rewarded with evil. There are people who did not practice in their previous lives, so in this life they have to suffer. If they do not practice, their next life will not be like this life. If they vow to practice, their next life will definitely be better than this life. Some people, because of their previous life's practice, have everything favorable in this life. As a result of this life, they continue to practice, and their next life will definitely be better and more favorable than this life. If they do not practice, their next life will definitely not be equal to this life. This principle is very simple, anyone can understand it. Whether your next life will be favorable or unfavorable, it's entirely up to you to decide. Even if Buddhas and Bodhisattvas want to help, they cannot do this.

How to avoid being born in the four evil realms? If you no longer have the mind to fight, you will be able to cut off entering and leaving the Asura realm. If you are not greedy, you will cut off interactions with the animal realm. If you don't have anger, you will stop going back and forth with the realm of hungry ghosts. If you are not ignorant, you will never enter or leave the hell realm. Above are the six dharma realms of the mortal world.

The ten dharma realms are ten paths that you choose for yourself. Whatever you sow, you will reap, it's just a matter of seeing whether you have Prajna wisdom or not!

A person with Prajna wisdom is someone who knows how to create good deeds and eliminate bad karma. People who do not have prajna wisdom will sow many evil deeds and destroy the seeds of good karma. Everyone has Prajna wisdom, it's just a matter of whether you know how to use it or not. If you know how to use this Prajna, it will illuminate the entire Dharma world. If you do not know how to apply Prajna wisdom, you will not be able to realize that the ten dharma realms have always existed in our minds.

Lecture on October 17, 1980

Dieu Dao

Living beings have many good or many evil natures, Buddha knows them all. The desires of sentient beings, whether many or few, Buddha still understands clearly. Therefore, Buddha taught many wonderful paths for sentient beings.

What is the miraculous path? To put it in a superficial way: Dao is everyday actions, the Dao that we use, practice, and experience every day is very wonderful. If we don't pay attention to studying it, we won't know its magic. If you pay attention to studying it, then everything will be wonderful, unspeakably wonderful. For example, where do the things we use every day come from? It comes from a very magical place. Then where do they go? Getting there is truly magical. In short, everything is a wonderful path.

The realm in which we live every day is also the wonderful path. Just like when we don't eat, we get hungry. Why be hungry? That's magic. After we finish eating, we are full. That is also magic. Even wearing clothes or drinking tea, everything is equally wonderful. If they aren't magical, why do we have to use them? Even though we use them, they cannot be used for a long time, but only temporarily. So what you say is miraculous?

Someone said: "Ah! Who doesn't know this principle!"

But your understanding is only on the surface, not the end. You don't know the magic yet.

Why do people like delicious food? That's the miracle. Why

People want to wear beautiful clothes? That is also a miracle. Why do people like to live in a nice house? That is also a miracle.

We are not very clear about the meaning of this wonderful thing. In other words, if we understand clearly, it is wonderful; if we do not understand clearly, it is not wonderful. Just like the two practitioners of "Three Steps One Bow" while walking three steps on the road, bow once; There was a woman whose pants were torn and could not cover her body. At that time, a pair of pants appeared on the side of the road!

That's the miracle. Then someone threw a beer bottle at them, but it didn't hit, which was also a miracle. There are many things to say about the meaning of this miracle.

Lecture on November 5, 1980

tieu_de: Han Bon Hoan Nguyen /
tom_tat: This body is not formed by the accumulation of the five aggregates. It's not from the twelve realms or the eighteen realms either. Buddha did not have a form, but why do sentient beings see thirty-two appearances and eighty appearances...
noi_dung:
Han Bon Hoan Nguyen /

This body is not formed by the accumulation of the five aggregates. It's not from the twelve realms or the eighteen realms either. Buddha did not have a form, but how could sentient beings see His thirty-two appearances and eighty beauties? That's because the Buddha appeared according to the discriminating minds of sentient beings. Because sentient beings have the mind to distinguish between good and bad, and because Buddha wants sentient beings to develop Bodhi mind, He manifested many different bodies so that sentient beings would increase their joy and faith. That is a method of very skillful expedient means.

Men want to find a beautiful girl to be their wife, and women want to find a handsome guy to be their husband. That proves that everyone likes to be beautiful, not ugly. Human minds are all like that and human psychology is the same. Everyone hopes to have a beautiful wife, or a handsome, handsome husband. That's a normal human thing, it's obvious.

Someone asked: "You are preaching the sutra, but why are you talking about this?"

You told me not to talk about this, so what should I talk about? The ancients said: "The path of a gentleman begins with his husband and wife." There are only two people in this world, man and woman. Only men and women can create the world. Here I have a special clarification: this man and woman are not Adam and Eve, nor are they created by God using mud to come to this world. In short, this world was created by the organization of husband and wife.

There is a husband and wife, then there are father and children, brothers, me, and others. Men and women are inherently yin and yang. Therefore it is said: "One yin and one yang is called the path, leaving the yin and yang path cannot be achieved." It is said again: "The solitary yin does not arise, the solitary yang does not grow." That is natural morality.

When we cultivate the Way, we need to return to our original nature and return to our origin. A man who cultivates the Way should be like the word Ly ( ) in the eight trigrams, with a broken line in the middle, reflecting the word

Can ( ) has three solid lines. A female cultivator should be like the word Kham ( ) with a line connecting it in the middle, returning to the word Khon ( ) with three lines all broken in half.

into six sections. Qian represents men, Kun represents women. Men should return to the same feet, women should respond to the same feet. Men should be like the Good Talented Child in the Avatamsaka Sutra. Women should be like the Dragon Lady in the Lotus Sutra. They are both male and female and have returned to their origin. We should practice the Dharma in the same way, maintaining the same purity, so that we can easily attain the pure Dharmakaya.

Because living beings have discriminatory minds and often discriminate about many issues such as: good and evil, beautiful and ugly, right and wrong, black and white, Buddha, depending on the minds of living beings, manifests many different incarnations, so that living beings can see the Buddha's body, called:

"The sky is full of water, the sky is the moon, there are thousands of miles and thousands of miles of clouds."

Mean:

A thousand rivers have water, a thousand rivers have moonlight, a thousand miles without clouds is a thousand miles of sky.

Buddha incarnates depending on the species. If sentient beings' minds are like clear water, Buddha will appear within them. Why can't we see Buddha's body? Because we have too much desire and ignorance, wisdom cannot manifest itself. Because our mind is like a pond of muddy water, even if there is a Buddha, the Buddha cannot appear.

Ignorance is darkness, wisdom is light. To have ignorance is to have affliction, to have affliction is to be stupid, to have ignorance is to have darkness, to have darkness is to have no light, to have no light is to have no wisdom, to have no wisdom is to not be able to see the Buddha. These are all interconnected. If we want to see the Buddha's body, we must diligently cultivate precepts, concentration, wisdom, and destroy greed, anger, and ignorance. Thus, Buddha will naturally appear and preach to us.

Lecture on November 8, 1980

True Sutra of No Self

In the first chapter of the Buddha's Recitation of the Tripitaka, it is said: "Buddha told Sariputta: People who do not understand all dharmas are covered by words. Therefore, the Tathagata knows that language is evil. Even if he has a little language, this person cannot achieve the truth." The Buddha told Venerable Sariputta: "Whoever cannot clearly understand all dharmas are covered up by language." Why? Because they don't have "no" about accepting the dharma. Because of this reason, the Buddha knew that all language was incorrect and erroneous. Whenever there is language, there is a place to cover up, and where there is a coverup, there is an obstacle to the inherent wisdom of sentient beings. Even a single sentence or word is not true. Why? Because every time we say even one word, we still have attachments. Therefore, to say "The One Dharma is not independent" means that even one word does not exist.

People who know how to read scriptures not only know how to read scriptures with words but also know how to read scriptures without words. If one knows how to read sutras without chanting, then that is the only person who truly understands the Buddha Dharma. You can read a sutra with words and keep reciting it over and over again, then that's just a problem-free person looking for something to do. If you know how to read the sutra without words, then you already have the method. But if you have to read the "wordless sutra", can you read it? If you don't know how to read the true sutras impartially, you should first read the sutras with words, and then you can clearly understand the sutras without words. Wait until you have clearly understood the sutras without words, you will not need to read the sutras with words. So it is said: "It is not difficult to know, but it is difficult to not know." Studying Buddhism is the same!

After all, what is a wordless sutra? That is, "a single thought does not arise." If you can not give birth to a single thought, you will naturally return to emptiness. All Buddha Dharma is like that and nothing else! If you cannot "not be born at one thought", then you still have to do a lot of merit, cultivate many good Bodhi roots and practice many Bodhi paths. Wait until you reach the fullness of the Six Paradigms and all your actions are complete. At that time, you will naturally "not be born at one thought and not pass away."

Why is it said that Buddha did not preach the Dharma? The sutras say so, the commentary also says so. So in the end, did Buddha preach the Dharma or not? If it is said that Buddha did not preach the Dharma, then where does the Avatamsaka Sutra that we are preaching come from? If it is said that Buddha preached Dharma, then why did Buddha not admit that he had preached Dharma? If we say Buddha preached the Dharma, that is slandering Buddha. But if you depart even one word from the scriptures, it means the devil is speaking. So how can we teach the Dharma?

Why did Buddha not admit that he had spoken the Dharma? Because every word is a hindrance to the true meaning. No one can tell the true Dharma. The Dharmas that the Buddha spoke are all expedient Dharmas. Although it is a temporary declaration of power to reveal the truth, if this truth can be displayed, it is not real!

Lecture on November 22, 1980

tieu_de: The Gate of Patience /
tom_tat: You should know that this Master is very harsh, not sweet at all. There were times when I was so harsh that my disciples had tears and snot in their eyes. Now I would like to tell you how I learned...
noi_dung:
The Gate of Patience /

You should know that this Master is very harsh, not sweet at all. There were times when I was so harsh that my disciples had tears and snot in their eyes. Now I would like to tell you how I learned to be so harsh.

When I was sixteen years old, I began preaching the Diamond Sutra. In the sutra, there is a story about a patient immortal who, even though all four limbs were cut off by King Ca Loi, still did not give rise to anger. After reading that story, I vowed to follow it and wholeheartedly practice the method of patience.

I know that my innate nature is harsh and stubborn. Therefore, it is most appropriate for me to practice the method of patience. But once I made up my mind, many trials and challenges came rushing in from all four directions. Someone who has never scolded me is scolding me now; The person who had never beaten me, now also beat me. Friends who had previously treated me very well, ended up attacking me. So I thought to myself: "I preach the Diamond Sutra to people. In the sutra, it talks about a patient immortal who had his hands and feet cut off without feeling angry. Right now, these people only curse me and attack me, but they haven't come to cut off my limbs. If I can't be patient, how can I still preach the Diamond Sutra?"

So I made up my mind to be patient. No matter who is not good to me, even if they want to harm me, I endure it all. As a result, I am not swayed by the outside world. Actually, these people did not want to harm me, but on the contrary, they educated me to see if I could withstand those tests. If anyone scolds me, I bow to that person. If someone hits me, I immediately go to sleep and let them see. When I was at home, I was often attacked by things like that. But after becoming a monk, wise men also came back and forth endlessly. Oh well, all the monks from before and after have surrounded me left and right, no one looked at me. They all see me as a thorn in their side and want to bully me. There was a teacher who, when he saw me lighting incense, scolded me loudly: "Why did you become a monk? You don't even know how to light a stick of incense. What a fool! How dare you even talk about becoming a monk again!"

At that time I thought: "Ah! The test has come again. The patient immortal had his arms and legs cut off by King Ca Loi without anger. And now I have not suffered like that. Okay! Just bow your head and pay respect to him!" So I went in front of that teacher and bowed my head to thank him for helping me. At that time, regardless of whether they were "good wise men" ordained or lay people, they constantly came to help me like that, but in my heart there was still not the slightest bit of anger towards them. Every time that happens, I reflect back: "I must have never helped them in the past, but today they help me, so I should thank them, right?"

Do you understand now? Your Master is that kind of teacher. He is a teacher who specializes in cultivating patience, and specializes in being bullied by people. I specialize in tolerating what others cannot tolerate, and yielding to what others cannot yield. What is the benefit of such a person? But you were so unfortunate, because you met someone who was of no use. So why do you still want to study under this stupid Master? But when you have followed me, I cannot help but tell the story of my past experience, that I came from that path of practicing patience.

When you study Buddhism, you should not listen to a lot of Buddha Dharma and then not practice it, but you should practice it in a practical way. You should think for yourself and try to apply according to the Buddha's teachings.

Jesus proposed the doctrine of "Love for enemies" which means loving one's enemies. For someone who is not good to us, we have to love that person even more.

Buddhism advocates "Equality of resentment," meaning that whether we are friends or enemies, we consider them the same. Our benevolence towards everyone should be equal, regardless of status or esteem. If a person who studies Buddhism cannot truly practice, then learning will always be just superficial learning, and will never be able to achieve true benefits!

Remember! Remember! The first step in learning Buddhism is definitely to practice patience! Even if someone wants to kill you, you shouldn't have anger. Even compared to the practice of the patient immortal, we have to go one step further. But that doesn't mean to say: "The patient cultivator had his hands and feet cut off without anger, so now you can cut off my body, I won't be angry either!"

That's imitating others, not coming from your own ideas, so you're ranked second. Not only should my arms and legs be cut off, I should not be angry, even if my body is chopped into pieces, my bones and flesh should be crushed, I should not be angry! Therefore, when someone slanders me or treats me poorly, I don't get angry.

Lecture on December 1, 1990

tieu_de: in You Give Me Alms /
tom_tat: Today I want to give an order to those who have taken refuge with me. What order is that? Please give alms! I would like to be with you. Someone said: "Master! Over the past few years, You have never made a request to us....
noi_dung:
in You Give Me Alms /

Today I want to give an order to those who have taken refuge with me. What order is that? Please give alms! I would like to be with you. Someone said: "Master! In the past few years, You have never changed fate to ask us. But today Master wants to change fate and ask us, so it must be Master who wants to change great fate, right!"

Not wrong! I don't ask for small grace. What does it mean to ask for a small favor? Even if it's three million or five million, it won't be of much use. In this world, money is just colorful pieces of paper. Even if you bring me gold and silver, I can't eat it and I can't take it with me when I die. Those things are of no use.

So what do I ask you for? That's asking for all of your anger, ignorance, affliction, and anger. All of those things, please give them all to me! Because I'm a "hot pepper" teacher, I don't criticize all that much, the more the better. If you give all of those things to me, I will put them in the furnace of ignorance to practice. I will use the fire of ignorance to slowly refine them into pure gold, into diamonds, and in the future we will become Buddhas together. So even if you don't want to give up, you have to give up. If you don't want to give alms, you have to give alms.

Whoever is truly my disciple must surrender all his anger, ignorance, affliction, jealousy, and obstacles to others to me. I'm a trash collector, so please put all those things in the trash, okay?

After that, we take another step to purify and make this world clean. Dissolve all the evil spirits of this world, so that disasters will become invisible and transform suffering into good fortune. That's what I want to tell you today, not just joking around. When you first hear it, it sounds like a joke, but what I say is completely true, not a joke.

Make it clear that I want to make love to you. If anyone does not have the heart to let go, then that person is not my disciple. Whoever is willing to give will be truly my disciple. If you don't let go, you have to let go. If you don't give in, you have to give in. If you don't give in, you have to be patient. Do you understand?

This Dharma is definitely like that, so don't be negligent and just rush through the matter. No one should harbor jealousy or hinder others. On the contrary, we should only do our best to help others practice. These are the things I want to tell you today. I've said too much, you're probably so "spicy" that you can't breathe, so today that much spicy is enough!

Lecture on December 25, 1980

Do You Want To Know What A Devil Is?

There are many types of demons. Some people think that demons have a cruel, scary appearance with a green face and sharp teeth. Actually, that's not necessarily the case. Sometimes ghosts turn into human bodies. At first sight, they seem like real people, but they are actually ghosts. If you are someone who has opened the Five Eyes, the demons cannot deceive you. Demons can transform into animals such as horses, buffaloes, goats, dogs, rabbits and fish... Why can they transform like that? Because they have magical powers, or they transform into ants, mosquitoes, insects, flies, sparrows, bees... For example, in spring, hundreds of flowers bloom, so there are hundreds of bees coming to suck honey, but among them there are many reincarnations of demons. There are real bees in the flowers, but there are also fake bees. Real bees receive retribution due to karma, while fake bees are transformed into demons. They go to different places to suck flower pistils and drink flower dew. Therefore, don't think that you definitely cannot see ghosts. You face it every day, yet you still don't recognize it. That's why there is a saying: "Facing without knowing is Avalokiteshvara." But this can also be said in the same way as: "If you face it and don't know it, it's a ghost!"

Now someone says: "Teacher! If you say something like that, I really can't believe it!" Oh! If you don't believe it, that's fine. But why say you can't believe it? I'm not forcing you to believe, I'm just telling you the truth so you can be alert, so you don't interact with demons day after day without knowing it. Someone said: "Hey! Teacher, if you say that, it will only make us scared, and at night we won't dare to sleep." Then you definitely shouldn't sleep anymore, but just focus on cultivating the Eightfold Samadhi and you'll be fine. (It means practicing the Buddha's name method continuously for 90 days, the practitioner will not sit nor lie down.)

If I tell the truth, you definitely won't believe me, so I rarely talk truthfully. So am I talking fake? No, false words should not be said. We rarely say true words, but we should not say even a little false word. If we say a lot of truth, people won't believe it.

Furthermore, demons can also transform into many different types of animals. Do you remember 1976, when we first moved to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas? At that time, a layman bought some turtles to release them. One of them was turned upside down, its four legs raised in the air. Layperson Phung Phung was also present there. He saw a person dressed in blue looking towards him asking for help. Mr. Phung Phung went to the place to observe and discovered that it was a turtle that was upside down. Have you seen it? That turtle also had a spiritual nature, so it knew how to turn to Mr. Phung Phung to ask for help. Yet for many years no one has paid attention to this matter. But from that, we know that all living beings, each species, have relatives. That is, things of the same species gather together, and their qi and energy flow together according to their type to manifest.

Now that everyone is paying attention to studying the Shurangama mantra, they know that ghosts also come in all shapes and sizes, with thousands of different species. They all receive retributions due to feelings and results, depending on the species. In the Shurangama Mantra, there are many kings of ghosts named, including the yaksha (fast) ghost, the rakshasa (fearful) ghost, the ghost of the soul, the ghost of the corpse, the ghost of the abode (sips essence), the ghost of the tea table (paralyzes people, also known as sleep paralysis, ghost of pressure), the great body ghost, the crazy ghost, the foul ghost (rotten), the devil of Danna (with a toxic smell), the heat ghost, the cold ghost, the shadow ghost, the music ghost... There are also ghost eaters. flowers, ghosts that eat placenta, ghosts that eat fetuses, ghosts that eat babies, ghosts that eat fat, ghosts that eat lamps, ghosts that eat grains... Their transformations are truly endless, immeasurable and boundless.

Before, when we had not heard the Shurangama mantra, we did not know that there were so many types of ghosts. But after we heard it, we realized that there are many types of demons. Of course, demons are much more numerous than humans. People who create bad karma will fall into the demon realm and cannot escape on their own.

When Buddha was still alive, he once grabbed a handful of land and asked his disciples: "Do you say there is a lot of land in my hands or a lot of land on this great earth?" The disciple replied: "Of course there is a lot of land on the great earth, but the land in the hands of the World-Honored One is very little." The World-Honored One said: "Sentient beings gain a human body like the soil in my hands, while sentient beings lose their human body like the soil on the great earth." Losing one's body is like soil on the earth, so after losing one's body, where do they go and what do they do? Of course I'm going to be a ghost! So do you still have to ask? Therefore, demons are more numerous than humans. Even if you use a computer, statistics cannot be calculated, unless you use "brain god". The brain is also called "celestial brain".

Someone said: "When did you invent that heavenly brain?" It's not that I invented it. If you don't believe it, just go to heaven and see. The heavenly brain is the natural self that always exists. This type of brain does not need a manager, nor does it require hands to press down on the keyboard.

When you want to know something, you just need to start thinking and it will naturally be calculated right away, and the line will not be wrong. Whatever your mind thinks, it immediately knows. Because it is so magical and spiritual, I call it "Spirit". But I'm afraid the number of demons is impossible to calculate with my brain, because there are too many of them. Moreover, just after calculating it, it skyrocketed to thousands, hundreds of billions. A moment later, they increased by thousands of billions more. Therefore, there is no way to calculate it accurately. Because ghosts suddenly ascend to heaven, then suddenly descend to earth, there is no way to determine.

Demons also have relatives and friends. If he knows where to eat, he will invite his friends to eat with him. For example, flower-eating ghosts can turn into honeybees or butterflies. Wherever they go, they eat flower pistils and drink flower dew. Hungry ghosts are caused by the feeling of retribution, so they are often burned by fire without stopping. Its body also has fire, outside and inside it also has fire. The fire inside and outside collided fiercely, burning, the pain was indescribable. Why such retribution? Because when you become a human, you have too much anger, so after death, turning into a ghost is not comfortable, you are burned day and night, you will never be able to fulfill your time limit, and even if you want to escape, you can't escape. But if they eat a little nectar or flower dew, they can relieve some of the heat. Even if they wish to be cool for just a moment, it won't work. Therefore, good and evil, cause and effect, are like shadows following shapes, never going wrong. Ladies and gentlemen, be careful!

There is also a type of devil that specializes in eating fruit. But first I would like to briefly explain the four types of (real) food. All living beings depend on food to live. Talking about food, there are four types:

The portion of food cutting: All sentient beings, all beings with blood and form, are part of food cutting. "Part" means you have your part, I have mine. “Segment” means each piece, each paragraph, or each meal, each meal. Like eating breakfast, lunch, dinner, and not eating between meals, so it's called paragraph. Humans and animals both belong to the portion of food cessation.

Touching food: When you touch it, it's like eating. Demons are of the eating type.

Food: Just thinking about it makes me feel full. Heavenly people belong to private food.

Food: Even thoughts do not need to arise, because the ability to eat and drink is in the eighth consciousness. The gods in the Four Heavens belong to consciousness.

All animals have their own kind. For example, birds, of the same species, live together peacefully. If you are not of the same species and want to go to another species' house to be a guest, you cannot, because they will definitely fight. Surely you also remember that in the forest of Ten Thousand Saints in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, there was a time when a flock of white cranes fought with an eagle. Last year, a white crane was seriously injured, or perhaps it fell from a high nest and was injured. My disciple is Tieu Qua Da, this uncle used to be friends with him. Perhaps in his previous life, Guo Da was also a crane, but because he heard a little Buddhist scripture, in this life he changed into a human. This is also not necessarily the case. Qua Da saw that the bird was in trouble and could not bear to give up, so he brought the bird to the hospital for treatment. But the entire team of doctors had no choice but to help but couldn't. As a result, he had to return it to the tree. Even though a large white crane stood guard and protected it, it was eventually captured by an eagle. Therefore we know that: all living beings will follow their own species, each species has its own relatives.

Returning to the main topic, all sentient beings rely on food to live. For example, we eat fruit. When the fruit is just picked from the tree, it is originally two fruits. For example, an apple is not simply an apple, because on the face of the apple there is another apple. Someone said, "Why don't I see that fruit?" If you could see it, you would secretly eat it! These two apples, one of which is a shadow, can also be called the "Nature" of the apple. Likewise, each individual is not simply a human being, but also has a different spiritual nature. But a person's spiritual nature is hidden inside the body, not revealed. If this spiritual nature escapes, it will be eaten by demons and demons.

No matter what species turns into a human, a shadow remains behind it, which is called a "ghost soul" (humans have three souls and seven souls). For example, if a person was a horse in his previous life, there will be a horse shadow behind him. Some people were born as donkeys, buffalos, goats, chickens, dogs or pigs in their previous lives, and the image of that species still remains behind their backs. The person who has opened the Five Eyes will immediately know at a glance: "Ah! So this person was originally a dog in his previous life!" But not everyone has the Five Eyes. Because I'm afraid people will reveal all the problems about other people's past lives. That's why it is said: "Heaven's secrets cannot be secreted".

Fruit is not an animal, although it does not have blood, it is still a living thing. Whenever there is a life, there is a nature. Like offering fruit to a demon god, the demon god will eat the nature of that fruit. The devil does not hold the fruit to bite and eat it, but he just needs to touch and suck the nature of the fruit, which means he has already eaten it. Therefore, if you eat fruit that has been offered to ghosts and gods, you will not feel much of a taste.

My hometown is in the northeastern mountainous region of Manchuria, where there is a large bear. It doesn't need to bite or tear anything it eats, meaning it swallows it whole. In the mountains there grows a type of pear, called iron pear because it is very hard. But bears don't need to chew, just take a bite of the pear and swallow it immediately. What's even more miraculous is that when it defecates, it also produces a whole pear, the same shape as when it was not swallowed, without any dents. But that pear no longer had any flavor. Because once the pear runs through the chemical factory (digestive system) in the bear's body, the essence is absorbed. So even though the form is still there, its nature is gone. From this point we can understand the situation of Buddhas, Demons, and Gods eating fruit. Fruit that has been offered to Buddha should not be left for long because it spoils very quickly. Just like when people are born, the soul is still inside. Once they die, the soul leaves the body, and the body rots very quickly. If the fruit still has its birth nature, it will not quickly rot, but once it has lost its birth nature, it will perish very quickly.

Of the four types of food, ghosts only need one smell and one touch to finish eating. Unlike us humans, we have to bite and chew a piece, then have to swallow it, which is very troublesome. Someone asked: "How do you know about such a thing? That's because in my previous life I was a ghost, so I still remember it today! Demons belong to the category of food contact, Astral people belong to the category of food, and the Gods in the Four Space Lands belong to the category of consciousness.

The karma of all ghosts and spirits is due to causes and conditions that are felt, each cause has the same result, called: "Initiate or create karma, receive retribution." Therefore, we should know that if we do good, good fortune will follow, and if we do evil, misfortune will follow, just like the echo of a sound. Feeling pain or feeling pleasure is created by yourself, not by anyone else! If you don't want to be a demon, don't create the karma of being a demon.

Today I will only say a small part about my past life as a devil. If you don't get tired of hearing it, in the future I will tell everyone how I was an ant, a mosquito, how I was in hell, how I was an animal... I will tell you everything, without hiding anything.

All kings of ghosts and gods have great dignity. They can slash demons, eliminate disasters and subdue pagans. They use the Chieu Phuc method to subdue all left-wing sects, ghosts, goblins, bull demons, and snake gods. All bad elements, evil knowledge, evil views, evil magic and evil methods, they all have the ability to subdue them all. They can create good, destroy evil, exorcise evil, and destroy demons. Evil is an example for those who do not care about morality. Those who are stubborn and do not care about reason are very strange and overbearing. They are all reincarnated from demons. No matter how kind you are to them, they won't know that you are good. Even if you sacrifice all your flesh and blood for them, they still won't know enough, nor will they thank you because they have bottomless greed. Why so? Because they have gone through many lifetimes of cultivating evil habits, those evil habits have become ingrained, and the bad nature is formed from darkness and stupidity that they refuse to change.

The demon kings in the Shurangama Mantra command their relatives such as: heavenly soldiers, heavenly generals, heavenly warriors, vajra athletes... All of them are concerned about protecting all ten directions, protecting practitioners and supporting to make the ashram more prosperous. Above, we talked too much about the types of demons and their relatives. You should know that all living beings, each type, has its own "ghost soul". Dogs have dog ghost souls, cats have cat ghost souls, large living beings and small living beings all have their own ghost souls. Although people often say they are afraid of demons, in reality there is no division between humans and demons. Demons are in the underworld, people are in the earthly world, but yin and yang are inherently one entity, regardless of high or low, without limits. Demons have strong greed, anger and ignorance.
