Therefore it is said: "Ma Ha Tat does not care about people, Amitabha Buddha takes care of everyone." That is the principle of the Hinayana. And they view the three worlds as a house on fire and birth and death as unjust, so they take care of themselves to escape birth and death, and do not care about the birth and death of living beings.

If we are concerned about others, then the thought is of benefit to others. I want to be liberated myself and also want to make all sentient beings liberated. That is the Bodhisattva's thought. In other words, forgetting oneself to benefit others, that is, practicing the Bodhisattva path. So say:

"Buddha's light shines, Dharma's martial arts shine." Practicing the Bodhisattva path should be based on the spirit of "Unconditioned great compassion, great compassion."

If we truly think about the ashram, we should support the ashram in all aspects. We should not seek fame, profit or any other intention. That is truly supporting the ashram.

Every day we should reflect and examine ourselves, whether we calculate a lot for ourselves, or calculate a lot for others, or worry a lot about the ashram. Through such reflection, we will know whether we have broken our ego or not. This is just a simple way of saying it. If we speak more deeply, that means asking: Are we afraid every day that we will be disadvantaged? Are you afraid every day that you won't get any benefits? If you have those thoughts, you should change them; otherwise, try to avoid them.

We should also reflect and examine ourselves to see if we are patient or not. For example, if someone is ungrateful, scolds you for no reason, or hits you, can you be patient? Am I angry? Do I have revenge in my heart? If there is, it means the ego attachment has not been broken. If not, it means the ego has been broken. Think carefully: Where do all the problems and troubles come from? Well, it's all caused by the ego's strange actions. If we do not break the ego attachment, then the dharma attachment will be even more impossible to break. The Hinayana level has broken the attachment to ego, but has not broken the attachment to dharma. Only Bodhisattvas can destroy both ego and dharma attachment.

After breaking the ego attachment, we must destroy the dharma attachment. Why is it called legal attachment? That is, we do not understand clearly that the five aggregates (form, feeling, perception, actions, consciousness) arise from causes and conditions, so we accept them as real. If we can get rid of all attachments, we will be completely harmonized without hindrance and will be free in any realm. When both ego attachment and dharma attachment no longer exist, then only is a true practitioner. A true practitioner, at any time or under any circumstances, absolutely does not calculate for himself. On the contrary, always sacrifice yourself for others and enthusiastically do good deeds. Their actions are all impartial, upright and unbiased.

Buddha teaches the Tripitaka and the Twelve Collections of Sutras, there is no place that does not teach people to break their attachments. But we still do not listen to Buddha's teachings, but want to be traitors in Buddhism, which means we are still attached to our "Self". The appearance of a self is not yet empty, the appearance of a person is not yet empty, the appearance of a living being is not yet empty, the appearance of a life-person is even more non-empty, but we cling tightly to these four characteristics, so we cannot let go.

As for the morality of the three minds, we cannot understand nor know clearly. The past mind cannot be had, the present mind cannot be had, the future mind cannot be had either. Why? Because the "past" mind has passed away, where do you go to find that mind again? The present never stops, you say this is "the present" but

This “now” has passed. The present does not exist, so the present mind cannot exist. The future mind is also not available, because "future" means it has not yet arrived, but if it has not yet arrived, why talk about it?

As the Diamond Sutra says:

“No self form, no human form,

There is no form of living beings, no form of life.

Again:

“The past cannot be attained by the mind,

At present the mind cannot attain,

The mind of the future cannot be attained.”

Everyone can read these verses, but no one remembers to do them. I hope you will rely on the above sutras to make good use of them. Once the "four signs" no longer exist and the "three minds" are completely eliminated, that is one who practices the true path.

Preached on February 15, 1984

Luc Can Support -

Dieu Bat Khac Ngoc

Ordinary people only know: The eyes can see colors, the ears can hear sounds, the nose can smell scents, the tongue can taste flavors, the body can know feelings and the mind can know dharmas. If you say the principle "the six bases are useful," they will never believe it, and will think it is baseless words. But if we have truly reached this realm and achieved this use, we will know for ourselves that the Buddha Dharma truly has this kind of realm, which is truly indescribable and inconceivable.

Some people mistakenly think: "I don't want to have a realm like that! Why? Because it's too troublesome. When I look up, I see the movements of heavenly people, and can even hear their voices, which will affect my purity of mind. Just like when I look down and see the situation in hell, my mind is frightened and paralyzed, so haunted that I can't sleep at night. Therefore, I don't like to have a realm like that."

Even if you like that kind of realm, it is not certain that you will achieve it. Why? Because you don't seriously meditate, or even if you meditate, you have delusions, wandering thoughts, your ape mind keeps running away, and you can't control yourself. Or maybe you're meditating and falling asleep, dreaming that you're chatting with Chau Cong, then snoring loudly, your breathing is as strong as thunder. In a situation like that, how can you become enlightened, how can you reach a place of miraculous use - you're just wasting your time!

To reach that realm, you must have no delusions. You must be like: seeing but not seeing, hearing but not hearing, smelling but not smelling, tasting but not tasting, touching but not touching, thinking but not conditioned. If you are not shaken by the realm, then you can reach that realm. If your realm is shaken like: "Ah! I can see the sky so far away! Then I don't know if I can sleep or not?" Let me tell you everything, once you reach that state, you can still sleep as usual. Whenever you want to sleep, sleep; if you don't want to sleep, don't sleep. Feel free and at ease, you absolutely do not have to do anything forced. Such magic!

People who have just had delusions like the above, after hearing me say that, they think again: "I have delusions, but how can Master know? Or does Master have other people's minds?"

Why do you have that delusion? If you have that delusion, how could I not know? If you are afraid that I will know, then don't give rise to that false thought. You should know that, because the six senses work together, everyone can achieve this wonderful effect, it only depends on whether you practice or not!

The Venerable Ana Luat Da did not use his eyes, but could see the entire three thousand great thousand worlds as clearly as seeing the Am-ma-la fruit in his hand. That's because although his eyes were blind, he achieved heavenly vision.

Although Long Bat Nan Da has no ears, he can use his heavenly eyes to listen to sounds to save people in distress.

The six senses of the goddess Ganga (god of the Ganges River) can all smell scents; Regardless of the sense, it has the ability to smell and know everything.

Venerable Cau Pham Bat De did not use his tongue but could taste flavors because he used his nose to replace his tongue.

Although God Thuan Nha Da (God of Emptiness) does not have a body, he can use other senses to contact him and therefore knows that all dharmas are empty. So he is the god of nature.

Venerable Mahakasyapa did not use his mind to know the truth of the true form of all dharmas, that is, formlessness. Formless also means "without any form," nothing is without form.

Above are examples of people who have achieved the wonderful mutual use of the six senses.

Lecture on February 16, 1984

In the Unlucky

There is Great Luck

Hey students! The best time of a person's life is before the age of twenty, which is called: "The Golden Age." During this period, your inherent Buddha nature has not been lost and your pure self-nature still exists. At that time, if you come into contact with good people, you will be a good person. And if you hang out with bad people, you will become bad people. Children are very easily influenced by surrounding circumstances. As the saying goes: "Close to lipstick, it's red, close to ink, it's black" means that principle.

If you meet a good teacher and good friend, you will gain true education and have dignified conduct. On the contrary, if you meet teachers and friends who do not keep rules and regulations, you will be influenced by them and will become people who do not keep rules and regulations. If it is small, it "harms the herd of horses" meaning that one horse harms the entire herd of horses; Anything bigger will ruin society.

Remember! Your self-nature is like a pure white cloth. If you dye it blue, it is green, if you dye it yellow, it is yellow. You are in such a good learning situation, in the future you must definitely become someone who benefits society, and improve society in a better direction. You should have the spirit of sacrificing your selfish small self to become a big self that cares for the masses.

Hey students! Most of the students come from abroad (such as students from Vietnam, Cambodia and Eastern countries

South Asia), was once overwhelmed by the suffering of leaving home and losing the country. In a time of excitement and insecurity, you have a special predestined opportunity to come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to study, to build the foundation of being a good person. This can be said to be a place of great misfortune but great luck.

Because the mission of Duc Luong Primary School in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is to cultivate students into excellent and honest people, making them know how to be filial to their parents, know how to respect their teachers, know how to choose good friends and be loyal to the country.

The educational mission of Bui Virtue High School is to foster students with moral concepts and know about the four moral principles: propriety, righteousness, integrity, and shame, so that in the future they will be good and upright people. This is the fundamental ambition of the school at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.

Since you have such a good learning environment, you should know how to cherish your time, your life, and also how to pity all sentient beings and all material things. Don't let your precious "golden age" pass by in vain. You should not read novels or watch television, but should make an effort to study, which is called: Read with your mouth, think with your mind, same in the morning, same in the afternoon (Khau Nhi chanting. Tam Nhi Duy. Trieu u tu. Tich u tu.) Whichever book the mouth reads, the mind should think about the morals in that book; Morning or afternoon, I think about the morals in the book. Don't forget what you've learned in the book at any time. Always review the lessons you've learned.

In the book Analects, it is written: "Welcoming the old child, knowing the new," reviewing old lessons can gain new knowledge, that is, that morality.

Currently, children are in the learning period, except when helping with housework, they should take care of their studies. Take your time, don't waste it.

The ancients said: "An inch of time is an inch of gold, but an inch of gold is difficult to buy an inch of time." You see, how precious time is! So it is said: If you don't try when you're young, you'll regret it when you're old. In the golden age, if you don't study, you won't have time to regret it when you get old!

Hey students! During their youth, they encountered many hardships, had to leave their homeland, and travel to find freedom on the path of exile and exile, suffering unspeakable suffering. You have gone through so much hardship to reach a land of peace. That's because in many previous lives, you didn't know how to cultivate blessings and wisdom, or you caused trouble for others, causing them to suffer. Because of that, today you are suffering. These are all feelings due to the karma of the previous cause and effect. Even though you are still young, you have experienced all kinds of disasters. If you don't develop Bodhi mind and don't try to study, then your future will be more dark and dark than bright. Do you understand?

Now the students studying at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, have learned the Six Great Principles: not fighting, not being greedy, not seeking, not being selfish, not taking personal advantage, not lying and understanding the spirit of being a true human being. This is a good opportunity for you to correct your mistakes to start a new life, to create a bright future for yourself. You should not let it pass in vain, but must clearly understand its important nature. This is the key point that affects your entire happy life.

Now that you have come here, in addition to taking care of your studies, if you know how to take advantage of this good opportunity and regularly practice, sincerely recite Buddha's name, worship Buddha, meditate, sit quietly and practice like that, you will probably achieve a super power such as: Divine eye penetration, Heavenly ear penetration, other mind penetration, life-saving penetration, even divine power or astronomy. Right now I only teach four passages, later I will continue teaching about the remaining two passages.

Why is it called heavenly vision? That is, on the earth, you can see every gesture, every move, every word, every action of the heavenly people very clearly, without any obstacles. Currently in China, there are many children who, even though they are indoors, can see things outside the walls. They can know what other people are holding in their hands. That is called the heavenly eye, which is also the effect of clear vision.

Why is it called heavenly ear communication? Being able to hear the gods talking, being able to hear Buddhas and Bodhisattvas speaking, or being able to clearly hear people talking from thousands of miles away. Currently in China, there are some children who use their hearing to read words written on paper. That is, someone had previously secretly written words on paper, then they put the paper to their ears and listened for a bit to know immediately. Try it a hundred times and you'll get it right, not a guess. These effects are due to the good roots they have cultivated in previous lives. But if there is no wise man to guide them, then when they are past childhood, they will lose these special powers.

Why is it called altruism? That means you can know whatever other people think in your mind very clearly, clearly, without any hindrance.

Why is it called sufficient network information? Is it possible to know very clearly about other people's past cause and effect, such as knowing what good karma they have created, or what bad karma they have committed? If you seriously practice, you will gain even more of this special ability, and you will be able to open up great wisdom and attain miraculous powers of unhindered eloquence.

Many children in China have this special supernatural ability. But unfortunately there is no one who understands this kind of talent. Therefore, these talented people with supernatural powers are all forgotten. For Buddhism, that is truly unfortunate!

If we know how to actively cultivate and help these little prodigies develop their ability to preach the Dharma incarnate, it will make people have a different perspective on Buddhism. For example, people have just awakened from a nightmare and realized that Buddhism is indeed the religion that saves humanity.

They are currently studying at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. If you are willing to single-mindedly study Buddhism, I believe that you all have the opportunity to gain such professional abilities. Those things are not superstition, but the truth. Like television, radar, tape recorders, telephones, telegraphs, etc., they also have the ability to have supernatural powers such as clairvoyance and clairaudience, but these are magical powers invented by humans, not natural supernatural powers. If through meditation one can attain magical powers, that is truly the free application of magical powers. As long as you have the will, you can cultivate and achieve such realms.

Lecture on March 5, 1984

Students at Gold Mountain Monastery

Why is it called Humanity?

A compassionate person is a person who loves everyone. This word benevolence, in terms of humans, is an expression of benevolence, having the thought of putting oneself in another person's situation, called: "If you don't want to push something on others." If you cannot accept something yourself, do not assign it to anyone else. If you force people to do things that you yourself don't like, that person has no compassion.

A merciful person is one who endures disadvantages and is patient, called:

“The first child is reluctant, the ninth child is natural,”

That means at first I felt forced and uncomfortable, but over time I got used to it and it became natural, and I no longer felt forced at all.

This word benevolence, if we talk about it in terms of things, means we need to have patience and do everything to perfection. That's why it is said: "If you seek purity, you must practice diligently, diligently, and thoroughly, and your contact will be profound." If you want to do good things, you need to work hard. When you have worked hard enough, you will know immediately when something happens. No matter what we do, we must: if we have done it well, we still want to do it better, until it is perfect. But how to do this? That means we must have hard work.

Why is it called suffering? That is the word "Forbearance".

The word forbearance ( ) is like the image of the heart ( ) being stabbed by a knife ( ʳ ), so it hurts extremely. This means we must endure pain, endure suffering, must fast from hunger, from thirst, from wind, from rain, from heat, from cold, from everything. We must endure! Hold on! Hold on! Patience with all the things that cannot be endured. For all things, we must work hard and endure suffering. We have to work hard, and when our efforts are complete, we will naturally achieve success. At that time, we can “hear one and know ten.” We will open the door of wisdom and for everything about things and reason, we will suddenly understand everything thoroughly, that is, at a glance we will know immediately, there is no obstacle at all.

We can also use seeds to talk about this word cause. For example, when growing cereals, we must choose good, large seeds. Because good varieties will germinate strongly, and when autumn comes, there will be a large harvest. Every farmer understands this clearly. If we don't choose good seeds, don't plow, and don't water and fertilize, then when autumn comes, we won't be able to harvest anything, which is called: "If you plow partly, you'll harvest partly."

The situation for students studying at school is similar. While at school, if you work hard to study and research to understand the principles in books, of course you will become useful talents later. But if you don't seek to understand the profound meaning and just study to get things done, then after graduation you won't have a career you're good at, so you won't be able to find a way to make a living. Then the children become a burden to their families and parasites in the commune

society and are despised by others.

Seeds are divided into two types: sentient seeds and inanimate seeds. The seed of a sentient being can give birth to four types of animals such as: fetus, ovum, lower body, and transformation. The unintentional seed will give birth to herbs, plants and minerals such as iron and stone.

Sentient beings are species with feelings and nature. Insentient beings are species that do not have feelings but have nature, called: "Sentient beings without emotions, of the same intelligence." The nature of sentient and inanimate beings is interconnected, because they are inherently one. The inanimate is temporarily inanimate, if they can return to their original form, they will also become sentient. But this is not so easy, because it takes a very long time for them to have a chance to return to their original form. That opportunity is like a very small speck of dust in three thousand great worlds. Besides, even if they transform into sentient beings, they are still low-class animals like larvae, worms, and ants.

Although we are sentient beings, we are only temporary, not permanent. If we are not good people, our spiritual nature will change and decline, then turn into a heartless plant. Therefore, ancient trees all have ghosts and spirits residing inside. Why? Because ancient trees and ghosts and gods have a close relationship with each other. Humans and ghosts are also interconnected, there is no separation. Cultivators must clearly understand this principle and should not fall into the position of a vegetable. Although plants have nature, they cannot easily transform into sentient beings.

Hey students! Everyone can return to their original nature and become a Buddha, as long as they soon develop Bodhi mind and try hard to practice; Otherwise, when you fall into the state of indifference and turn into plants, it will be very difficult for you to practice. At that time, if you regret it, it will be too late!

Lecture on March 6, 1984

Ancient tree in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas

Hung Vuong Buddhism -

tieu_de: Prosperous Buddhism - Responsible People /
tom_tat: When the Buddha Dharma is about to be on the verge of destruction, whether it is a Bhikkhu, Bhikkhuni, Upasakas or Upasaya, they should take the revival of Buddhism as their mission, calling

Prosperous Buddhism - Responsible People /

When the Buddha Dharma is about to be on the verge of destruction, regardless of whether it is a Bhikkhu, Bhikkhuni, Upasakas or Upasakas, they should take the revival of Buddhism as their mission, called:

"The world rises and falls, the seven men are responsible."

Now we can say: "Buddhism rises and falls, people are responsible." As Buddhists, we should be even more responsible, not leave it to others. We should ask ourselves: How should we revive and promote Buddhism more brilliantly? This means you should have deep reflection! Every hour, every moment, you should examine yourself! Have I done the things worth doing? If not, then why haven't I done it yet?

Promoting Buddhism is everyone's job. But only when everyone is assigned to cooperate and work together, such as: Those who have money contribute money, those who have strength contribute, and work together to unite and unite, can Buddhism flourish again. That's why there is a saying: "Unity is strength." We should not be scattered like scattered sand trays, nor should we have the notion of remaining indifferent, that is, just standing by and watching.

As Buddhist disciples, once we clearly understand our mission, we should not have any reliance on ourselves: "Anyway, there are already people propagating the Buddha Dharma, I am just a member, so I have no influence." If everyone has such thoughts, then when will Buddhism be revived and become exceptionally glorious? I'm afraid I never will!

In this era, if there is no one in the world who truly devotes himself to practice and becomes a leader, I am afraid that Buddhism will gradually decline and eventually go to the point of destruction. Since we are Buddhists, we should wholeheartedly take care of Buddhism. During the period of propagating Buddha Dharma, we should move forward boldly, not be timid and worry about the future, nor be afraid of people's jealousy, or of being hindered by others, because those are all tests and challenges. Because once it goes through the fiery furnace, it takes thousands of times of heating and hundreds of times of forging to become fine steel, called:

"In the middle of suffering, in the middle of suffering, the way is for the superior person." To be able to endure extreme hardship in a miserable situation is to be superior to others.

Those are the words of someone with a lot of experience. We should sincerely devote ourselves to Buddhism, should bring our solid will and sincere determination to do Buddhist work. Only then can Buddhism change for the better every day.

Ten Thousand Buddhas, the Holy Saints, is the true place of practice. Everyone knows we are absolutely not liars. Therefore, we must sincerely follow the Dharma and practice it, not pretend to wear a mask to deceive people. We should also not have the idea of ​​desiring fanciful things, far from reality. Whatever you know, do as much as you can, that is the true duty of a practitioner. If we only know how to talk but do not act, then it is just lip service, not good at all. So how can we have any hope of reviving Buddhism again?
