noi_dung:
Everything Is Created by the Mind /

In the Avatamsaka Sutra, it is said: "If anyone wants to know clearly, all Buddhas of the three times, should contemplate the nature of the Dharma realm, all created by the mind." That is, all moral principles are manifested by the mind. All Buddhas of the three times also manifested through the mind. In short, everything is created by the mind. People can create heaven, people can also create hell. Practicing the ten good deeds creates heaven, practicing the ten evil deeds creates hell. The mind can also create humans, asuras, animals and hungry ghosts. The human mind is wonderful like that. Because it changes all the time without leaving a single thought, it is said that "all is created by the mind."

Every time our mind begins to meditate, the Buddhas see and know everything. But most of us humans cover our ears to steal the bell, deceiving ourselves, thinking that Buddhas and Bodhisattvas probably don't know, ghosts and gods don't know, and everyone doesn't know. When we have thoughts like that, we will create many crazy things, harm others, harm ourselves, and make huge mistakes.

As for Buddhism, we should support ashrams and consider revitalizing Buddhism as our responsibility. We should not create evil karma in the ashram and should understand that it is all created by the mind. Therefore, at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, Dharma Realm University, Virtue Cultivation High School and Duc Luong Primary School all take the Six Great Principles: don't fight, don't be greedy, don't seek, don't be selfish, don't seek personal gain, and don't lie as teachings.

Lecture on April 12, 1984

Retribution for Killing

The world's greatest hatred is nothing more than "killing". So it is said: "If you kill someone, pay your life, if you owe a debt, pay the debt." If you kill someone's father or brother, they will kill your father or brother. Just like that, they kill each other, never ending. Because there are too many people who kill living beings, the retribution comes very quickly, called "retribution in the present world" or present retribution.

Why do people today often develop so many strange diseases? In short, it comes from killing. If you kill living beings, living beings will come to you to claim their lives. Regarding those strange diseases, doctors have no choice but to give up. So what should you do? That means you must sincerely repent, correct your mistakes to become a new person and do many meritorious deeds that benefit sentient beings, so that you can eliminate past karma. If you don't do that, I'm afraid you won't be able to heal easily. This is truth, not superstition.

Ulcers on People's Faces in the Present Life

Today I will tell two koans about killing. Around 1945, there was Venerable Dai Minh, abbot of Thua Thien Pagoda, Suzhou Province, China. Although this Venerable is a Buddhist, he believes in paganism and in the temple worships the Fairy Fox. Therefore, the foxes in this temple freely enter and exit without being chased away by anyone, and they are also not afraid of people. Humans and foxes live together peacefully.

At that time, the Venerable Master was in retreat at this temple to review and read the Tripitaka. The fox also came to the Venerable's room to practice together. While the Venerable recited the sutras, he slept on the Venerable Buddha's cushion. When the Venerable wanted to bow to the Buddha, the Venerable said to him: "I want to bow to the Buddha, you go out!" At that moment, the fox obediently walked out of the room. Waiting for the Venerable to finish the ceremony, he went back in and continued to sleep on the cushion to worship Buddha. Every day was like that, over a long period of time and the two sides became like friends.

One day, the Venerable Master had a bit of a temper. When it was time to pay homage to the Buddha, the Venerable told him: "If you don't come out immediately, I will beat you to death!" The fox glared at him as if he didn't care about the Venerable, then he closed his eyes and continued to sleep. Perhaps he thinks something like this: After all, monastics also have the ambition to be compassionate and use means as a gateway. So it doesn't go.

So at that time, the Venerable Master got angry and said: "Why is that so! You really want to overwhelm the host as a guest! I'll beat you to death!" Having finished speaking, the Venerable took his stick out to scare it away. But the fox still didn't pay attention. In anger, the Venerable waved his stick and took a breath. Unexpectedly, the Venerable lost his hand and broke the fox's head, causing blood to stain the Buddha's offering mat red. Indeed, the Venerable Master beat it to death. The Venerable Master committed the crime of killing, so he felt extremely regretful and did not know how to resolve the matter amicably. How can this sinful karma be eliminated? Thinking about it, I can't think of a way. Suddenly, the Venerable's spiritual nature suddenly remembered that someone had said: if you kill a fox and give its meat to others to eat, you will eliminate the karma of killing. So the Venerable peeled the fox's skin and gave the meat to the workers - thinking that was the end of the matter.

Unexpectedly, seven days later, the fox spirit came to the Venerable and said: "I have gone to the King of Hell to denounce you, you must pay for my life!" The Venerable was in the middle of meditation when he heard that, so he was extremely frightened. So the Venerable began reciting the Great Compassion Mantra. Thanks to the blessing of the mantra, the fox could not get close to the Venerable, so it had no way to harm him. But it refused to leave, and it always came to harass him. Seven days later, the fox knew that he could not take revenge on his own, so he went to ask for reinforcements. Can you guess which reinforcements it asked for? They are the souls of Japanese soldiers who died in battle during Japan's invasion of China. The fox gathered many troops, then they used cannons to shoot at the Venerable's body. But they bombed for many days but could not hit the Venerable. Why? Because the Venerable concentrated all his spirit on reciting the Great Compassion Mantra, without leaving his seat, the artillery shells did not hit him but kept falling around the Venerable.

After many days of not eating or drinking, the Venerable Master was truly exhausted. In an instant, the Venerable felt confused and panicked and unfortunately the Venerable's right knee was hit by a cannon. So the Japanese soldiers immediately retreated. The Venerable escaped the artillery threat, so he felt extremely happy because he thought the matter was over. Just thinking like that, the Venerable felt pain right at the spot where the cannon was hit. The Venerable looked down and saw a boil on his right knee that resembled a human face, with a mouth and teeth. The wound is both swollen and painful, and no medicine can cure it.

One day, someone told the Venerable: "If you put fatty meat on the mouth of a boil, the pain will go away." The Venerable Master tried it and it certainly worked. But when the piece of fatty meat was eaten with pimples on his face, the Venerable began to have pain again. And just like that, the Venerable was tormented by boils all the time, and his suffering was unspeakable. After many painful days, the Venerable suddenly realized that only by destroying all karma can one be free from suffering. So the Venerable devoted himself to practice and did not care about the pain anymore. The Venerable tried to patiently endure the pain and single-mindedly worshiped the Buddha and repented of his karma of killing. After three years, the Venerable Master recovered from his illness.

This Venerable is a true practitioner. He often went to places to consult and study with wise men and also visited four famous great mountains (Wutai Mountain, Emei Mountain, Jiuhua Mountain, Putuo Mountain) and eight great and small mountains in China. The Venerable Master is a very virtuous person. Even though he accidentally killed the fox, the Venerable still had to repent and worship Buddha to eliminate karma. Therefore we should know that the karma of killing is the worst. Please pay attention! You should not kill living beings but should do a lot of merit to release living beings. If you arbitrarily kill living beings, you will suffer from strange diseases that cannot be cured, or you will become disabled and regret it for the rest of your life!

Boils on the Face of People from the Past

During the time of King Y Tong of the Tang Dynasty, there was a National Teacher named Zen Master Ngo Dat. When the Master was at Cu An pagoda, Truong An province preaching sutras, King Y Tong personally came to listen to the Dharma and specially gave the Master a throne made of sandalwood and incense. At that time, the Zen Master became arrogant and considered himself the highest monk in the world, with no one equal to him. Unexpectedly, as soon as false thoughts arose in my mind, the Dharma Protector immediately left the Zen Master and walked away. So the unjust bondholder had followed the Master for ten generations. Now when he found an opportunity to take revenge, he struck the Master in the shin. From then on, a pimple appeared on the Zen Master's knee with a human face, with eyelashes, eyes, mouth, and teeth. Every day it must eat meat and drink wine. If you don't give it meat and alcohol, the boils will become painful and indescribable. Many doctors are at a loss, there is no cure.

While Zen Master Ngo Dat had not achieved the glorious title of National Master. One year at the temple in Truong An, the Master met a monk who was suffering from a strange, poisonous wart. Pimples that ooze and bleed look really dirty, and also give off a foul smell, making people want to vomit. Everyone did not dare to go near the sick monk. At that time, Zen Master Ngo Dat was in the next room, coming every day to take care of this sick monk. The Zen master wholeheartedly served, offering food and water and cleaning the monk's wounds without worrying about the filthy stench.

Time passes without realizing it, summer passes and autumn returns. As the climate became cooler, the monk's ulcer gradually healed. When they were about to say goodbye, the sick monk said to Zen Master Ngo Dat: "Thank you for taking care of me. In the future, if you have any trouble, come to Mong Son in Sichuan to find me. On the mountain there are two giant pine trees as a sign. My name is Ca Nac."

Zen Master Ngo Dat reminisced about the past and went to Mong Son to find the monk who had suffered from poisonous boils before.

From afar, looking halfway up the mountain, the Master saw two pine trees towering above the clouds. When he arrived in front of two pine trees, he discovered a brilliant golden pagoda. Just as I was about to go look for him, I saw the monk waiting in front of the temple door, smiling, then took the Monk inside. After Zen Master Ngo Dat bowed to the monk, he told clearly about his suffering. The monk told the Zen Master to go down to the rock ledge under the stream the next morning to clean his wound, and that would heal him.

On the morning of the second day, the young monk took the Zen Master to the cliff under the stream. Just as he was about to wash the wound, the boil on his face came out and said: "Please don't wash! There is an unresolved grudge between us. You are a high-ranking monk, you have read many scriptures, you must have read the history of Western Han. So do you know the story of Vien An slashing Trieu Tho's waist? Vien An is you now, and Trieu Tho is me in the past. You have been a monk for ten lives, practicing seriously, so I have not found a chance to report it." Because he was arrogant, I had the opportunity to sneak in. Today, thanks to the compassionate Venerable Ca Nac, who wanted to reconcile the resentment between us, he used the samadhi method to cleanse me, so from now on, I will no longer resent him.

After National Teacher Ngo Dat finished listening, his soul wandered

spread to cloud nine. The Zen master quickly scooped up water to wash the poisonous boil, but he felt a sharp pain in his bones, then fell into a coma and lost consciousness. After a long time, when I suddenly woke up and looked down at my knee, I could no longer see any traces of the poisonous boils. Only then did the Master know that the monk was a holy monk. The National Master intended to return to the temple to admire and worship the monk, but as soon as he turned around and looked back, he could not see the temple anywhere. Then the grass monk set up a tent in that place and took care of the chanting in the morning and evening. The National Master is the author of the Dharma Repentance, as we know today, the "Compassionate Samadhi Water Repentance" consisting of three volumes.

Through the two stories above, although there are a few differences, they are mostly the same, they are a warning to people that the cause and effect of retribution is truly without error. The first story is the retribution that takes place in this life, and the second story is the retribution that occurs in the next ten lives. In short, when karma matures, our destiny has come and we will eventually have to suffer retribution. Today I talk about these two koans so that everyone can clearly understand that killing is harmful, and should not be seen as a child's game. Nowadays, science is getting more and more advanced, so the weapons used to kill people will also get worse. How can they eliminate all the causes and effects they have caused?

Currently, the world is in a dark place full of miasma, if you touch it a little, a great war will break out. The resentful demons will use this as an excuse to take revenge. But the unjust retribution, who knows when will it end? Unless it is not killing; Otherwise, we will never have a day of peace.

Lecture on April 15, 1984

tieu_de: Boils on People's Faces in the Past / 94 Why Are They Called Six Great Tong Zhi? /
tom_tat: Look! Currently, most people in the world are almost crazy, looking like mentally ill people. This world is about to turn into a crazy world. Whether male or...
noi_dung:
Boils on People's Faces in the Past / 94 Why Are They Called Six Great Tong Zhi? /

Look! Currently, most people in the world are almost crazy, looking like mentally ill people. This world is about to turn into a crazy world. Whether male or female, old or young, they are not aware of the basic conditions of being human. That's why there's a scene where you fight and I win. Because they want to achieve their personal goals, people ignore all tricks, forget the meaning, and sell out their friends. How scary! So what are the basic conditions to be human? That is, the Six Great Sects of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. If everyone obeys like this, the world will be peaceful.

Luc Dai Tong Chi means:

1- Don't compete: Don't compete with anyone. Keep what you should have, and don't have what you don't need. Absolutely do not get angry.

2- Don't be greedy: Regardless of material things, as long as you have enough, that's enough, and don't be greedy for anything. If you need my things, I will give them to you. We should not be greedy and greedy.

3- Don't seek: Don't seek outside things

is: "Humanity does not seek high self-esteem," people do not seek

that is, a person of noble character. Every person has a cause

The way is to be content with few desires, with little desire to know enough. Person

Not greedy for wealth, not greedy for beauty, not greedy for fame, no

If you are greedy for food and not greedy for sleep, your mind will be more peaceful and your heart will not feel afraid at all.

4- Not private or selfish: Whatever belongs to the public for everyone's convenience, we cannot hide it for ourselves. You can give alms, which means you don't have self-centeredness or selfishness, which is called: "Seeing all the elderly as our parents, loving all children as loving our own children." That is the manifestation of a person without selfishness. The establishment of universities, high schools, primary schools and nursing homes at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas also came from that thought.

Honoring the Elderly, Gold Mountain Monastery

5- Not self-interest: It means sacrificing yourself for others. If something is beneficial, we let others do it. On the contrary, if something is not beneficial, leave it to yourself to do. Absolutely never be greedy for fame and fortune, or buy fame and fortune, because those are thoughts

self-interest, self-interest.

6- Do not lie: There are four crimes in the mouth: false speech, false speech, evil speech and double tongue. A person who commits one of these crimes will in the future fall into hell and have his tongue cut out. False speech is one of the Five Precepts. Those who study Buddhism should definitely keep the Five Precepts. What is false language? Is telling lies, called: Seeing - saying you don't see; don't see - say see; listen - talk don't listen, don't listen - talk listen; don't understand - say understand, understand - say don't understand; know - say don't know, don't know - say know. That is false language.

Why do people in the world go crazy, so crazy? Because they have a competitive mind, a greedy mind, a seeking mind, a selfish mind, a self-seeking mind, and a mind of lying. That's why they keep going crazy all day and can't be at ease. This is a very serious problem. We should not take it as nonsense but quickly improve social customs, otherwise we will suffer unimaginable consequences.

Lecture on April 16, 1984

tieu_de: Descendants of the Demon King /
tom_tat: The Buddha used the power of concentration to overcome the supernatural power of demons while fighting with them. At that time, the demon king said to Buddha: "Now I have no way to defeat you, but wait until the future, when...
noi_dung:
Descendants of the Demon King /

The Buddha used the power of concentration to overcome the supernatural power of demons while fighting with them. At that time, the demon king told the Buddha: "Now I have no way to defeat you, but in the future, when your disciples do not have enough concentration and their knowledge is not right, at that time I will break through the door and enter your house, wear your clothes, eat your rice, and then I will urinate in your bowl, see what you will do!" Shakyamuni Buddha calmly said: "Then I have no choice."

Apparently, currently, there are people who have become monks publicly saying that the Amitabha Sutra is fake, for the reason that in the sutra there are sentences that have no basis for verification such as: "From here going to the west, passing through hundreds of millions of Buddha lands, there is a world called Ultimate Bliss." He asked: "Which local official measured that? Comparing the distance of 100,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 Buddha's Buddha lands, he asked. These are really stupid arguments, just making fun of people!

Recently, there was a monk who announced to everyone that the Shurangama Sutra is a fabrication and should not be believed. Because based on the passage: "On the occasion of the taboo day of my father, King Ba

Tu Nac set a boy to invite Buddha to the palace. The king personally welcomed the Tathagata, and set out a full set of precious foods," he said, saying that this passage was not in accordance with Indian customs at that time - because filial piety was not preached in India. He therefore determined that the Shurangama Sutra was a fabrication, not preached by the Buddha. That was the act of destroying the sutra to slander the Buddha, and the retribution of this defamation is hard to imagine. This monk's thoughts are so childish! Where is the Master's mind, you can think about it. I know!

In the Dharma Ending Sutra, it is said: "When the Dharma Ending Period comes in the future, the Shurangama Sutra will be destroyed first." Because the Shurangama Sutra represents the Dharma era. If there is no Shurangama Sutra, there is no Dharma. Currently, there are many mountain monsters and water monsters, they maintain that the Shurangama Sutra was not spoken by Buddha, and want people not to believe it. If you don't believe in the Shurangama Sutra, then you can use a pen to erase it all without believing it! Why? Because there is no basis! So you can see that the demon king's mind is truly too cruel!

This is also because the Shurangama Sutra speaks the truth so clearly. Meanwhile, the demon king cannot keep the Four Kinds of Purity and Repentance, or the four pure precepts, nor can he practice the Dharma Door of Perfection of the twenty-five Saints, and he even does not dare to read about the realm of the Fifty Types of Skandhas. Because it is afraid of revealing its true form, making people know its true face, that is why it seeks to destroy the Shurangama Sutra. This destruction is not about burning the sutras, but rather destroying the sutras from the hearts of sentient beings, causing people to lose faith in the Shurangama Sutra.

Things in life are magical like that. Very few people are aware of it. Just like business, people selling fake drugs have a lot of money, while people selling real drugs have no one buying them. Why? Because no one truly recognizes its value. That's why I say that no one recognizes the truth, but the fake makes everyone fascinated. That's a very easy to understand principle!

Currently, it is the end of the Dharma period, and many people slander and do not believe in monks who truly practice the Buddha Dharma. But the monks, because the sermon was so bustling, had so many people coming to listen to the Dharma, that there was no more room in the lecture hall, people were crowded together like bait fish boxes, making it hard to breathe. Yet there are monks who promote the slogan of not being vegetarian. This monk told everyone: "Everyone who is a vegetarian has a greedy mind; but a non-vegetarian has no greedy mind." Such reasoning is truly laughable to the whole world, blinding people's eyes, making people confused - confused, confused again, confused until they go to hell, never to escape.

Therefore, when studying Buddha Dharma, we need to have a Dharma eye, an eye that knows how to choose the Dharma, so that we can clearly distinguish between right and wrong, right or wrong, and good or evil. Otherwise, we are like a blind man touching an elephant, unable to find the true truth. Whatever people say, I repeat it, listen and then follow along. People say an elephant is like a wall, I also say an elephant is like a wall. People say elephants are like pillars, and I also chimed in and said elephants are like pillars. After all, what is an elephant like? We all don't know. When studying Buddhism, we must understand its principles, not follow them blindly. Everyone should pay special attention to this point!

Lecture on April 17, 1984

It's Not That It Looks Different

I come from the countryside and had very little school education, so I don't know much. That's why I want everyone to gather together, as the saying goes: "Gathering useful ideas," is to gather many useful ideas. Use everyone's intelligence to discuss issues together. If anyone has any valuable comments, please feel free to state them. We consult with each other to improve education.

After becoming a monk, I realized that the state of Buddhism was deteriorating day by day, so I wanted to improve it. I feel like the education system is also going downhill every day, so I hope to make things better. I vow to use all my strength to benefit people. Because of this aspiration, I have now established Dharma Realm Buddhist University, Virtue Cultivation High School and Duc Luong Primary School at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. And to fulfill that wish of mine, all classes are free.

Why do I want to do that? Is it because I'm eager for fame and reputation, or is it because I want to style things differently? That's not it. My intention is to reform the school's business system, so that money-minded people in the education department will change these unjust ideas. They should take educating and training students to become honest, talented people as their guiding principle. Although the idea of ​​school as a business is deeply ingrained, it is not easy to change. But I ask everyone to join forces to rebuild this cause, so that we can gradually sensitize school business owners, making them see their conscience and realize that education is a divine work. Because education is training talented people in the world, it is a fun and pleasurable job. If they are still confused and refuse to wake up, it's just to make some stinking money, without knowing any regrets, they will harm the students' future prospects. This sin is truly unforgivable and they will regret it forever. We should know that money is something outside the body, it is not brought to birth, and it is not brought to death. That's why it is said: "You can't take all things away, only your karma and sins will follow you." The karma we created while we were alive will go down to hell so we can suffer without interruption. By then, even if we regret it, it will be too late!

On May 27, 1984, Dharma Realm Buddhist University will hold a graduation ceremony. Students who meet good ethical and academic standards will be given a certificate of academic standing upon completion of the course. Normally during the ceremony, university graduates will wear black hats with four square corners. Whether they are bachelors, masters or doctors, they all wear the same hat and the world recognizes this.

Students graduating from Dharma Realm Buddhist University are also allowed to wear hats, but there are improvements such as: Bachelors will wear four-cornered hats, Masters will wear five-cornered hats, and Doctors will wear six-cornered hats. Why should that be? Because each type contains different meanings. The four corners represent that the people in the four seas are all brothers, and also mean that the four directions are all transparent; It also represents the Four Immeasurable Minds: kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity. The five corners represent the Five Elements: metal, wood, water, fire, earth; or the Five Basic Precepts: killing, religion, lust, delusion, alcohol; or also representing five continents: Europe, Asia, Africa, America, Australia. The six corners represent the Six Virtues: generosity, morality, patience, diligence, meditation, wisdom; or represent the six directions: east, south, west, north, above and below; It can also be said that the six corners represent six professions: ceremony, music, radiography, courtship, poetry, and numbers. Those are my opinions, I hope everyone will give their opinions so we can research together and then decide.

Someone said: "Because of tradition, all students who graduate from university wear four-cornered hats." But in my view, if there is a good method but we don't use it and still keep the old rules, then it must be said to be too stubborn, it can also be said to be foolish.

In the West, I have never met anyone who graduated from a genuine Buddhist University. Buddhism here is just starting, so there are no definite regulations yet. Dharma Realm Buddhist University is the end of space, transforming the Dharma Realm, boundless and vast. For now, no one knows, but in the future there will be many people imitating the way our school does. So now I propose that lay students will wear black hats when graduating from university, and monastic students will wear yellow hats when graduating from university. I don't know if this opinion is valid anymore!

Lecture on April 20, 1984

Educational Motto of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas

No matter what we do, we must have patience and do it slowly without rushing. You should know that the Holy Roman See (Rome) was not established in just one day. Similar to the above argument, educating students does not take just one or two days to teach them to understand clearly. But it takes a strong, long-term mind to teach them how to become good people, and how to create the basis for good character. Not teaching students how to get a good job and make a lot of money to enjoy themselves. That is a utilitarian way of education.

The educational motto of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is to teach students about humanity and morality. In the future, when we serve society, no matter what position we are in, we will work based on morality and humanity. They absolutely will not band together to do anything wrong, nor will they harm others for their own benefit.

You remember! We should not be greedy for fame, nor should we learn from the pseudo-gentleman style of pretending to be a philanthropist, doing a little work and then advertising and propagandizing ourselves wherever we go. We should study true virtue, and practice it practically. Our educational method is completely different from the educational method of other places. It's not that we want to destroy their education to highlight our own education; It's not that we want to compete or compete with anyone. We just want to maintain our stance on education to teach the next generation. It doesn't matter whether people do things right or not, we just want to do things right, and not against our conscience, that's enough.

Lecture on April 25, 1984

tieu_de: It's Not That It Looks Strange
tom_tat: Practitioners must definitely cultivate the Four Immeasurable Minds. When we have the Four Immeasurable Minds, we can teach and transform living beings and make them happy and free from suffering. If a cultivator does not have the Four Immeasurable Minds, that means doing...
noi_dung:
It's Not That It Looks Strange

Practitioners must definitely cultivate the Four Immeasurable Minds. When we have the Four Immeasurable Minds, we can teach and transform living beings and make them happy and free from suffering. If a person cultivating the path does not have the Four Immeasurable Minds, it means doing the opposite of the path and even if one cultivates for eighty thousand eons, one is still eighty-four thousand kilometers away from the Buddha path.

The Four Immeasurable Minds are the basic conditions that every practitioner should have. Why is it called the Four Immeasurable Minds? That means kindness, compassion, joy, and forgiveness. Immeasurable is without limit, which means not giving up halfway, or not reaching the middle of the road and then drawing a limit for yourself, not wanting to move forward. If you just get that little bit, then you take it as enough and think it's over. In fact, Compassion, Joy and Forgiveness is never enough, but the more you have, the better. We should expand and strengthen our compassion, joy, and forgiveness until we reach the realm of perfection.

The word is possible for joy. Do we give living beings joy? If we don't have it, it means we are not using all our compassion. We should move toward the goal of "unaffiliated pronouns," which is to treat those who have no affinity with us with compassion. We should not only sympathize with people in difficult situations, but we should also sympathize with animals in need. If something unfortunate happens, we should help and help sentient beings escape the cycle of suffering. That is the work that Buddhists should do. We should not have an indifferent attitude, just stand by and watch without helping, thus losing the savior spirit of Buddhism. On the contrary, Buddhism takes compassion as its ambition, using Buddhist means to receive sentient beings.

Compassion can eliminate suffering. Can we eliminate the suffering of sentient beings? If we can't, it's because we haven't used all our compassion. We should have the thought of "oneness and great compassion," which means seeing people drowning as if we were drowning, seeing people who are hungry as if we were starving ourselves. Buddhism uses compassion as its guiding principle, because compassion is compassion and mercy. Meanwhile, Confucianists say that "compassionate compassion" is also consistent with the above meaning. Therefore, we know that the thoughts of saints in the world are the same, as if starting from the same tire tracks, inseparable from compassion and mercy. Buddhism advocates compassion, Confucianism promotes loyalty and forgiveness. Similarity of mind and heart, that is the essence of religion, otherwise it is a heretical theory of paganism.

Joy is a happy mind. Are we happy and excited to learn the Buddha Dharma? Do we experience sadness, trouble, or frustration? If that is indeed the case, let's quickly change it and not give rise to such a behavior. If you still have a little bit of habit energy, then apply the effort from the seven emotions and six desires, then that is a wrong concept. We should understand that we must not continue to have such misconceptions. If not, we cannot imagine what the consequences would be.

Equanimity is the mind of letting go. Do we have the mind to let go? If yes, is it big or small? Is it temporary or permanent? Discharge what? It is to develop the mind to give living beings happiness, eliminate their suffering and help them in difficult situations. If we can do that, we will be filled with infinite joy, but we should not be attached to it - once we have finished the task, we should forget everything and not keep it in our minds. If we accept but cannot forget, that is not the Bodhisattva's vow. We should have the spirit of doing kindness without asking for reward in order to be considered true Buddhists.

Lecture on April 26, 1984

Path of Kindness & Path of Joy at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas

tieu_de: Rings Are Priceless Treasures /
tom_tat: As Buddhists, we must know patience. Ring what? It is to endure what one cannot endure. Someone said: "I really can't stand it anymore!" If we can't endure it all, it means we can't "finish" it. Run out of…
noi_dung:
Rings Are Priceless Treasures /

As Buddhists, we must know patience. Ring what? It is to endure what one cannot endure. Someone said: "I really can't stand it anymore!" If we can't endure it all, it means we can't "finish" it. Out of what? It's the end of karma. If karma is not eliminated, emotions are not empty, meaning there is still birth and death. Therefore it is said: "Karma is not important, it does not give birth to Saha. Love is not cut off, it does not give birth to the Pure Land." When karma is exhausted and love is empty, only then will we end birth and death and be truly liberated.

Practitioners should practice patience. Enduring hunger, enduring thirst, enduring wind, enduring rain, enduring heat, enduring cold, to the point of having to endure scolding, and enduring beatings. These scenes are all challenges. As I often say: "Everything is a test, see what you will do? If you don't know the situation, you have to practice again from the beginning." No matter what adversity we encounter, we should accept it with the mentality of "the opposite is true." We should not let the situation change, or raise a white flag to surrender. The ancients said: "If you don't hold back on small things, you will ruin big things." Patience is a priceless treasure: "Patience for a moment, the wind calms down; take a step back, the sea is wide and the sky is blue."

When Shakyamuni Buddha was still alive, one day he passed by the riverbank and saw a wild canan (of the wolf species), wanting to eat the turtle. But the turtle withdrew its head, retracted its limbs into its shell, and then lay still without moving for a long time. Because the wild goat did not have patience, he left, but the turtle, thanks to his patience, saved his life. The Buddha told Venerable Ananda: "Practice practitioners should also be like that." The ancients said: "I have recently learned the way of the turtle, when it is worth withdrawing your head, withdraw your head."

If you can endure anger while you are angry, you will be worry-free for a hundred days. If people curse at me, it's like I'm enjoying a popular song. If someone hits you, it's as if you accidentally bumped into the doorpost while walking. If you visualize like that, no matter what kind of spear or spear it is, it will naturally turn into jade and silk. Otherwise, the fire of ignorance will rage and rise three feet high, causing a great battle. As a result, both sides were injured, not only emotionally, but also lost their personality and were criticized for lacking composure.

Therefore, it is said: "If you endure all the world's tyrannical energy, nurture it until the fiercest spring," that is, to endure a hundred times of criticism from the world, it will grow into a spring song in our hearts. We can take these golden words as a motto for ourselves.

Lecture on May 5, 1984

Have Greed

Nothing Will Be Achieved

A practitioner should be as pure as his eyes

cannot contain even a single grain of sand. For example, if you have a grain of sand in your eye, you will definitely feel very uncomfortable and worry about finding a way to get it out immediately. Otherwise, your body and mind will not be at peace. Cultivation is the same. What is that grain of sand? It's greed. With greed, everything will begin to change. The original nature is pure, but once there is greed in the mind, it starts a chemical effect, turning clean water into dirty water. This is not beneficial to others, on the contrary, it is harmful to ourselves.

As long as a cultivator has one part of sincerity, he will have one part of achievement and inspiration. If he has ten parts of sincerity, he will have ten parts of achievement and inspiration. When we have achievements and inspirations, we should not harbor them in our minds. Because it is "abiding without a place", we should forget about it. Our main purpose of cultivating the Dharma is to escape birth and death, not to seek enlightenment. You should remember this! When we practice, we should not have any intentions, such as wishing for achievement or wanting to be inspired, because that is a huge mistake. Everyone should clearly understand this point. If you practice single-mindedly and single-mindedly, when your practice reaches maturity, you will naturally achieve success and inspiration. But if you practice without intention, you will never achieve anything and will never have any inspiration.

As the saying goes: “To have a mind is delusion, to have no mind is to feel

response.” You can hope for inspiration, but you should not pray.

Practitioners should: "Only ask about plowing, not about harvesting." No matter what we do, we should do it with all our heart and not care about the results. No matter what, we should be clear and righteous, the starting point is only for work and not for private, not to have a selfish mind when working and not to calculate and worry about success or failure. When working for the public, we should do the same. We should not be afraid, like in front there is a wolf, and behind there is a tiger. Because if something happens, no one dares to take responsibility, and then push responsibility onto each other. Small things are like that, but if you think about big things, you will know.

Don't have the delusion that stupid people do, that they don't go to school but want to get a PhD; do not plant crops but want to harvest grain; Don't buy horse racing tickets and claim to win the first prize. There's no such thing as convenience. Just like in the spring, you have to worry about sowing seeds, plowing, watering, and fertilizing, then in the fall you can harvest. So saying: "Part of the plowing, part of the harvest," is a natural principle!

Please pay attention, do not give rise to greed for pursuit, greed for achievement, greed for inspiration, because that is a dream, like walking in a dark world and also do not deceive yourself. If you don't clearly realize your goal, you will waste your precious time for nothing, and it will be too late to regret later!

Lecture on May 17, 1984

tieu_de: Having Greed will not achieve anything / 113 Ignorance Is the Foundation of Birth and Death /
tom_tat: Ignorance means greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, and doubt. These five negative karmas can drive people crazy
noi_dung:
Having Greed will not achieve anything / 113 Ignorance Is the Foundation of Birth and Death /

Ignorance means greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, and doubt. These five types of negative karma can make people go crazy.

Greedy mind: For favorable circumstances, we will have such craving that we cannot have it without it. There are even people who want to achieve their goals but regardless of tricks, otherwise they would not be willing.

Anger: When we encounter adversity, we will be angry and angry. If we don't curse people, we will beat them, even kill them. This is all caused by anger, it causes people to lose both reason and will to do things. People with such a mind will certainly make society unstable and orderly.

Stupid mind: A person who has no wisdom, does not know right from wrong, and cannot distinguish between good and evil, so he is confused and crazy, and as a result, he becomes a dishonest person and creates many criminal karma.

Arrogance: Is promoting oneself and oppressing others. I think I'm better at everything, more outstanding than others. This kind of arrogant and arrogant behavior is a taboo, we should not have it.

Doubtful mind: A person who is skeptical about righteous things and does not believe anyone's words. People with such mentality are abnormal and are wrong because they lower themselves.

These five types of psychology are all abnormal and are all caused by ignorance. Practitioners must destroy ignorance and not let it cause such endless disasters.

Ignorance makes ordinary people only know how to spend their time on sexual things. They think that love in the world is real, so they can't stay away from it and can't bear to let it go. Therefore, they are entangled with their six relatives and cannot let go. Then they create so many mixed good and evil, they cannot distinguish between pollution and purity. Life after life, they keep spinning around in the cycle of birth and death, never ending forever. Therefore, ignorance is the basis of birth and death.

People who practice don't have those kinds of troubles weighing down their minds, so they can easily become pure, liberated, and free from birth and death. If we do not cut off ignorance, we will forever be controlled by it, then go to hell, run to the mountain of knives, or into a pan of boiling oil. At that time, we will regret why we did not practice diligently in the first place. But unfortunately there was no time left.

I would like to advise you to practice in a timely manner, don't think that the days are long and make appointments.

The ancients said: "Don't wait until you're old to learn the Dharma. There are many young people in the grave." After studying the Dharma for one day, you will be a little closer to the Pure Land. So little by little, you will reach the Pure Land. If you don't diligently cultivate the Way and want to go to the Pure Land, you won't be able to get there! The work in the world, even if we waste time doing it, ultimately has no benefit. But only the method of practice is not a waste of time. If you practice for one minute, you will gain one minute of benefit. So it is said: "Gather sand into a tower," meaning step by step, step by step, constantly moving forward, you will naturally reach the other shore.

Lecture on July 5, 1984

People of the Ky Kingdom are worried about the sky collapsing - Finding themselves suffering

Some people have false thoughts in their hearts: "I wonder if when I get old, I will die of hunger or cold?" This is an unhelpful way of thinking. As true disciples of Buddha, even if we die of hunger and cold, we have no reason to think that if we sacrifice for Buddhism, there is nothing more glorious than that.

In the past, Shakyamuni Buddha spent three eons cultivating blessings and wisdom, and hundreds of eons cultivating good signs. Of all the great earths and lands in the three thousand great thousand worlds, there is no place, even as small as a speck of dust, that is not the place where the Buddha gave up his life. We should examine our hearts to see what we have let go of? Even the things outside my body that I can't bear to give up. We are still controlled by our own, selfish minds, so we can't give up this thing, we can't give up that thing, let alone the matter of giving up our lives, we can't even talk about it!

You should know that: because we cannot let go, do not give alms, do not have sympathy, do not know mercy, that is why we constantly rotate in the cycle of reincarnation. We only worry all day about what to do when we get old, but we never think about what it will be like when we die. It's like a person in the Kingdom of Ky who was so sad all day that his face was so gloomy that he never showed any joy. Someone asked: "Why are you so sad?" He replied: “What if the sky falls? Wouldn't we be crushed to death?” It's true that this way of thinking is so childish!

We are practitioners, so we should live each day as a meaningful day and not let delusions overwhelm us. If we keep thinking wildly all day long. Isn't that a very stupid person? Because if you think about impossible, unnecessary things, that's really making things difficult for yourself, making yourself miserable!

Now we need to counteract delusion to return to enlightenment, so let go of the false to grasp the true. I often tell you: "If you don't get rid of the false, you won't be able to achieve the real; if you don't get rid of death, you won't be able to change life." Worldly Dharma is relative! If the other side is heavy karma, then this side is gentle purity. If this side is more pure, then the karma on the other side will be lighter. Just see how you want to do it. This is all up to you to decide according to your preferences, no one bystander has no way to interfere.

As monastics, we should have noble personalities, be outstanding people, surpass everyone else. Monastics should not join together to accomplice with bad people, only know how to eat and wait for death, making the Buddhist atmosphere become heavy, not enthusiastic at all.

Lecture on July 15, 1984

tieu_de: People of the Ky Kingdom worry about the sky collapsing - Finding self-suffering / 118 Cultivating Noble Character /
tom_tat: The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a place of spiritual practice, so the Heavenly Dragons of the Bat-Buddha always protect and maintain this ashram. If you develop Bodhi mind, they will definitely protect you and make your body and mind feel light and peaceful,...
noi_dung:
People of the Ky Kingdom worry about the sky collapsing - Finding self-suffering / 118 Cultivating Noble Character /

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a place of spiritual practice, so the Heavenly Dragons of the Bat-Buddha always protect and maintain this ashram. If you develop Bodhi mind, they will definitely protect you and make your body and mind feel light and peaceful, achieve great achievements and have great inspiration. But don't have hope in your heart that you will be like that, then those things will naturally appear. If you still have hope for achievement and inspiration, that is greed and also a violation of the Six Great Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.

The daily activities of practitioners in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas do not depart from the following six items:

No fighting. Absolutely do not compete with anyone. Nor do we compete for fame or profit. Whatever other people like, we give it to them, without having to fight for it. It's called: "If you fight, you won't have enough, but if you give, you'll have a surplus," meaning that if you fight, it's not enough, but if you give, you'll have a surplus.

Not greedy. It's not that you say you're not greedy, but when the scene comes, you only worry about being greedy, you can't ignore it, that's wrong. We need to be: Words follow actions, and actions follow words, don't let them contradict each other. Only a person without greed can cultivate a noble personality.

No demand. If we have desires for something, we will have afflictions. If we pray but don't get it, of course we will be troubled. Therefore, it is said: "If you don't seek, you won't have any worries," if you don't seek, you won't have any worries - what a wise saying. Once we reach the level of non-seeking, our character will naturally be noble. Humanity does not seek self-centered qualities, that is. In the Eight Sufferings, there is "sought without suffering," just as if one did not receive one's wish, one would suffer, but one would also suffer if one received one. Because of worrying about gain and loss, we seek suffering for ourselves. So why do I have to suffer like that? If you see clearly and let go of everything, you will no longer be troubled.

Not selfish or selfish. Everyone has selfishness. We always plan for ourselves first and worry about our children and grandchildren first. Therefore, those who practice must cultivate to the realm of selflessness. If we have no self, what else do we want to fight for, what do we crave, what else do we want? We deny everything, and don't want anything. We must learn to follow the Bodhisattva's spirit of sacrificing ourselves for others. Why is this world so stuffy and full of miasma, and never so pure and bright? Because everyone is selfish and self-interested, as if saying: "This is mine, that belongs to me," it causes great chaos and the world is not at peace.

No self-interest. If everyone does not have self-interest, always knows enough, and feels peaceful in any situation, then naturally everyone will live together peacefully. If a person has a greedy mind, he is like a fish chasing bait. When he sees the benefits, he forgets all gratitude and then does things that harm morality. How many people have ruined their reputations and ruined their families for profit? Some people even caused the country to lose their homes, to the point of having to wander without a place to stay.

No lies. Regardless of the circumstances, we absolutely should not lie. Whenever we see, we say we see, when we hear, we say we listen. Let's just speak honestly and don't say unfounded things. We should know that lying is telling lies, harming others without any benefit to ourselves, and after death we will definitely fall into hell and have our tongues cut out. There is no doubt about that at all. So we must be very careful.

Today I tell you some very superficial words, but if you are willing to act according to that principle, they will be extremely useful. That's why there is a saying: "Speak well! Speak wonderfully! But if you don't practice, it is not Tao. Tao is action, if you don't practice, how can there be Tao? Virtue is doing, if not how can there be Virtue?" If you can practice according to the Six Great Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, your character will naturally be nobler.

I would like to add one last sentence: You should not do stupid things like: "Haunting the spiritual ear" which means covering your ears to steal the bell. Because you cannot deceive yourself, but you also cannot deceive the Buddha! Ha's stomach must be full of devious things, then she thinks she can cover it all up to lie to everyone. Wouldn't that mean bringing absurdity upon yourself? I hope that everyone in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas will demonstrate that they are honest and exemplary people, so that people in the world can look at them with admiration.

Lecture on September 25, 1984

Welcome to the Holy City

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a newly-emerged ashram. It can be said that this is the area of ​​origin of Buddhism, and it can also be said that this is the area of ​​origin of Buddhism.

Why is it called the origin region of Buddhism? Because Buddhism in this world has reached the end of the Dharma era, and those who truly follow the Dharma and practice are few and far between. Although there are people who claim to be Buddhists, their actions are completely contrary to Buddhism. Because of this, Buddhists need to reform and reorganize to build a new Buddhism, making the Dharma last forever in the world. The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is determined to restore and revive Buddhism, so it is said to be the origin of Buddhism.

Why is it called the original land of Buddhism? Nowadays, many heartbreaking phenomena often occur in parts of the world, such as the destruction of Buddha and burning of sutras. Even temples have been converted into construction sites, factories, or entertainment theaters. The pure land turned into a dirty place, and monastics were oppressed to the point of having no place to stay. Some people even have to run to the mountains, and some have to go to remote coastal areas. People who practice in the mountains use wild vegetables for their daily meals, people who practice on the coast use seaweed to relieve hunger. They endured all the trials and hardships, but they did not change their will and remained dedicated to their practice. With that indomitable spirit, it truly made everyone admire him. If those practitioners who have endured many hardships want to come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to practice, we absolutely welcome them. We not only welcome those unfortunate people, but at the same time we welcome true practitioners from all over the world to come to the Holy City to practice with us.

Anyone who sincerely comes to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to do meritorious deeds, we all welcome them. This is a place where there is no distinction between sect, race, nationality or position and everyone is treated equally. Everyone in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas enjoys equality and freedom. The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a place that does not belong to anyone, but belongs to all religions and sentient beings around the world, including Catholicism, Christianity, Taoism, Islam, Judaism, etc. This is not an empty slogan but a true promise.

In short, no matter what religion, anyone who sincerely wants to practice, the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas welcomes them all. Therefore, it is said that the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a place to return to, the original land of Buddhism.

Lecture on September 29, 1984

tieu_de: Welcome to the Holy City / 123 Basic Precepts /
tom_tat: There is only one basic precept, which is not to be selfish. People who have a selfish heart will break the precepts; if they do not have a selfish mind, they will not break the precepts. With the same argument as above, anyone who has a selfish heart will break the law, and anyone who does not have a selfish mind...
noi_dung:
Welcome to the Holy City / 123 Basic Precepts /

There is only one basic precept, which is not to be selfish. People who have a selfish heart will break the precepts; if they do not have a selfish mind, they will not break the precepts. With the same argument as above, those who are selfish will break the law, and those who do not have selfish hearts will not break the law. Like some people who are unfairly judged by a court of law. That's because in the past they committed unfair acts against others, so today others also bring unfair deeds to them.

You should open your eyes wide to correct your thinking and see: People who break the law in this world are actually all motivated by their selfishness. All people who do not follow the rules are motivated by selfishness. If they were not selfish, they would not break the laws of this world.

So if you can practice according to the Six Great Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas: not fighting, not being greedy, not seeking, not being selfish, not taking personal advantage, not lying, then you will not only be a good person in the world, but you can also be a Saint in the world. The reason the world is in chaos is because people are selfish and cannot be selfless for the sake of great success.

Like some parties, they always say they are impartial, but in reality, they do things purely for themselves. That's why the world is in chaos, making people anxious and afraid of not being at peace. All of those feelings of not being at peace and fear are caused by selfishness.

Currently we are studying the precepts. Once we understand the precepts, we will know how to be human. Once we clearly understand our duty as humans, we will also clearly understand our duty as Saints. Therefore, studying the precepts is extremely important. So if we want to help this world, first of all we must not fight, not be greedy, not seek, not be selfish, not take personal advantage, not lie. We should use ourselves as rules and examples for others. Only then will this world become more and more peaceful every day. Therefore, when studying the precepts every Friday, we must be very sincere and respectful to gain benefits.

Lecture on October 5, 1984

Transforming Old Habits -

New Apostolic Selection

Today is the last day of the year of the Rat and tomorrow will begin the year of the Ox. At that time, we should correct our old habits and habits. Our actions in the past were all due to bad habits, so there were many illegal places. So starting from tomorrow onwards, we should choose a new tone and become a new person. If we still do not "know what is right now, what was wrong in the past," then our practice will not progress and will only be a waste of time!

Ladies and Gentlemen! Don't cover up your shortcomings, but promote your good qualities, which is called: "Seeing good people and focusing on improving yourself to be like them." We should follow the example and learn from Master Tang Tu's style. In Analects it is written that:

“Zeng Tzu wrote: Ngo Nhat Tam Tinh Ngu Than.

The schemer is disloyal.

Untrustworthy friends make friends.

"Transmission of no collection lake,"

Teacher Tang Tu said: "Every day I have three things that I need to self-reflect on: In my work, have I honestly done my best? When communicating with friends, have I been dishonest in any way? Have I reviewed and studied the exercises every day?"

Therefore, we should also follow those sayings to set an example for ourselves.

The Three Characters Sutra begins with statements such as: “Humanity

primordial, good nature. Proximity. The practice is long-lasting, the dog does not teach, the nature is natural." Meaning: When babies first come out of their mother's womb, their nature is good. Because nature and goodness are close to each other, it is said that "nature is close to each other," as they grow up, they are gradually conditioned by circumstances and contaminated by habits. As the saying goes: "Dye it blue and it will turn blue; dye it yellow and it will turn gold." So their nature gradually moves away from the good, so it is said: "The future is far away." During this period, if people are not properly educated to correct their old habits and restore their good nature, their character will change.

When we are young, we are taught by our parents and teachers to correct our bad habits to become better. But when we grow up, no one teaches us anymore. Therefore, if we want to change our character for the better, we must change it ourselves. Because of this, today's topic is: "Changing Old Habits, Choosing New Aspects."

We should clearly realize our goals. What kind of people do we want to be? How can one become a true Buddhist? What is our new motto? What is our new tone? Those are issues that we need to understand clearly. Otherwise, we will have no way to change our old habits and habits, nor will we have any way to choose a new tone. So you should pay attention to this point.

In short, those problems are very simple. That is, we should just conscientiously practice: "If the evil acts, the good will serve," meaning not to do bad things, but to do good things, that's good. If everyone practices according to this motto, we will naturally achieve our goal as humans.

The new motto is to completely destroy the diseases of jealousy, obstacles, high tributes, and pride, and not let them prevail. How can we destroy those four types of unjust mentality? That means using the Four Immeasurable Minds: love, compassion, joy, and equanimity to treat them. People with loving kindness will not have jealousy; If you have compassion, you will not create obstacles; If you have a happy mind, you will not pay high tribute; If you have a mind of letting go, you will not be arrogant. Please research and see if this is ethical or not?

The new principle is not to fight, not to be greedy, not to seek, not to be selfish, not to benefit, and not to lie. In fact, those things are the ancient principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. Although you have heard it many times, no one seriously practices it. Anything that you haven't practiced before is considered new. Once you have practiced, it will no longer be new. Today I repeat the old tone, discussing the meaning of Luc Dai Tong Chi as well, hope you will pay attention!

Why do we have troubles and worries? That's all because

There is fighting, there is greed, there is demand, there is selfishness, there is self-interest, there is lying, they are doing mischief. They control us so much that our body and mind are not peaceful and free. If we can subdue them, we won't be driven crazy. Then we will reach the realm of no worries, no worries and no matter the time, we will be free. Why can't we be free? In short, it is because we are turned around by those six realms.

When I was young, I liked to argue with people and often intervened in grievances. If something unfair happens, unless I don't know it, it's okay, but if I know it, I will definitely come out to argue right and wrong. I am also greedy, but what am I greedy for? It's greed for food, and children often have this bad habit. Like if there's something delicious that I don't have a part of, I have to fight for it to get it. When I was twelve years old, I began to reflect and examine my own character - Why am I so stubborn? Once it was clear, I immediately changed my mistakes to become a new person. From then on, I started bowing my head to my parents to show my repentance. Because in the past, I did many things that made my parents worry. From then on, I did not fight, was not greedy, did not seek, was not selfish, and did not seek self-benefit. I feel that doing so is very useful, so I still adhere to it until today and for the rest of my life without changing.

After that, in addition to bowing to my parents, I also bowed to heaven, earth, the king, relatives, and teachers. I also bow my head to pay homage to the great saints, great sages, great good people, and great filial people in the world, and even to the great evil people, I also bow. Why so? Because I want them to also change from evil to good. Every day I bow more than eight hundred times in the back garden, which takes about two hours, and no matter what kind of rain or wind, it doesn't hinder my worship.

Last time when I went to Golden Buddha Temple in Canada, I said

with the two Tam Bo Nhat Bai monks (Master Heng That and Master Heng Chao) saying: "You guys, if you don't fight, don't be greedy, and don't seek like that, how wonderful it would be! Not being selfish, not taking personal advantage, that is the magic in the magic, and there is no other dharma more wonderful than that. If everyone truly practices according to the Six Great Tongs, you ask, is there any dharma more outstanding than this?"

Ladies and Gentlemen! Make an effort to practice according to the Six Great Principles, only then will your practice progress. Otherwise, it's all just empty talk, just like eating cake won't make you feel hungry, like cooking sand won't turn into rice.

This Six Great Tongs of Order in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, everyone should remember to keep it in mind and not forget it. Because we have it, we let go of everything, we give alms to others, not asking others to give alms to us. Of course, if someone gives me alms, I won't refuse. But we should do our best to give alms. Whenever we have the opportunity, we should give a little alms. Whatever we do, if we can do it, we should do it, and if we can't do it, we shouldn't be forced.

Think about it! If we can do that, then what is there to be sad about, what is there that we can't let go of? If we seriously practice according to these Six Great Teachings, then we can truly understand Buddha Dharma. In other words, the truth of Buddha Dharma has been covered in the Six Great Teachings.

Not fighting: Not violating the precept of killing. Why must we kill? Because he wanted to compete, he fought with me, then committed acts of murder and arson. Moreover, if you don't fight, you won't kill, so you can keep the precept of killing.

Not being greedy: You do not violate the precept of stealing. Why steal? Because it is greed, desire for people's things as their own. Not being greedy means keeping the precept of not stealing.

If you don't ask for it, you won't violate the precepts. A man searches for a woman, that is a bridge. A woman searches for a man, that is also a bridge. If you can't pray, your soul will go crazy. Even in sleep, I dream and pursue things, my body and mind are not at peace.

Not being selfish: Do not violate the precepts of lying. Why lie? Because I want to protect my own rights, I lie wherever I go to deceive people. If people are not selfish, they will speak the truth wherever they go, and never commit deceitful acts.

Not taking advantage of oneself: Then one does not violate the precepts of alcohol. People who drink alcohol think that alcohol increases blood circulation, has benefits for the body, and will definitely make them strong. When drunk, people feel lightheaded like in a fairyland. That's because their self-interest is playing havoc.

Do not lie: We have covered the five precepts above, but because we want to raise awareness for everyone and especially emphasize the evil of lying, we add this section as a reminder.

At the Golden Buddha Temple in Vancouver, Canada, we often preach about the Six Great Sects to teach everyone, including the elderly, young people and children, to let them clearly know the important nature of Buddha Dharma. If people can truly not fight, not be greedy, not seek, not be selfish, not take personal advantage, not lie, then society will definitely be secure and families will definitely be happy.

If people in the world can strictly keep the five precepts and do not commit acts such as killing, stealing, adultery, lying, or drinking, they will have no afflictions or worries at all. That's why I say this Six Great Tongs is the most mysterious method. You can also say it is:

"The wonderful and profound Dharma is difficult to encounter in hundreds of thousands of eons. Now I see it, hear it, receive it, and uphold it. May I understand the Tathagata's true meaning."

I would like to say one more sentence: As a Buddhist disciple, we must at least strictly maintain these five basic precepts and thoroughly practice them. Only then can we be happy and free. Suppose we cannot keep those five precepts, then the 250 precepts of Bhikkhus, or the 348 precepts of Bhikkhunis, are even more difficult to keep. Therefore, in the Song Tho forest, when Shakyamuni Buddha was about to enter Nirvana, he advised Venerable Ananda to "take precepts as his teacher." Therefore, we also know how important the precepts are!

Lecture on February 19, 1985

Upper Dharma Lecture

At Kim Luan Temple, Los Angeles

I.

The Dharma king is wise to irrigate all things.

Biomedical medicinal stone cures poisons.

The Buddhas have the source of light and clarity.

It is necessary to cultivate the consciousness of impurities.

Mean:

The Dharma King's wisdom and water benefits all living beings.

Traditional medicine cures all poisons.

Buddhas are inherently luminous.

Try to clean it carefully so it doesn't get dirty.

The Dharma King is the Buddha. He used the water of Prajna to wash away the dust in the minds of living beings, to benefit all living beings.

The medicine of the physicians is effective in eliminating all diseases.

The Buddhas are treasures of bright light in a pure, often tranquil realm. But if we don't have anything, where will the dust of the world be?

We must clear away all false thoughts so that the full mirror of wisdom can appear. When things come, the mirror shines, when things go, the mirror is silent. The projection depends on the situation and the situation, there are no obstacles.

The original Buddha nature does not increase in the Holy, it does not decrease in the ordinary: The original Buddha nature is the truth. This truth does not increase in the Saints and does not decrease in ordinary people. Saints and mortals each have enough wisdom and light.

Just because of one unenlightened thought, the three manifestations are formed, then wander in the five beasts, circulating along the six paths: But because sentient beings have one unconscious thought of ignorance, they are born into the three subtle appearances: appearance, karma and transformation. Then from there, he wandered in the five realms: heaven, human, hell, hungry ghosts, animals and reincarnated in six paths, including three good paths: heaven, human, asura; and three evil paths: hell, hungry ghosts and animals. Due to doubts, sentient beings commit crimes, then have to suffer retribution forever in the six realms, unable to emerge.

Drifting thousands of miles, dispersing into thousands of connections: The nature of living beings is as crazy as water in a vase pouring out, dividing into countless branches, thousands of heads and thousands of connections, the more they scatter, the more chaotic they become. The more chaotic it is, the harder it is to gather back.

Like sea water breaking the shore, like a volcano erupting, the majesty of

It is more magical than an atomic pump, more magical than a computer: Once the self-nature is dispersed into ten thousand parts, it is like water overflowing and breaking a dike, or like a volcano erupting, its power is greater than an atomic bomb exploding. It is infinitely variable and more magical than a computer. For example, like the terrifying karma of sentient beings, good and evil keep interacting with each other, binding each other. Because it is inconceivable, humans cannot imagine it.

It's spread out in no order and we can't gather it together

Okay, I don't know how chaotic it is: That pervasive karma is becoming more and more amplified, to the point where it's impossible to correct the situation. We have to pay forever to pay off those pollution debts. No one knows what the future will ultimately be like?

Therefore, we should know the era of pollution and chaos

Despite the chaos, we should first awaken, develop Bodhi mind, use Prajna wisdom and clearly realize the purpose to move forward: Therefore, we should know that we are in a polluted world, so the country, environment, and air are also polluted. So where does that pollution come from? The source is from our one ignorant thought. Because ignorance belongs to fire, the more the fire burns, the more strongly it burns, the more the world will be covered with black smoke. Then it causes the person's character to be polluted, and the family is also polluted. You see! If a person smokes, all the six organs and internal organs turn black. Why is human nature increasingly obscure and dark? Because everyone is greedy for profit, no one is willing to be disadvantaged. Everyone is self-interested and self-interested, so how can the world not be corrupted? Therefore, at this time we need to clearly recognize that the era is chaotic and dirty, so that we can turn around and be alert and develop the Bodhi mind. We should use our great wisdom, not our foolish mind. When we clearly understand the truth, we should be sure to practice it, not do it dishonestly.

Hien Gate, Holy Coast, why worry about not being able to reach it? If we can do so, it means we have followed the example of the Sages, and in the future we will surely reach the realm of the Saints.

Today, the pagoda's dharma protectors, doctors Ho Kien Quoc, Tran Quoc Boi and Qua Gao, came to the pagoda to hold a ceremony to invite Son Sangha to preach the Dharma: These three lay dharma protectors were sincere in their hearts to pray for the Dharma, so they set up an altar to worship the monks to form a good relationship.

Now I'm going to preach a Dharma sentence, but what should I say? The Dharmas are separate from the appearance of speech, separate from the appearance of written words, and separate from the appearance of the mind. Actually, is there any Dharma left to talk about?

There is no Dharma that can be forced to preach the Dharma. The right lobe is enlightened and the right lobe is enlightened. Returns to the origin and returns to the family road. Transports the three chariots reciting the Dharma flower.

Mean:

There is no Dharma to say but to say, Whoever is enlightened, what is enlightenment? Returning to the source is the way home, Carrying three carts reciting the Lotus Flower.

There is no Dharma that can be forced to preach the Dharma: The Dharma is inherently unspeakable, called: "Language is cut off, mind action is destroyed." Even though we don't have written words, we must reluctantly use written words to preach the Dharma.

The right lobe is enlightened, the right lobe is enlightened: The ultimate goal is that no one is enlightened, and what is enlightened? Basically, the person who is enlightened and the place to be enlightened are all lost.

Returning to the original nature and returning to the family path: Returning to the self-nature of the treasure of great light, that is, our inherent Buddha nature.

Transporting three carts reciting the Dharma Flower: Often recite the Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma, and if we can pull three carts, we can go back home. (The three carts in the Example Chapter of the Lotus Sutra are: goat cart, deer cart, and buffalo cart, examples for Shravaka, Pratyekabuddha, and Mahayana.)

II.

One grain of dust implicates the Dharma Realm,

The sum of all phenomena is the Dharmakaya,

Buddhas mindlessly preach the sutras,

Bodhisattvas have the will to transform living beings,

The Five Aggregates are impure, and because of afflictions one attains fame,

The eight sufferings and non-sufferings, breaking attachments and liberating oneself,

The three minds are willow, the sutra family is la,

The five desires are empty, the land of lotus flowers, No fighting, no greed, no desire to gain,

There is no self-interest or self-interest.

Renew your ability to be truthful and not lie, the Japanese practice the nine virtues to deepen your true nature.

You people, will you attain the devil?

Reciting thoughts in thoughts, reciting objects supports,

Disturbing the universe, destroying the gourd,

Try the time of heaven and earth,

The eyes of the world of Ultimate Bliss are to record,

Ha tu looking outward and looking forward to pray?

Mean:

A speck of dust contains the entire Dharma world, All vast things are Dharmakaya.

Buddhas do not have the heart to preach sutras, but Bodhisattvas have the ambition to save sentient beings.

The five aggregates are not impure, because afflictions have their name.

The eight sufferings are not suffering. If you break the attachment, you will be liberated.

The three minds are not over yet, step by step is thorny.

If you don't have the five desires, lotus flowers will bloom everywhere.

Don't fight, don't be greedy, don't seek to get,

No more selfishness and self-interest.

Be honest and not lie,

For a long time, practice deeply cultivating your true self-nature.

Can the wise men understand?

Always remember, don't forget, don't help.

The stone broke the universe, punched the gourd.

At that time everything was complete,

The World of Ultimate Bliss is right in sight, what is the need to search outside?
