tom_tat: Studying Buddhism and cultivating is equivalent to good architecture: Bamboo is architecture. Like building a house, it is architecture. To become a Buddha, we must architect and build the foundation to become a Buddha. Good deeds are doing meritorious deeds, which also means doing things...
noi_dung:
Transforming Old Habits - Selecting New Apostolic Instructions / 127 Dharma Lectures at Kim Luan Temple, Los Angeles / 134 Buddhist Study Facilities /

Studying Buddhism and cultivating like Bamboo Thien Co,

Wealth nourishes blessings and wisdom nourishes mani.

Close to knowledge and practice of precepts,

The story of the Holy Daoist is amazing.

Mean:

Studying Buddhism is like building a house,

Compensate for blessings and wisdom, nurture mani jade

Close to the knowledge of precepts,

Listening to lectures in the morning, dying at night is miserable.

Studying Buddhism and cultivating is equivalent to good architecture: Bamboo is architecture. Like building a house, it is architecture. To become a Buddha, we must architect and build the foundation to become a Buddha. Good deeds are doing meritorious deeds, which also means doing good deeds. If we want to learn Buddha Dharma, we must first build the foundation to become Buddha. Once we have merit, blessings, and wisdom, we can achieve our goal.

Wealth and blessings, wisdom and wisdom nourish mani: Cultivating your blessings means doing a lot of merit. To cultivate your wisdom, you should read and recite Mahayana sutras. Diligently practicing Prajna means learning the wisdom method. Mani is Jade as Wish; also means the Four Immeasurable Minds: loving kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity. We should diligently practice these Four Immeasurable Minds, depending on the time and circumstances. This is a method that practitioners cannot miss.

Close knowledge of precepts: People who study Buddhism

should be close to wise people. When there is something we do not understand, we should ask wise people for guidance. In Analects it is said:

"Min Nhi is studious and willing to ask questions."

It means that people who are diligent and studious will not be ashamed to ask questions of those below them. For the sake of studying, even if they are not as good as me, I should still follow them to study. Good people are Dharma Masters who teach us, bad people are Precept Masters who teach us. The purpose of practice: morality, concentration, and wisdom is to eliminate the three poisons: our greed, anger, and ignorance. If we are not greedy, not angry, not ignorant, that means we have concentration, wisdom and will not be shaken by the outside world.

Trieu of the Possible Saint: Suppose in the morning we hear a Saint preach about the way to become Buddha, and then at night we die, we will have no regrets.

Ladies and Gentlemen! To study Buddhism is to bring out your true efforts, not to be afraid of being disadvantaged. When the time is right, you should take the trouble to take responsibility, accept being blamed, and devote all your energy to Buddhism. The main point of the Dharma is not to give rise to afflictions and not to get angry. We must endure everything: Endure things that others cannot endure; endure things that people cannot bear; eat what one cannot eat; wear things that other people cannot wear. If we can do that, then we are truly cultivating the Way.

Finally, I would like to tell everyone that patience is a priceless treasure, called:

"Hold on for a moment, the wind calms down; Take a step back, the sky and sea are vast."

If that's the case, then you'll be free and free! If we encounter people who do not know anything about morality and expertise in finding fault, finding fault, and causing chaos with unreasonable things, we must be patient, not argue with them. This way, the wind will naturally calm down and the waves will calm down. If you meet someone who gossips, spreads rumors about you, no matter how unjustly you have been wronged, or whether they say things that are not true, you must be patient! Because those are the unjust karma that I owed from the past. In this life, if they come to demand it, you should not resist and refuse to pay the debt. Once we have paid off all our debts, the sky and ocean will naturally be vast, meaning we will be free, without worries or worries, without worries or sorrows.

Lecture on March 16, 1985

Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara Comes to the Holy City

Today is the beginning of the Guanyin Chamber's spring season. I hope you will bring all your sincerity and earnestly recite the holy name "Namo Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva." Not only must the mouth recite, but the mind must also recite. The corresponding mind and mouth will form a block, naturally the sensory realm will appear. Please pay attention! Having a mind is delusion, not having a mind is a feeling.

Although we cannot go from the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, we can bow every three steps to the Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva ashram in Putuo Mountain. But if we can recite with sincerity, it will be the same, and we will be inspired by Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara to bless us, causing us to become enlightened and gain great wisdom.

The proverb says: "If you practice, you can, if you practice, you can, if you don't practice, you can't." This saying is very logical, it is called:

“Birth and death by yourself, end by yourself, Eat by yourself, be full by yourself.”

Other people absolutely cannot help you. Don't think that this retreat is a common thing as usual, then do it quickly and get it over with. Therefore, we should understand that time is very precious and not let it pass in vain.

If you sincerely recite the holy name, Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara will definitely bless you, help you destroy all past karma and grow more good roots. So know that, when you remember Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara will also remember you. This is called “induction and communication.” If you recite the Bodhisattva's name, it is a feeling, and the Bodhisattva's coming to bless you is a response. Just like a child calling for its mother, the mother immediately responds when she hears. That is the principle of induction and communication.

In short, when you attend the retreat, you must be more diligent and more diligent, and absolutely must not be lazy or lethargic. Why do we practice? Because willow will escape birth and death, in order to go beyond samsara. If we do not make an effort to practice, life and death will never end. Everyone should be quick and firmly step into the real world to practice. Don't use superficial efforts on the outside, because then we won't get anywhere!

Lecture on April 1, 1985

We Are All One Family

Today is the day to commemorate the birth of Avalokiteshvara. Hey lay people! People from Los Angeles, Seattle and Vancouver, Canada came to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to participate in this great Dharma conference. You have come with such sincerity, which is truly commendable.

Everyone who comes to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a member of the Temple of Ten Thousand Buddhas and is also from the same family. You should feel like you are returning home. Since we are members of the same family, today's vegetarian meal, we don't care about whether the food is delicious or not. I hope everyone won't be so polite and think like they're eating at their own home. If there is a place where the hospitality is not attentive, everyone will forgive and ignore it, because we are all family.

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the land of origin of world Buddhism, and is also the place where Buddhism returns to its roots. You see! Buddhists from all over the world have understood that the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a living Dharma ashram, so they eagerly come to seek refuge. Among you, if there is anyone who wants to come to the Holy City to practice, we all welcome it. Although the food here is not delicious, you won't go hungry. Therefore, it is said: A gentleman seeks the Way and does not worry about earning a living. That means you come because you practice the Way, not because the food is delicious.

"The house has house rules, the shop has shop rules."

Any organization has its own rules. Without rules, if you don't have a compass, you won't be able to draw a circle, so of course the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas also has its rules. What is Thanh Quy? In the temple, you should not talk, and in the Buddhist temple, you should worship. When participating in a Dharma assembly, everyone should follow the group and not act individually. People coming to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas are definitely prohibited from smoking and drinking alcohol. The hippies weren't allowed to come. Why so? Because the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a pure ashram, I'm afraid they will cause chaos, disturbing the pure minds of practitioners.

The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the place where ten thousand Buddhas gather. So every year in the spring, we celebrate a great dharma conference, with thirty days of worshiping the Ten Thousand Buddhas, praying for world peace. The merit of worshiping and repenting is inconceivable, because it can eliminate disasters, increase longevity, eliminate sins and increase blessings.

Ten Thousand Buddhas Repentance Ceremony, City of Ten Thousand Buddhas - May 2007

Very few people in Asia worship the Ten Thousand Buddhas and Repentance, so misfortunes such as natural disasters and man-made disasters constantly occur in Asia. Why are there so many Asian refugees? If we look carefully at the previous benevolence, because in ancient times they did not know how to practice, did not know how to bow and repent, so they have planted evil results for today. Now we should reflect, and taking the opportunity of the Ten Thousand Buddhas and Saints to hold the repentance ceremony, we should participate in the worship to destroy all our mistakes first. I hope everyone will wake up! There is a saying: "It's not too late to build a barn if you lose a goat."

The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas seeks happiness for all humanity, so we have created a great forest to practice the Way. No matter who wants to come to the Holy City to practice, they can register at any time. The Holy City can accommodate twenty thousand people. Right now it's not full. When it's full, you won't be able to come even if you want to. Now is the right time, so don't ignore this personal right. And I'm just a doorkeeper for you. In the future, people from all over the world who come there will be the owners. I am just a worker, keeping the ashram clean so that you can concentrate on practicing so that you can leave suffering and attain happiness.

Lecture on April 7, 1985

Ordination Completely

tieu_de: Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara Comes to the Holy City / 143 We Are All One Family / 145ø If we leave the world, we will fall into ruin /
tom_tat: Everyone wants to become a Buddha, but becoming a Buddha requires conditions. Everyone wants to be a good person, but to be a good person you have to go through long periods of trials without changing your wishes. Just like every time…
noi_dung:
Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara Comes to the Holy City / 143 We Are All One Family / 145ø If we leave the world, we will fall into ruin /

Will be damned

Everyone wants to become a Buddha, but becoming a Buddha requires conditions. Everyone wants to be a good person, but to be a good person you have to go through long periods of trials without changing your wishes. Just like we always do all good things and do no evil things, only then are we qualified to be good people.

In our hearts, we want to be good people, but we have behaviors that refuse to cooperate with us. Just like there is no evil thing to do, even if there is good thing to do, one still refuses to do it. If mind and actions are not in harmony with each other, then how can we talk about being good people? When we first make our vows, we are very serious, but as time goes by, we become lazy. If we are not lazy, we are just living for the day, then forgetting all the wishes we had when we first made our vows.

As we talk about monastics, when we first became monks, we were very spiritual and made diligent efforts. But slowly our initial wishes change, we don't know how to move forward, and start doing things that go against our conscience. In the end, not only will we not become Buddha, but we will also fall into hell. There are people who have been monks for a few years, but cannot stand the tests and challenges. Due to changes in circumstances and lack of concentration, they were born again. From then on they do things as they please. Either they will make great fortune, or they will become high-ranking mandarins; However, those things are just illusory things in front of our eyes. But their retribution is like a shadow, difficult to escape.

Today I honestly tell you. Any monastic who wants to return to the world will definitely fall and suffer endlessly. That is the truth and I am not being polite at all when talking about this. One thought at the beginning is to become a monk and become a Buddha, and one thought at the end is to return to the world to become a demon. These are two paths that you must choose, the decision is in your hands.

If things in the world are not good then they are bad, if they are not successful then they are failures, if they are not prosperous then they are in decline. Therefore, it is said: "The superior man attains, the inferior man attains," the gentleman goes up, the petty man goes down. If you go up, you will reach the four stages of Sainthood; If you want to slip down to the stage of falling into the three evil paths, called: "There are two paths of good and evil, cultivating is cultivating, creating is creating." People with deep roots practice good paths, people with heavy karma create evil paths. If we tell them the truth, they won't believe it. On the contrary, if we tell a lie, they immediately believe it. Why? Because their karma is heavy. We have studied Buddhism for many years, but do not clearly understand the above principles, how pitiful! I didn't want to talk about this principle, because I thought you all already knew it. But now I know that people do not fully understand and are still stuck at the crossroads because they have lost their direction.

Now I will repeat to everyone: We humans are living in the great ocean of birth and death. If we cannot float, we can only sink.

There is a proverb: "Climb high, fall hard!" Ascension

We want to become Buddha, but if we don't go up, we cannot become Buddha; If you fall down, you will fall into hell, and it will be difficult to escape forever.

Someone asked: "After all, is there a hell?" I would like to tell you that as humans living here, we are in hell. You see, there are some people who are troubled, troubled, and argue endlessly. Isn't that like being in hell? What does it mean for people to live like that? There are also fire disasters, wind disasters, wars and other disasters caused by humans, so it's like living in hell on earth! Look, when people have illnesses on their bodies, they suffer beyond words, like when cancer is raging, they are in so much pain that they no longer want to live. Isn't that like hell? But people still don't see it, they can't let it go, they can't let it go, they're just worried about attachment and stubbornness, they don't have a compassionate heart, they see the benefits and forget the meaning, they're left with too much water and let it go. So in the end they are still stuck in the cycle of reincarnation, never ending.

Okay, I won't say anymore, otherwise everyone will be scared and run away!

Lecture on May 4, 1985

Destroy the External Three Evils

And Noi Tam Doc

Why is it called the three evils? These are murder, theft, and prostitution. Why is society not peaceful? It's also because of those three evils. Every day the news published in the press, more than half of the news is related to these three evils: murder, theft, and prostitution. That's why it is said: "among all the evils, lust is at the top," also because in the world there are eight or nine out of ten people who are motivated to kill because of lust. This kind of wind poison is so scary! If we do not commit murder, theft, or adultery, we will invisibly help society to be peaceful and maintain peace in the world.

Why is it called internal three poisons? These are greed, anger, and ignorance. If you are greedy without being bored, you will never have enough. If we are greedy and get it, we are happy. If we are greedy and we don't get it, then we are angry. Once we develop anger and ignorance, it will cause turmoil and encourage struggle. At that time we lose all reason, so stupidity appears, causing crazy things to happen without thinking about the consequences. Light things are contrary to love, but serious things harm heaven's principles.

How do we destroy the internal poison? Shakyamuni Buddha left us a very good remedy, which is precepts, concentration, and wisdom. People who practice Buddhism must keep the precepts. Because of precepts, the power of concentration arises, and from the power of concentration, the power of wisdom is born. These things are interrelated. If we can keep the precepts, we will not have thoughts of lust. When we have concentration, we will not have anger. If we can generate wisdom, we will not commit foolish actions.

The three evils of our body are brought about by the external nature of our body. The three poisons in our thoughts arise from our inner nature. Because once there is greed, anger, and ignorance, people will commit murder, theft, and adultery. If we can turn greed, anger, and delusion into morality, concentration, and wisdom, there will be no killing, stealing, or lust.

The three poisons pollute the self-nature, causing the self-nature to not be pure. The true mind was obscured and the false mind entered the house to be its master and command everything. Then it makes people crazy, confused, and never clear. This person's life is like a walking corpse, so what is there to talk about?

We must cleanse our own nature. So how to wash? Then use the Six Great Principles: don't fight, don't be greedy, don't seek, don't be selfish, don't seek personal gain, don't lie to this to cleanse, to sweep, and definitely clean until there's not a single bit of dirt left. If there were no wars, there would be no war in the natural world. Without greed for fame or profit, everyone will live in harmony with each other. If you don't seek, your personality will naturally be noble and you will be respected everywhere. Not being selfish means thinking about others and forgetting yourself, and not calculating with others, nor distinguishing between the four characteristics: self, person, sentient being, recipient. Not self-serving means that when we receive benefits, we divide them equally, without having the thought of wanting to monopolize. We even follow the principle of suffering ourselves, making others happy. No matter what we do, we use trust to treat each other. When you speak the truth, unnecessary trouble will not arise.

We use these Six Great Tongs to do with our bodies and our minds, thereby indirectly helping the national government and directly helping ourselves. We should clearly realize how important our responsibilities and obligations are. Therefore, we should be a complete and excellent member, not corrupt and cause chaos among the people. If we can do that, we will not be ashamed of being Buddhists. I hope everyone will take advantage of this aspect. If you specialize in searching for magical and eternal dharmas, then you abandon the roots to chase after the branches, which means you will never find the true dharma.

Finally, I hope everyone will throw the three internal poisons and the three external evils out of cloud nine, and never associate with them forever. Because they are petty people, whenever they see benefits, they forget gratitude. So if we are not careful, we will fall into their trap. Because they also welcome us to cooperate with them, to drift with them into the mud. Remember! Don't fall into their trap. We must be vigilant, and must have wisdom to reach enlightenment, that is, turn our backs on the worldly world to harmonize with enlightenment. If we do not know how to perceive clearly, it means we merge with the dust and turn our backs on the shore of enlightenment, we merge with the six ceilings to form a joint stock company with them.

Lecture on May 5, 1985

tieu_de: Destroying the External Three Evils and Internal Evils / 151 Proverbs of Buddhists /
tom_tat: We gather here together to study Buddha Dharma, but everyone should not be attached to Buddha Dharma. We should observe everything objectively and analyze things with our inherent wisdom.…
noi_dung:
Destroying the External Three Evils and Internal Evils / 151 Proverbs of Buddhists /

We gather here together to study Buddha Dharma, but everyone should not be attached to Buddha Dharma. We should observe everything objectively and analyze things with our inherent wisdom. Don't be superstitious or believe in a foolish, forced way. We should not accept enemies as children, wrong as right, black and white are not clear, good and evil are inverted. The most important thing is that we should be true Buddhists in our search for the truth, and not use tricks like the blind leading the blind, hypnotizing people to make them believe in a confused way, then doing chaotic good and evil deeds to confuse cause and effect. People who study Buddhism should pay attention to this point.

Why do we need to study Buddhism? Is it because we have a place to seek? If anyone is greedy, he should not study. Studying Buddhism requires eliminating greed, otherwise anger and ignorance will easily arise. Once we have greed, anger and ignorance will arise, so there is no need to discuss morality, concentration, and wisdom anymore.

Because our own nature is inherently Buddha, when studying and learning the Buddha Dharma, we should not be greedy for speed, greed for freedom, or greed for magical powers. Because those pursuits are contrary to religion, they make us forget the true meaning of studying Buddhism. We originally wanted to leave the sea of ​​suffering, get out of the burning house of the three worlds and leave suffering to be happy, but being greedy means that the more we learn, the more suffering we will have.

Six Great Tong Zhi: No fighting, no greed, no seeking, no selfishness, no self-interest, no lying is the maxim of Buddhists. If we can practice at any time and anywhere, then we are Buddhists who truly understand Buddha Dharma.

No matter what I say over and over, I still say the same principles. Although it seems very superficial, it is not easy for you to do. If you can do it, you will soon become a Buddha. If you practice according to these Six Great Teachings without becoming a Buddha, then I will forever stay in hell and never escape. I believe and guarantee that: Anyone who practices according to these Six Great Tongues will definitely become a Buddha in the future.

Lecture on May 20, 1985

Exploiting the Treasures of Self-Nature

From many years until now, it's just me telling you. So from now on, you will be the one to tell me. Why? Because this is to teach each of you how to exploit the treasures in the mine of wisdom of your own nature. We bring out precious objects such as gold, silver, diamonds, mother-of-pearl, agate, jade... from the mine for everyone to enjoy, that is only fair. Otherwise, in the end, no one will know what treasures you have in your treasure trove.

This lecture session on the Nirvana Sutra is called the Buddhist Dharma Research Committee. Regardless of whether they are monastics or lay people, everyone should compete to get to the podium first. You should take the study of Buddha Dharma, propagating the Dharma, giving alms and helping sentient beings as your responsibility. You must have such thoughts to be qualified to be a Buddhist.

Ladies and Gentlemen! Now you have such a good opportunity to study Buddha Dharma. This is truly a rare opportunity for thousands of years. So you should seize the opportunity, don't let it slip away. Otherwise, it would be like entering a treasure mountain and returning empty-handed, which would be a great pity!

Think about it, where can you find a pure ashram like this? I dare say I searched all over the world, I'm afraid I couldn't find it! If we are lucky enough to have encountered it, we should concentrate on studying Buddhism and develop our own talents. So why is it that when it's time to go to the podium, this person pushes past the other person, instead of going up first? It really makes me extremely disappointed.

I once said that when the first person is about to finish preaching, the second person must prepare to go up. That way you don't waste time. I want to train you to have experience in propagating the Dharma, because each individual has enough eloquent talent. So, when you officially go to propagate Buddha Dharma, there will be a scene of "Heaven's flowers are in chaos, earth's golden lotus is strong," meaning flowers from the sky fall, yellow lotuses grow on the ground. Only then will you be able to undertake the Buddha's mission of "continuing the wisdom life"!

This is called: "Master brings to the door, practice is up to each person." When I first learned Buddhism, no one taught me, no one encouraged me, and no one promoted or supported me. So I hope you will be self-reliant, keep moving forward and don't become dependent. If you have the mentality of relying on the Master for everything, you will never be liberated.

We study Buddha Dharma, that is, we learn true wisdom.

Once we have wisdom, we will solve all problems easily. No matter what job we do, we can do it completely satisfactorily. If we only use our conscious mind to solve problems, we will hesitate and lack the energy to make decisions. So no matter what we do, we absolutely cannot succeed.

To learn true wisdom, we must first cut off desire. How to stop lust? That means not fighting, not being greedy, not seeking, not being selfish, not taking personal advantage, not lying. These Six Great Sects are Dharma treasures to eliminate desire, allowing you to gain true wisdom. At that time, you will be as familiar with the dependent origination of all things as the back of your hand, and will be able to analyze very clearly. That way you can distinguish between right and wrong, good and evil, and absolutely do not do crazy things.

Lecture on June 24, 1985

tieu_de: Exploiting the Treasures of Self-Nature / 156 Music in Self-Nature /
tom_tat: All Chinese letters have meaning and are structured according to certain rules. Each word when formed has its own explanation. Chinese texts are structured in six ways such as: narrative, pictograms,...
noi_dung:
Exploiting the Treasures of Self-Nature / 156 Music in Self-Nature /

All Chinese letters have meaning and are structured according to certain rules. Each word when formed has its own explanation. Chinese writing is structured in six ways such as: indication, pictogram, image, sound, discussion, incantation and imitation.

Regarding Pictograms: like the word "horse" for horse ( ʼʳ has four legs, the word "loc" for deer ( ʼʳ has one dot above, and the word "yang" goat ( ʼ has two dots above, because the words deer and goat both represent horned species. The word "ox" for cattle ( ʼ has a commaʳ on the left, representing the personality of the buffalo species which is very strong and often butts to one side. So each word each has its own meaning, and we should also know more about the six ways of forming these words: Rites, music, archery, poetry, numbers. Confucius had three thousand students, but only seventy-two people were proficient in the six arts. Rites is music; archery is also martial arts; in ancient times, confucius refers to driving and driving machines flying, sailing... Poetry is a method of writing, generally divided into five ways of writing: trien, weeping, hailing, practicing, and writing. Numbers are arithmetic, so it is said: "Knowing a number, knowing a number," people now know how to create rockets and missiles, which were invented in the field of mathematics.

As far as music, Buddhist chanting belongs to music. Therefore, anyone who plays the flute in a rhythmic rhythm will have merit. If anyone knocks the gong with an angry mind, or knocks too loudly, or knocks too softly, it will be a sin. Praise is like using music to make offerings to Buddha. So if on the one hand you make offerings and on the other hand you get angry, do you think that Buddha will be happy? Using music to make offerings to Buddha has a lot of merit, but when you're angry, you can't praise it, and instead bang the bell and banging the bells wildly, that's a sin.

Practicing comes from every action in every aspect. There is no place that is not a place of practice. And it's not just meditating or bowing to Buddha that is practicing. Therefore, eating, wearing clothes, even every move, every movement is all practice. Practicing practice means subduing the body and mind. Body care is to prevent the body from getting sick and keep yourself healthy. But don't love it too much: you can't be cold, you can't be hot, you can't be thirsty, you can't be hungry, it's not too pampering your body. We have to work hard to control ourselves to train our bodies, as long as we don't harm it, that's enough. Not because we love our body like a fragile mirror that no one can touch.

In our daily activities, we should also train ourselves, that is practice. Walking, standing, lying down, sitting, there is never a time when I don't practice. Practicing practice does not mean that only two sessions of chanting, morning and evening, are practice. But in normal times, every move, every movement, every word, every action, we should all be in harmony with the rhythm, in accordance with the rules, because each of us has "music" in our nature. We must practice to have a peaceful mind, no afflictions, no causes, no ego and no ignorance. If we are jealous of talented people, or like to do unrealistic things, or boast about our talents to gain fame, then that is not music. If we practice the Dharma every day, that is music. Cultivate yourself to calm your mind and train your character, because we don't need to look for music outside. Because our minds are not at peace, we have to borrow outside music to balance ourselves. If our mind can be at peace, we will always be filled with good energy, and that is true "music". As for the six arts: ceremony, music, music, music, poetry, numbers; These six things are already included in our nature. If we can spend a whole day without saying useless words, without thinking about meaningless things, and can control our minds to be calm, peaceful, unbound, unattached to obstacles, without cause, without self, without right or wrong, then you say, if that is not music, then what is it?

When Confucius was in the state of Qi listening to Shao music, he did not know the taste of meat for three months. If you understand the music of your own nature, you don't need to talk about the smell of meat, you don't even know the smell of water, or whether it's sour, sweet, bitter, spicy, you don't even know. Then it is said that you have reached the realm of "seeing but not seeing, hearing but not hearing, eating but not knowing the taste." You should pay attention: Don't consider your own nature as a battlefield to fight, if that's the case then it's not music.

Lecture on July 16, 1985

tieu_de: Studying Buddhism Should Maintain Your Duty /
tom_tat: When preaching the Dharma, you should not praise that "The Venerable" is like that, like that. The thing I hate the most is people praising me. If someone criticizes me, I humbly accept it immediately, and use it as an example to enlighten...
noi_dung:
Studying Buddhism Should Maintain Your Duty /

When preaching the Dharma, you should not praise that "The Venerable" is like that, like that. The thing I hate the most is people praising me. If someone criticizes me, I humbly accept it immediately, and use it as an example to illuminate and reflect. I and emptiness are the same, both do not have the appearance of a self, the appearance of a human being, the appearance of sentient beings, and the appearance of a false life. If there was a self, I wouldn't have come to America. The reason I came to America was to open a new land for Buddhism, to spread Buddhism to the whole world!

Regardless of the circumstances, my policy is to absolutely never promote my own position, nor to be picky or eccentric. I don't feel that I am superior to others, or bigger than others. I don't have that way of thinking, because if I did, it would be a sign of complacency.

Anyone who is complacent will absolutely not achieve anything. People should have the thought "Existence is weak and non-existence, Truth is weak and nothingness" means existence is like nothingness, reality is like home. Even if we have noble morals, we are still as if we have nothing; Even though I am indeed talented, I still look like I have nothing. Please pay attention! “Complacent” is the nickname for that arrogance. Tu grand means "stinky" ( ʼ, meaning stinky, foul is a Chinese character, including the character ( ʼ located above the word dai (). When the foul smell of air rushes into the sky like that, who dares to come close to me? At that time, everyone has to cover their nose and pass by, not daring to come close to me!

I hope you use the Six Great Tong Zhi as principles. If you cannot do things like "not fighting, not being greedy, not seeking, not being selfish, not taking personal advantage, not lying," no matter how talented you are, how wise you are, or how fluently you speak like flowing water and how skillful you are in eloquence, it is still against the Dharma. Thus, no matter what you do, you will not achieve perfection.

I only recognize those who are honest and know how to keep themselves safe, not cunning people who often argue. From now on, no matter who they are, everyone must be honest and keep their duties. You must not be arrogant and think that you are extraordinary and that no one in the world can compare to you. Anyone who behaves like that will not last long in Buddhism, sooner or later he will fail.

Even if you are truly talented, you don't need to show it off. You should study the behavior of great virtuous people of the past, but focus on virtue. For everything, you should practice the Four Immeasurable Minds: love, compassion, joy, and equanimity. Don't harbor murderous intent in your heart and refuse to forgive people. We should understand that: "Compassion is the ambition, the door is the means." Today I want to tell you that much, whether you want to change it or not is up to you.

Lecture on July 30, 1985

Studying in the Spirit of Bodhisattva Maitreya

We should learn from Bodhisattva Maitreya's practice of patience. As He said:

The old fool wears a patched shirt,

Loose rice fills the stomach,

Patch your shirt to cover the cold,

Everything depends on fate.

Someone scolded the old fool,

The old fool only said good things.

Someone beat the old fool,

The old fool lay down to sleep.

Spit on his face,

Just let it dry on its own.

He did not waste his effort,

And people don't mind.

Such Paramita,

A magical treasure.

If anyone knows this,

Why worry about not achieving enlightenment?

You say, is that magical or not? That's why His mouth often smiles and his belly is big, called: "If the mind is spacious, the body is fat," without afflictions.

The name of Bodhisattva Maitreya is Amitabha. Maitreya is translated as Tu Thi, A Dat Da is translated as Vo Nang Thang.

Why is it called Infinite Thang? Someone said: "I know, because this Bodhisattva eats more than anyone else. Otherwise, how could his belly be so big? Because no one has a belly as big as him, that's why it's called Infinite Victory."

Others said: "This Bodhisattva has great strength, with one hand he can push over a large mountain. Because there is no one equal to him, that is why he is called Incompetent Victor." If you say so, it is not correct. So what is Infinite Victory? He is a person who practices the Six Paramitas method to the edge of the sea and no one can win more than him, so he is called Infinite Victor.

This Bodhisattva often carries a large sack on his shoulder. He went everywhere to beg for grace from everyone. What do you ask for? He created the conditions to ask for afflictions, hoping that everyone in the world would be free from afflictions so that they could leave suffering and be happy. That's why it is said: "Opening your mouth means laughing, laughing at laughable people in the world; having a big belly to hold, containing what people can hardly contain." He and the burlap sack were never apart, so he was nicknamed Venerable Bo Dai, called:

"Walk with Bo Dai, sit with Bo Dai, put down Bo Dai, how free!"

Therefore we should study His thoughts and behavior.

Lecture on July 25, 1985

tieu_de: Learning According to the Spirit of Bodhisattva Maitreya / 164 What Causes the Three Disasters? /
tom_tat: Tam tai is divided into two parts: major tam tai and minor tam tai. The great three disasters are three great disasters of fire, water and wind. The three minor disasters are the three minor disasters of war, crop failure and epidemics. That also means disaster. In a great…
noi_dung:
Learning According to the Spirit of Bodhisattva Maitreya / 164 What Causes the Three Disasters? /

Tam tai is divided into two parts: major tam tai and minor tam tai. The great three disasters are three great disasters of fire, water and wind. The three minor disasters are the three minor disasters of war, crop failure and epidemics. That also means disaster. In a great kalpa, there are four intermediate kalpas: formation, abiding, destruction, and emptiness. Each middle kalpa has twenty small kalpas. At the end of the reduction period of each kalpa, the phenomenon of minor three disasters arises. The three great disasters arise during the destruction period of each great kalpa. Now let's discuss the cause of the great three disasters.

Because people have greedy minds, fire disasters arise; When people have anger in mind, water disasters arise; People with stupid minds are born with bad luck. Therefore, the three disasters arise from the three poisons. In our minds, everyone has all three poisons. This mind expands more and more every day and when it reaches a certain level, it will form a great disaster.

The three disasters that arise also have layers, because humans have seven emotions: joy, anger, love, attachment, love, hatred, desire, that is, joy, anger, sadness, fear, love, hate, and desire. These seven types of emotions gradually develop and expand. And each type of love will cause a disaster, so seven fire disasters will form. After seven fire disasters, there will be one water disaster. Of the seven emotions, each emotion is divided into seven, so each of these "seven fires and one water" will be repeated seven times in order. Then went through seven disasters. At the end of the day, a disaster occurs and destroys the entire world.

When a fire disaster occurs, it can burn all the way to the First Heaven

meditation of the Form Realm, which includes the realms: Brahma Heaven, Brahma Heaven and Great Brahma Heaven.

When a water disaster occurs, it can flood the Second Meditation heaven of the Form Realm, which includes the Heaven of Little Light, the Heaven of Infinite Light and the Heaven of Light and Sound. When a wind disaster arises, it can blow to the heavens of the Three Meditations of the Form Realm, which includes the Lesser Pure Heaven, the Infinite Pure Heaven and the Variable Pure Heaven. So say:

The Heaven of the Six Desires has five declines, the Heaven of the Three Meditations has wind and disaster, Even if one cultivates to Phi Phi Thought, it is not as good as going to the West and then coming back.

Where does wind come from? It comes from the synthesis of seven emotions: joy, anger, guilt, attachment, love, hatred, and desire. Phong tai symbolizes ignorance and poison. When people fall into a state of ignorance, they forget everything. Therefore, a great wind arose, then from the heavens of the Third Zen to the depths of hell, nothing remained, everything was swept away. Even if a fire disaster, water disaster or wind disaster arises, the inner courtyard of the Tusita heaven of the Desire Realm still exists, not affected in the slightest. Why so? Because that is the Pure Land of Buddha and Bodhisattva. Currently, Bodhisattva Maitreya is residing in the inner courtyard in the Tusita heaven, waiting until the tenth kalpa of the Hien Kiep period, before he descends to the Saha world to teach sentient beings (currently in the cessation of the ninth kalpa).

Greed, anger and ignorance form many types of evil energy, like atoms in an atomic bomb; Atoms are terrifying substances, but the atomic bombs that we ourselves create from the fire of samadhi are even more terrifying. This type of atom does not come from the outside, but is inherent in its own nature. The true fire samadhi in our nature is inherently positive, but because we abuse it, it turns into the fire of desire. In the human body there are three fire elements: upper fire, middle fire and lower fire. This fire can form a disaster, or turn into an atomic bomb to destroy everything. Because there are atomic bombs inside, there are atomic bombs outside. They are formed by correspondence and continuity with each other. Many problems in the world today are also from this point.

If there is something in the mind, there is something outside. If there is no war in our hearts, there will be no war outside either. That's why it is said that "all is created by the mind".

Lecture on July 29, 1985

tieu_de: Illness and Karma /
tom_tat: All incurable and poisonous diseases such as malaria, cancer... are controlled by demons from behind, causing the five internal organs in the human body to be out of position, and the four elements to be out of harmony. It's all due to evil karma. By…
noi_dung:
Illness and Karma /

All incurable and poisonous diseases such as malaria, cancer... are controlled by demons from behind, causing the five internal organs in the human body to be out of position, and the four elements to be out of harmony. It's all due to evil karma. Because people have bad karma for a long time, when the time comes, the devil comes to collect the debt. And it's also because humans don't have enough yang energy, that is, yin and yang weaken, so ghosts can act haphazardly. If you are usually free from afflictions and wisdom is always present, there will be no loopholes for the devil to take advantage of. But once you initiate desire and ignorance, the devil takes the opportunity to easily sneak in.

From that, it can be deduced that eighty-four thousand diseases all have causes and consequences. Even when you are bitten by a mosquito, stung by a bee, and all the accidents you encounter are all woven together by cause and effect. People who clearly understand this principle will not dare to make even the slightest mistake, because if they make a mistake, they will have to pay for it. Especially those who practice the Six Degrees of Van Hanh, they must be even more sincere in their efforts, without the slightest trace of false pride. That's why it is said: "If the cause is not true, the result is false." If you sow dishonest causes, you will reap crooked results. And by the time the fruit is achieved, there are a lot of troubles.

Therefore, you should "eliminate old karma according to conditions, do not create new karma" and must not have the slightest bit of indolence in all actions. Regardless of time or place, everyone should be vigilant. If we don't harm others and only benefit others, then we won't get sick at all, and the devil won't be able to find us.

Speaking of demons, yesterday an "enlightened" demon from San Jose came to find me. That demon possessed a woman and she thought she was enlightened. Her husband also thought she was enlightened. But she said: "People do not need to practice, nor do they need to keep the precepts."

Actually, her purpose was to find me to fight. This lady took refuge with me in 1980 at the Lay Buddhist Association in Singapore. She came to America for a few years, learned to meditate, and then considered herself enlightened. As soon as she entered, she immediately bowed her head to me, but did not let her husband and children see. She was the only one who bowed to me. At first nothing happened, but when she bowed her head for the third time, she continued to bow again and again, then began to cry, the more she cried, the louder she became.

I asked: What are you crying for?

She replied: I don't know, it's not me crying, but someone else outside is crying.

Who told her to bow her head like that?

It's because I want to bow.

What are you playing at?

Don't know! In short, there is no need to practice, no need to study, no need to keep the precepts.

She is a university graduate in Indonesia. Is it true that she did not need to study to graduate?

Not!

Cultivation is the same. Even at the door, she couldn't even enter, so if she didn't practice, how could she attain enlightenment? Is it true that you can read and write without going to school?

This time, her demon had to tell the truth. It is a “natural” demon from the Luc Duc heaven. It originally wanted to fight with me, but when it came here, there was no way to fight. So it used a hidden trick, using soft and magical methods to attack! It cried and spit poison, but the poison had no effect. After that, I talked to that demon until it reached its wits' end, then it truly went down to earth. At that time, the Buddhist lady also woke up and was no longer in a commotion.

Lecture on July 30, 1985

Cannot be compared between

tieu_de: There Can Be No Comparison Between Ghosts And Buddha /
tom_tat: During the Ming Dynasty, Great Master Lien Tri (1535-1615) after becoming a monk, went everywhere to find a master to study the religion. After entering the capital, he went to pay his respects to two great and virtuous elders in Zen Buddhism, Nhan Dung and Tieu...
noi_dung:
There Can Be No Comparison Between Ghosts And Buddha /

Ghost With Buddha

During the Ming Dynasty, Great Master Lien Tri (1535-1615) after becoming a monk, went everywhere to find a master to study the religion. After entering the capital, he went to pay his respects to two great and virtuous elders in Zen Buddhism, namely Nhan Dung and Tieu Nham. Master Lien Tri, after receiving instructions from the two teachers, went to Dong Xuong and when he heard the sound of the drums, he suddenly became enlightened. On that occasion, He wrote a verse:

Two decades of suspicious history,

The Three Thousand Reasons meet strangely!

The fragrance is as stimulating as a dream,

Demon Buddha does not fight evil and evil.

Mean:

Doubts from twenty years ago How strange is the realization thousands of miles away! Burn incense and throw halberds like in a dream of a Demon Buddha, right and left are in vain.

Regardless of whether we read the Sutras or read the Abhidharma, we must use wisdom to distinguish right from wrong. The taboo is that we use our mind, thoughts and consciousness to speculate. Because the mind, mind and consciousness are just to deceive people. These three things have great enchantment, making people unable to distinguish between right and wrong, reasoning is not clear, black and white are mixed up, creating unclear chaos. There are some theories that, at first hearing, seem to make sense, but as soon as a wise person looks at them, they know they are not correct, while an unwise person is deceived and listens with pleasure. There are others who are like the blind leading the blind, not because of intention, but because they themselves do not understand clearly. So they push others astray down the wrong path, and in the end they don't get to a good place. Therefore, we should not underestimate expressing our opinions. If we interpret the fundamental issue incorrectly, it will be like the saying: "A difference of a dime or an inch will make a difference of heaven and earth," even causing the whole world to fall into a dark, lightless situation. Therefore, based on theoretical principles, we must have accurate and clear perception. If we only rely on the heart, mind, and consciousness to speculate, then criticize haphazardly and arbitrarily praise and criticize, that means leaving Buddha to join the demons, which is impossible.

As we talk about the issue of ghosts and Buddhas, we should not follow nonsense arguments. For example, there are some people who think: "Devil and Buddha are like one, two but not two." But Buddhists are not like demons; If it's the same, then people don't need to believe in Buddha, they can just believe in the devil's crazy words! Some people say: "Demons are the dark side of wise men who come to help us." That is originally talking about the ambition of compassion, and is also a way of speaking to comfort the ego, using the psychology of comforting a child to tell him not to be too angry. Such a way of speaking is still to resolve internal conflicts and resentments, because we do not want to see the devil as an enemy. If the devil's dark side is said to be helping people, but he continuously devours people alive, or puts people to death, is that called "helping"?

Therefore, we need to maintain our basic stance,

Always maintain mindfulness at all times. Once we give rise to greed, or greed for quickness, greed for magical powers, greed for quick results, greed for premonitions, then demons will immediately enter. There are some people who are very smart, but why do they sometimes have evil spirits? That's because they don't have a clear understanding of the basic principles. If they understand the basics clearly, the demon's spell will not be effective. We don't need to recite mantras, but just don't fight, don't be greedy, don't seek, don't be selfish, don't seek personal gain, and don't lie, then demons will have no way to enter.

After many years of studying Buddhism, I concluded that these "Six Great Teachings" are the most useful. Buddha Dharma is not a far-reaching, vast discussion or magical, strange talk. It's also not about guessing nonsense about misfortunes and blessings, or divining bad luck or bad luck. I don't know how many people in this world know how to predict and predict like that. But that is a trick of gangsters who like to talk about magical powers, using mythical demonic words to mesmerize the people. That's what they're trying to sell. And it is true that those people can know the past and future. For example, they say to you: "I know someone will come to visit you tomorrow, and that person will tell you like this, like this..." Or like: "I know everything you have done before..." But they all have a mistake: they cannot stop being lustful, or greedy for money, or attached to sex. Those are all ghostly realms. If someone has a competitive mind, a greedy mind, seeks fame and profit, or spreads propaganda to promote himself so that others can worship him, is also selfish and does not speak the truth, then we should know that this person is in the realm of demons.

On the occasion of Great Master Lien Tri paying his respects to two old masters Vang Dung and Tieu Nham, the Great Master was advised by them: "People who become monks practice the religion for the sake of life and death. Don't let fame and profit get in the way!" At that time, at that ashram, there were also a number of people participating in the study, but not many people paid any attention to this declaration. Only Great Master Lien Tri understood the profound meaning and filled his mind with excitement. Therefore, when leaving Sutra to Dong Xuong, the Great Master suddenly became enlightened and wrote the above verse. Actually, those four verses are only secondary. The most important words are not to seek fame and fortune, that is the main key to this story.

Don't think that Great Master Lien Tri came to Dong Xuong to become enlightened. But from the very beginning, the Great Master has walked step by step on the path of enlightenment. When he was standing in front of the two Elder Masters, Transformation Dung and Tieu Nham, they shouted loudly at his head, causing the Great Master to suddenly have a great enlightenment. After becoming a monk, do not be passionate about fame and fortune. That is the most effective mantra that can defeat all demons. Let's look at the text of the verse as follows:

Suspicion from twenty years ago. This great matter of life and death has long confused and confused Master Lien Tri. Because he did not understand, the Great Master had to go abroad to consult and ask the wise man to resolve his doubts.

How strange is the realization thousands of miles away. After three thousand miles, the Great Master arrived at Dong Xuong and suddenly became enlightened. How wonderful this is! All of the Great Master's attachments suddenly disappeared!

Burn incense and throw halberds like a dream. Burning incense to worship Buddha is a good thing, while throwing knives and fighting with demons is bad. “Dismissal” can also mean throwing away weapons, meaning not fighting anymore. All of that is just like a dream! Why is it like a dream? Because I don't fully understand it yet.

Demon Buddha, right and wrong are in vain. Now the Great Master understands. In the past, because the Great Master kept spending his efforts on false thoughts, right and wrong, it was all a waste of effort! Master Lien Tri also did not say: Buddha and Demon are one. A ghost is a ghost, Buddha is Buddha. Since both sides are not in a relationship with each other, there will be arguments and disputes, what is right and wrong worth arguing about? The previous discussions of right and wrong were all illusory, not real. If you want to subdue demons, you must have a little sincere practice. You can't do it just by meditating through your mouth.

There is another way: "Without demons, Buddha cannot appear, without Buddha, demons cannot appear." Without Demons, Buddha would not appear, without Buddha, Demons would not appear. Demons and Buddhas are also relative to each other. It is not true that when Buddha became enlightened, Demons and Buddhas were one and the same. After Buddha's enlightenment, during the Demonic period, Buddha remained the same as before, except that Buddha did not have hostile thoughts. Buddha considered all living beings equal and Demons were also a part of living beings, so Buddha considered Demons equal. But is Demon equal to Buddha? Absolutely not! Because Ma always wanted to overthrow Buddha.

After twenty years, Master Lien Tri clearly understood the principle of not fighting. The Great Master realized that before he had only argued about right and wrong on the surface in vain. At that time, the Great Master did not reflect back the light and did not clean up his own nature, so whenever people fought with him, the Great Master would be troubled.

I say the principle is very simple, I hope you will think carefully. Because in principle, we cannot make mistakes. You are all still young, and you should not arbitrarily say "Devil Buddha is one." Or people who have reached great enlightenment and enlightenment can say that, because their level of understanding is not the same as yours. But we are still children, so we must not lie and borrow the principles of the ancients and then forcefully interpret them in a wrong way. For example, if a child does not know how to drive, if you let him or her drive, it is very easy to cause an accident, up to the point of losing your life.

There are some people who, when they hear "Devil Buddha One Like" they think: "Then why do I bow to Buddha? If I do demon karma, isn't it Buddhist karma?" Therefore, on the principle of discrimination, we must understand clearly, not listen in such a confused way, then think that fish eyes are pearls.

Lecture on August 29, 1985

Why Buddha

tieu_de: Why Did the Buddha Shine When He Preached the Dharma? /
tom_tat: When preaching, the Buddha often released halos. Why is that? Because He wants sentient beings to quickly become enlightened. When the Buddha preached the Nirvana Sutra at the end, he emitted light from his face, then gathered it back into...
noi_dung:
Why Did the Buddha Shine When He Preached the Dharma? /

When preaching, the Buddha often released halos. Why is that? Because He wants sentient beings to quickly become enlightened. When the Buddha preached the Nirvana Sutra at the end, he emitted light from his face, then collected it back into his mouth. That is the expression that going is also the same, coming is also the same. Going is also going to the treasure of bright wisdom, returning is still returning to the treasure of bright wisdom. But sentient beings only know how to walk but do not know how to return, which is called: "The energy released cannot be collected." That also means talking about our delusions. If you can release it, then you must know how to take it back. If you can only release light, but cannot collect it back, you will not be able to walk as freely as possible. That's called learning without knowing how to use it. We should be able to release and then we can gather, what can be big and what can be small, what can be and what can be not, there is nothing that we cannot do, depending on our mind as we wish, free and without hindrance.

Buddha releases light just to let people see, right? Not! So why did He release the halo to the viewers? Are you like us mortals who want to do advertising? Or because he wants to show off his special forte to let people know? There is no such thing. Buddha releases light because he wants to destroy the ignorance of sentient beings. The Buddha's aura shines through each living being in the Dharma assembly, called: "Buddha's light shines universally, the Buddha's light shines everywhere," meaning the Buddha radiates his aura everywhere like nectar rain, watering everything evenly. At that time, all sentient beings were blessed by the Buddha's halo, meaning they were sowing the seeds to become Buddhas and would definitely become Buddhas in the future. The Buddha releases light just because he wants sentient beings to become Buddhas, wants sentient beings to be devoted to their karma, to make sentient beings' minds enlightened, to have full wisdom so that they don't have to spend the whole day from morning to night being ignorant, without wisdom, and then just stay in the sea of ​​suffering moving back and forth. Therefore, at the end of his life, the Buddha shined his halo on all living beings participating in the Dharma Assembly, causing them to have the opportunity to become Buddhas in the future.

Then the Buddha regained his aura, which was to return to his essence. That also wants to teach people not to brag but to know how to hide the traces of their light, not to reveal their light too much. If someone reveals his talent in such an obvious way, it is an act of ignorance. So is it wise to intentionally hide one's own aura? That's not the case either. This means we use it when we should use it, and when we shouldn't use it, we don't use it. For example, if you spend money wastefully, no matter how much money you have, it will run out. Even though you are a bit poor, if you only consume a little, you will still have money to spend.

Why do people have to hide their traces? An oil lamp can be used as an example. Oil lamps emit light, but if we use them often, the oil will dry up, and the wick will burn out. But if we burn it when we need it, if we don't burn it when we don't need it, then we will use it for a long time. The same is true of human wisdom. Buddha can release light every day. Why does He release and then pull back in? That is teaching people to know how to move forward and know how to retreat, know how to move and know how to stay still, know how to follow and know how to stop. Who can know when enough is always enough? That's why it is said: "If you know how to be content, don't be humiliated, if you know how to be content, don't be insulted." If you know enough, you won't be humiliated, if you know how to stop, you won't be in danger. If you know you shouldn't do something, then don't do it. That's knowing how to stop. If someone can do that, then they can be said to understand Buddha Light. If we can't do that, it's like an ant that wants to eat a watermelon but it keeps crawling on the skin. Even though it feels sweet, in the end it can't be eaten. Think about this principle and you will understand.

Lecture on October 1, 1985

tieu_de: Dong Tinh Nhat Nhu /
tom_tat: At the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, we only experience suffering. Even though we experience suffering, we can also eliminate our sinful karma. Because for countless lifetimes, we have had many obstacles, so we spend all day worrying about troubles and worries...
noi_dung:
Dong Tinh Nhat Nhu /

At the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, we only experience suffering. Even though we experience suffering, we can also eliminate our sinful karma. Because for countless lifetimes, we have had many obstacles, so we spend all day worrying, arguing, arguing, and never have peace in our hearts. If you come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas and can endure a little suffering, that is called cultivating external energy. Once you have the external work, then you will have the internal result. If you don't have the external effort, the internal result will not be achieved. Outside work is doing virtuous deeds in the cave, cultivating blessings. The inner result is cultivating wisdom in stillness.

You need to train movement and stillness to achieve oneness, called: "Movement does not hinder stillness, stillness does not hinder movement; movement is stillness, stillness is movement; movement and stillness are not two." Once you practice this practice and gather it into a block, concentration will appear.

Surangama Dai Dinh does not mean that we only need to meditate. When you walk, stand, lie down, or sit without being moved by the outside world, without being moved by the external environment, and without being disturbed by false thoughts, that is concentration. If you sit there and keep thinking wildly, if you don't think east then think west, then you don't have concentration. Or if you see a realm and are immediately shaken by that realm, that is not having the power of concentration. Concentration is the incomparable movement and stillness. When we move, we are not moved by the realm, that is stillness. When we are still and not disturbed by false thoughts, that is also movement. If you practice the same movements and movements, your practice will become one. Once the practice has become a whole, it is neither dynamic, nor static, nor empty, nor cou, that is the Middle Way.

Lecture on October 12, 1985

tieu_de: Why is the World Decaying? /
tom_tat: Although the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is in the world, it can be said that it is separate from the outside world. Because people in the world like to enjoy things, like if they don't smoke, they drink alcohol. Men and women greedily indulge in lust, dancing,...
noi_dung:
Why is the World Decaying? /

Although the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is in the world, it can be said that it is separate from the outside world. Because people in the world like to enjoy things, like if they don't smoke, they drink alcohol. Men and women indulge in lustful pleasures, dancing, smoking, etc. There's nothing they won't do. But in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, there are no such bad habits. It can be said that this is a pure ashram, a place completely different from the world. Although the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas opens universities, high schools and elementary schools, we only focus on quality, not quantity. Everyone must follow the rules and order, so they can live in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. If anyone does not follow the rules, they absolutely cannot live together. And the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas did not need to chase them away, but they themselves felt unable to live. Therefore, people living in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas are like panning sand to find gold, looking for honest people among all humanity in the world.

Those who come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must first of all not fight, not be greedy, not seek, not be selfish, not take personal advantage, and not lie. Only then are people qualified to reside in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. If they still do not change their bad habits, then even if they are God or the Emperor, they will not be accepted. Even if the President comes here, if he doesn't follow the rules, he won't be accepted. The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas does not distinguish between poor, rich, or high or low. But everyone is equal, obeying together, not fighting, not being greedy, not seeking, not being selfish, not taking personal advantage, not lying. Who can keep these six conditions?

considered a good person.

Why is this world degenerate? Because of paintings. Fighting with yourself is to let the tiger fire (evil) anger and the fire of ignorance run out. People compete with people, families compete with families, and on a larger scale, countries compete with countries. Even today, the Earth is having conflicts with the Moon. Therefore, the word painting will harm people. But even after death, people still cannot understand this realm. The next thing is greed. The vast majority of revolutionaries in this world are motivated by greed. Because they are greedy for fame and profit, they commit murder and go beyond their authority to gain positions. They are greedy without getting bored. Therefore, they make the world more and more chaotic and more and more different every day.

The third bad habit is to seek, to seek profit and fame, to seek boys and girls. People are all searching, so they cannot settle down. When they don't get what they want, they worry, but when they get it, they worry about losing it. Bridges can also kill people. Praying to death but not knowing why I died.

The fourth is a selfish person, a person who does not have the thought of great meritorious care, and does not have the spirit of sacrificing oneself for others. Always put yourself first. Why do people have to be selfish? Because you want your own benefit, that is the fifth bad habit; Going further, they ignore tricks, do not speak words of faith, and speak false words to deceive people, so they commit the sixth bad habit of lying. Therefore, people who study Buddhism should take these six conditions to examine themselves every day and use them as rules for their practice.

Lecture on October 15, 1985

Layman Thuan Da Offers

Today everyone promotes the meaning of the text of the Nirvana Sutra which is very clear, precise and very reasonable. Each individual has unique insight and unique wisdom. The reason I tell you all to go up to the podium to preach the sutras first is because I want to train you to have the talent to preach the sutras and experience in propagating the dharma. There are two very similar sentences in the passage:

Mr. Thuan Da made an offering and the Buddha was of course the recipient. Some people thought to themselves: "Buddha must have been hungry so he accepted Mr. Thuan Da's offerings." Because Thuan Da was a working-class worker, but he was willing to give all his food to make offerings to Buddha, called "Self-giving and altruism," sacrificing himself for others. We can infer to know that Mr. Thuan Da had no more food to eat. So is he hungry? That's not it. Because he had received the Dharma Food, it was said: "Meditating on food, Dharma joy is abundant."

On the surface, Mr. Thuan Da seems to be arguing with the Buddha, but in reality, it is not an argument. Because Mr. Thuan Da had a very small mind, he did not understand the teachings of Buddha, so he said: "That's not true."

Lecture on October 29, 1985

Conversation with a Catholic Nun

Interlocutors: Venerable Master Tuyen Hoa, American and Chinese nuns, and nuns Heng Tri, Heng Dao, and Heng Giai in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.

Time: October 31, 1985

Location: Kim Son Pagoda, San Francisco, California, USA

Sister Hang Dao: We have just studied with the Sisters about how to establish a very successful school system in the past in Christianity, along with the strict regime of Priests and monastic Sisters. Based on the last twenty years, many Priests and Nuns have left the tradition of monasticism, and today many Sisters live alone.

Venerable Master: No matter what is good, there is also bad, success and failure. But I know that in Buddhism, if Bhikkhus or Bhikkhunis live alone, it is very easy to break the precepts. And the precept of sexual immorality is the precept that is most easily violated. In addition, they can also violate other precepts such as stealing, lying, drinking alcohol, and even killing, they can also violate them, so they can easily fall into the wrong path. Unless people have solid, immutable concentration like Vajra, then it's a different story. But in the world, how many people can practice and attain Vajra Dharma? People are still people, most of them are guided by the five desires to go down the wrong path. Therefore, a person who cultivates a solitary life without violating the precepts is truly as rare as phoenix feathers and unicorn horns! Sister Hang Tri: The Sisters just explained that the reason they want to live alone is because they do not admire the leaders and elders.

Venerable Master: If they do not trust their elders, then they should find someone worthy of respect so that they can rely on them. If we don't take care of maintaining traditions and rules, I'm afraid that twenty years from now there will no longer be anyone who believes in Christianity.

American Sister: Your suggestion is to find an elder worthy of our admiration. Nun Hang Tri: How should we maintain a strong Buddhist regime? Currently, many Westerners have converted their faith to Buddhism. Because the monastic system of Western religions is increasingly collapsing, such as Christianity, for example, there are people who change their faith.

Because of the discerning eyes of the public, over time his true identity will be revealed, and everyone will lose trust in that person. Another point is that in Buddhism, true practitioners do not hoard private wealth.

American Sister: The principles you speak of are very similar to Christianity in its early stages of development in the United States. When we joined the Church, we were full of enthusiasm and lofty ambitions. American Sister: The doctrine you just preached is similar to the thinking of missionaries traveling in Asia in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Nun Hang Tri: (Interrupting to correct) That's not true.

Chinese nun: We also have the same concept. It's just that in our minds we often ponder: Is God within us or outside of us?

Venerable Master: You should use your wisdom to answer my question, don't be vague, don't talk around things, don't make excuses. Our words need to be consistent with logic and be able to withstand any test.

Chinese Sister: I don't have a bit of wisdom, I just want to bring the teachings out for reference.

Venerable Master: Why don't you have wisdom? If you learn to follow God, you should learn God's wisdom. God should have given you wisdom! Why does God show favoritism and not give wisdom to Sister?

Chinese nun: (Laughs) Please don't discuss whether I am wise or not...

Lecture on November 7, 1985

Why Did Buddha Not Accept Offerings Before Entering Nirvana?

When Buddha was about to enter Nirvana, why did he not accept offerings? Because the Buddha had attained an indestructible diamond body, he did not eat or drink. Whether you eat or not eat has nothing to do with Him, that is, you can eat or not eat. It's not like us, if we miss a meal, we suffer as if we were lacking a lot. Even if I don't eat enough, I feel like I've lost a lot of capital. There is a famous saying in Zen Buddhism: "I have eaten all day, but have not eaten a grain of rice. I have worn clothes all day, but have not worn a single thread of silk." Is this statement a lie? If we analyze carefully, we will see that it makes a lot of sense. Although that person eats and wears clothes, his mind is not there. Then where is his mind? His mind was chanting, single-mindedly studying the first meditation. It wasn't until "the water dried up that the rocks were exposed" that he did not relax. Thus, he engraved the deadline for evidence as a goal.

Buddha Shakyamuni said: "After I received a bowl of milk porridge from the female shepherd, I went to the Bodhi tree to practice and attain Perfect Enlightenment." After drinking the bowl of milk porridge, his body was restored and healthy again. But if He doesn't eat, that's okay. When Buddha was in the Snow Mountains practicing asceticism for six years, that place was not in the Himalayas, but in the region south of the Ganges River. Every day Buddha only ate one sesame seed or one grain of barley and still did not starve to death. Although he was as thin as a stick, his spirit was still very healthy. That's why it's said that the Buddha can eat, or not eat, and doesn't have anything

What's the problem?

Because it was okay for the Buddha to eat or not, before entering nirvana, he received the last offering from Mr. Thuan Da. His purpose is to think of the masses. What is for the masses? How can He eat on behalf of the masses? As the saying goes: "If you eat by yourself, you will be full, if you eat and die by yourself, you will end it yourself." In other words, the Buddha accepted Mr. Thuan Da's last offering for the sake of the assembly. He accepts offerings also for us, for you and all sentient beings today. Why say like that? Because the Buddha compassionately helps sentient beings to plant a little root of blessings. If Buddha did not eat and drink, we living beings would have no place to sow blessings. Buddha planted merit fields for sentient beings, so he did not eat but ate, ate but did not eat. If Buddha did not eat, sentient beings would have no place to plant merit fields, and Buddha's disciples would also have no food to eat.

Buddha accepts offerings entirely for his disciples, called:

"Even though a Nelong is unable to cast rain, if a dragon is unable to rain, it will be a fake dragon. Even if an ordinary monk can't give blessings, if a monk can pray for blessings, he will be a fake monk," meaning that although an earth dragon cannot make rain, if he wants to pray for rain, he must use a fake dragon. Although ordinary monks cannot grow blessings, if they want to seek blessings, they must rely on ordinary monks. That is mutual support, not superstition. Because of responding to the fate of living beings, the Buddha reluctantly accepted the offerings, not thinking that the Buddha was contradictory, eating and then saying not to eat. We must understand this clearly, because this is also to destroy human attachments.

Even though layperson Thuan Da was an employee, he made offerings with a sincere and passionate heart, without any intention. That's why Buddha accepted his offerings. He told himself that he had poor roots (without the Three Jewels), so he hoped the Buddha would eliminate that same root. Because his sole purpose is to sow good roots for sentient beings, not for himself. That is the spirit of Bodhisattva.

We humans should not be afraid of extreme poverty. Because poverty cannot hinder the path of religion, it is only afraid of demons. Root demon means wrong knowledge and wrong views. If a person has wrong knowledge and wrong views, no matter what method they practice, they will absolutely never have the correspondence. No matter what abilities they have, it's like talking about food but not eating it, counting money for others, being busy for others but not getting any benefit for themselves.

Layman Thuan Da did things that others could not do, and gave in to what others could not give, so he did not compete with anyone. When everyone had finished making offerings, he made offerings. Absolutely, he did not compete with anyone. I believe the time he waited was very long. Furthermore, he ate what others could not eat, and endured what others could not endure. Therefore, he is the dragon statue among all people. Because Mr. Thuan Da had the two words "sincere," the Buddha accepted his offerings. Why did Mr. Thuan Da have that fate? Because of his past life, he cultivated merit, cultivated wisdom, cultivated religion, and cultivated virtue. Because of his many merits of practice, in this life he was able to be a perfect almsgiver.

Lecture on November 8, 1985

tieu_de: Great Opportunity at the End of Dharma / 204 Why Did Buddha Not Accept Offerings Before Entering Nirvana / 207 Wanting to Become a Buddha Must Be Destroyed by Demons /
tom_tat: The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is where the Saints practice the Way, so the devil comes to disturb the pure minds of those who practice the Way. Because he wanted to defeat the Saints and monopolize one area, the Demon King caused trouble everywhere so that the Saints...
noi_dung:
Great Opportunity at the End of Dharma / 204 Why Did Buddha Not Accept Offerings Before Entering Nirvana / 207 Wanting to Become a Buddha Must Be Destroyed by Demons /

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is where the Saints practice the Way, so the devil comes to disturb the pure minds of those who practice the Way. Because he wanted to defeat the Saints and monopolize one area, the Demon King caused trouble everywhere so that the Saints had to surrender and kneel down to confess. You should be patient, do not give up and absolutely do not raise the white flag of surrender. You must strive until the end and the ultimate victory will be yours. That's why it is said: "If you want to become a Buddha, you will be destroyed by demons. If you want to be a good person, you will find yourself in hardship." Those who do not have enough virtue will drift with the wind and then fall into ruin. A person with enough virtue will not be swayed by the devil. Why so? Because they have had deep roots in practice for life after life, they are not afraid of any ghost.

The bad habit that we often commit is liking to be praised and flattered. Like when someone compliments me just one sentence, I feel light-headed and enchanted. So how can one become a Buddha? I myself don't know, I don't know. If we can keep the precepts and practice concentration, we will have wisdom. When we have wisdom, we will not be moved by praise, criticism or slander. If someone slanders me, I don't feel angry at all; If someone compliments me, my heart is not at all happy. In fact, praise, criticism or slander are just the winds of the world, called "The eight winds that blow without moving." Why are they called eight winds and eight winds? These are confession, pain, suffering, pleasure, benefit, decline, destruction, anticipation; that is: praise, criticism, suffering, joy, gain, weakness, slander and honor. If your mind is shaken by these eight winds, it means you do not have a solid foundation. What is called a foundation? That is virtue.
