People who are not virtuous have a very hot temper, and their ignorance is also very heavy. A virtuous person will not be angry, and can transform ignorance into wisdom. Therefore, when we practice, we must focus on cultivating virtue.

People who study Buddhism must pay attention to virtue and not do unvirtuous things, because that is the truth of practice. If we want to eliminate karma, we must make offerings. Because making offerings can bring blessings and wisdom, we must practice religion and virtue. Otherwise, even if we practice the Six Virtues, it will have no effect. The Six Paramitas were established so that we can specialize in cultivating religion and virtue. If a practitioner does not pay attention to morality, he will create karma!

Lecture on November 9, 1985

tieu_de: Bodhisattva's Thoughts /
tom_tat: Why does the public praise Mr. Thuan Da? Because he works honestly, not avoiding work to pray for peace. No matter what he did, he did it sincerely and did not lie to others. Because whatever he does is complete and thorough...
noi_dung:
Bodhisattva's Thoughts /

Why does the public praise Mr. Thuan Da? Because he works honestly, not avoiding work to pray for peace. No matter what he did, he did it sincerely and did not lie to others. Because everything he did was complete and thoughtful, everyone praised him.

Layman Thuan Da is an employee, wherever he goes he works for others. People hired him for one coin, but his work was worth twice as much as what they hired him for. This is called consummation. For example, most workers arrive at work at eight o'clock in the morning, and he arrives at work at six o'clock in the morning. So he worked two hours more than others. At five o'clock in the afternoon, he stopped working, but at seven o'clock he left the factory, meaning he worked two more hours. I believe that your working situation is similar. If it is not so, how can you be praised?

Thuan Da is an honest worker, he is only afraid of making mistakes with people, not afraid that people will not be reasonable with him. He always reflects back, blames himself and finds his own shortcomings, rather than blaming heaven and blaming others. He always thought other people were right, and he was wrong. Because he had such thoughts, he was praised by people.

Why is Mr. Thuan Da pure? Because he did not have the three poisons of greed, anger, and ignorance, over time he became completely pure. Furthermore, diligently cultivating Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom, and stopping greed, anger, and ignorance are also the secrets of practitioners. Each of us has advantages and disadvantages, so we should use our advantages to compensate for our shortcomings. Only then is it compatible with the middle path.

Layman Thuan Da certainly worked wholeheartedly for the people, just like the saying "serve the people." His service attitude is very good, very enthusiastic and not fake. He did everything quickly and charged cheap wages, making everyone satisfied. If at that time you had improper intentions in your mind, you would not be pure. In other words, whenever there is intention or greed, it is impure. As for Mr. Thuan Da, he does not have such thoughts. He always devoted himself to duty, volunteering to serve people without anyone knowing. That is the Bodhisattva's thought. Because Bodhisattvas sometimes appear in the working class like that. Mr. Thuan Da has merit because he did not let others know, did not let people see what he did, so he was completely pure. Everyone, please reflect for a moment. If it's true, you should write it down and keep it as a reference. Otherwise, ignore it and pretend it doesn't happen.

Lecture on November 15, 1985

Receiving Fake But Not Realizing

Many people in the world speak lies, but few speak the truth. Just as there are many people who lie, and few people who tell the truth. Please try to research, why is this situation? Why do people study emptiness honestly? Why do they want to lie everywhere? Why do people like to lie, but not like to tell the truth? Because in this world, few people are truthful, and many are liars; There are many hypocrites, but few honest people. If you follow the worldly path and say good things, everyone will like them, but if you speak truthfully, no one will like you. Why so? Because people often like lies, not the truth. That's why it's called: Recognizing falsehood but not recognizing the truth. That's the psychology of some people. Even though they know it's a lie, they're still attached and refuse to let go.

Layman Thuan Da is an honest person. Although his family was very poor, he always spoke the truth. He is not like the demon king Ba-Tuan, who specializes in saying good things and saying that his mantra can save people's lives. Those are sweet, ambiguous words that make the listener feel goosebumps all over their body. Mr. Thuan Da is very honest. He did not brag about how he offered food with all the rich flavors and ingredients, or how it tasted. His words were very humble like: "May the World-Honored One be compassionate and accept our last offering!" Just like the Chinese who entertain guests, even though the table is full of wine and food, they still humbly say to the guests: "Today's treat is simple, there is nothing special!"

Speaking of this, I remember a story. Once upon a time there was a rich man who, because he had a son, held a grand party to celebrate. He invited a large number of guests, so "noble friends filled the table, and distinguished guests were as numerous as clouds." He again invited three Venerable monks to chant the auspicious mantra and say a few auspicious words to praise and congratulate him. Someone among the guests said: "Your son will definitely be honored and wealthy, and will live to be a hundred years old." Others said: "The baby will have blessings, fortune, and longevity, and he will have fewer illnesses, fewer disasters, and fewer disasters." When the owner heard these auspicious words, his face was filled with joy and indescribable pleasure, so he offered wine to the guests.

As for the three Venerable Monks, one recited the auspicious mantra, one spoke auspicious words, but one of them spoke the truth: "In the future your son will definitely die." As soon as the owner heard it, he immediately became angry.

- No way! Why did you curse him to death?

So he brought the Venerable out to fight him. The Venerable had diligently cultivated patience, so that he did not feel resentment. On the contrary, his face was still gentle as he said to his master: "Layman! You did not realize the truth, but you still loved flattery. In fact, do they really know that your child will be rich or have a long life in the future? Those are just words of praise and praise. Now I say that your child will die in the future, that is the truth. Not only will your child die, but all the people in this world, everyone. Everyone must die. Who is not dead? You have not enlightened to this truth, and yet you still attack me, you are too stupid!

After hearing this, the owner felt it made sense and felt a sense of repentance. From then on, he believed in the Three Jewels and supported the ashram. If that Venerable also said good words like everyone else, there would be no way to move the rich man to believe in Buddha and believe in morality.

We should not like to listen to praise, nor should we be complacent, self-indulgent, or boastful about ourselves. We must be humble and peaceful. Towards others, we are not arrogant, not arrogant, and need to have a spirit of compassion, joy, and forgiveness to help all sentient beings. Please try and see! Why does India have four types of castes? Because there are people who, in ancient times, despised the poor, so in this life they were born as lowly people. That is the cause and effect of the past, it is true!

We should clearly understand cause and effect, and believe in the principle - what is the cause is what is the effect. And no matter where we are, we must work honestly and cannot be fake at all. Because if we lie just a little, we will have to suffer retribution. That's why it is said: "If the cause is not true, the result is not right," that is, if the cause is not straight, the result will be crooked.

Ladies and Gentlemen! Plant beans and get beans, plant melons and get melons, plant rice and get rice, sow sticky rice and get sticky rice. This principle is definitely not wrong in the slightest. If you do crazy things, in the end you're fooling yourself, not everyone else.

Lecture on November 20, 1985

Compassion, Joy, and Equanimity Cures the Three Poisons

A person's toxic mind is created by three karmas of body, speech, and mind. That's because people don't have a heart of compassion, joy, and forgiveness. Therefore, people are doomed from one life to another and create more and more evil karma. Those karmas accumulate from a little to a lot, so the toxins in people's bodies become deeper and deeper every day. There is no cure for this type of poison, and over time it will turn into snakes, centipedes, scorpions, etc. These animals have poisonous mouths, poisonous tails, poisonous feet, and poisonous bodies. In short, there are types of poison like that, if it's mild, it will make people fall into a coma, if it's severe, it will cause people to lose their life. Truly extremely scary.

People should have compassion. With regard to people or things, we should live together in peace and treat each other with a sincere heart. It's all about thinking about others, we must not use cruel tricks to oppress people. People who study Buddhism must not reject cause and effect, but must pay close attention to the matter of cause and effect and retribution! If someone attacks you unreasonably, or they use defamatory words, or take actions to harm you, you should deal with them with a calm, non-rebellious attitude. You should use compassion to influence people, called: "Repaying evil with virtue," making them change their minds and repent. We should learn the spirit of Bodhisattva Maitreya, that is, Forbearance! Ring! Ring! In this way, the sword and spear will naturally turn into brocade; The rain will stop, the sky will be clear again, the waves will calm down, and the wind will calm down. Otherwise, if you don't have enough concentration and calmness, you will curse at small things, and fight over big things. As a result, both sides were hurt, and then, like a boy and a stork fighting over each other, in the end he took advantage, and they became the sacrificed product.

In the past, there was a Living Buddha of Gold Mountain Temple who, because he had the power of concentration, was not afraid of any kind of poison. Because He used great compassion to transform all poisonous animals, they became close friends and absolutely did not harm Him. In the Pho Mon chapter, it is said: "Anyone who recites the name of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva can transform and cause poisonous animals to turn evil towards good and will not harm humans. When studying Buddha Dharma, we should thoroughly understand the meanings and clearly understand the inner reasons, only then can we be considered genuine learners of Buddha Dharma.

Many people have an interest in far-fetched things, strange and magical things. They specialize in such realms. That's having the wrong mindset! We should stay in the place of Love, Compassion, Joy, and Equanimity to practice. So how to use it? First of all, we should put effort into not fighting, not seeking, not being greedy, not being selfish, not taking personal advantage, and not lying. Although this principle is shallow, we must first firmly grasp that shallowness, because from the near comes the far and from the shallow comes the deep. We should not discuss far-reaching magical things, or make endless arguments, so that no one can understand, which is of no use at all.

Therefore it is said: "You should contemplate the nature of the dharma realm, everything is created by the mind." The mind can create heaven, the mind can create hell. The Ten Dharma Realms do not go beyond a single thought, so we can know that: The mind is one movement, the karmic shadow depends on the branch, that is, as soon as the thought arises, the karmic shadow immediately follows. The ancients said:

Three dots like star clusters

The hook is like a crescent moon

Bring the feathers from here

Becoming a Buddha also came from there.

That is a description of the structure of the word TAM ( ) , so we can clearly understand our own nature. If you understand your mind clearly, then there will be no more anger. All the fighting, greed, seeking, and consistency will no longer exist. Only then will we be truly free, truly liberated, and truly understand what it means to be human.

Humans inherently have Buddha nature, each of us has it in full. However, we throw away our Buddha nature, abandon the near to seek the far and cling to the outside. We look for trash, consider it precious, and treat it like a treasure. That was both laughable and pitiful at the same time! I hope everyone knows how to realize this and practice diligently, keep their hearts pure, reduce their desires and do not compete with life.

Someone said: "Everything in the world, from mountains, rivers, houses, to thorns, poisonous grass, soil, trees, sand, and rocks, are all created by the mind." If we know that everything is created by the mind, then why don't we clean out all the trash in our minds to decorate the world in the future? Amitabha Buddha's World of Ultimate Bliss was created because, long ago, he wanted to make living beings happy and free from suffering. Because he diligently practiced the Six Virtues and Dedicated the merits

which creates the world of Ultimate Bliss.

We should also create a world of Ultimate Bliss. So how to create? First of all, we must not have broken hearts. What is love failure? These are joy, anger, guilt, anger, love, hate, and desire; i.e. happiness, anger, sadness, fear, love, hate, desire. When we tame those seven emotions, they will no longer be able to rebel. At that time, our mind will be at peace and no suffering will exist. Why is there suffering? Because the mind is not at peace. And if there are no sufferings and only enjoy happy things, then this is the world of Ultimate Bliss of the human world.

Once we have not conquered the seven emotions, it may be because they are too strong or weak and inadequate, not suitable for the middle path, so we go crazy and turn upside down. If we clearly understand our feelings and can subdue them and stop them from causing trouble, that means we have subdued our mind. Because love is born from the mind, so when the heart is happy or angry, it is all because the mind is being rotated according to the realm. Now that we have found the root cause, we will no longer be confused and will also make the heretical demons surrender. Why do pagan demons come to disturb my mind? Because we have used our emotions excessively. Once we seek externally, our mind will not be calm. Therefore, we have led demons into our minds to be their masters. If we follow its orders and are under its command, then we no longer have autonomy and will become its slaves.

Lecture on November 29, 1985

Cultivating the Way Doesn't Seek Outside Things

Whoever can subdue the eighteen precepts: the six senses, the six senses, and the six consciousnesses, preventing them from rebelling, is a Bodhisattva. Whoever can clean up his emotions so that they are no longer messy is that person who is a Bodhisattva. Bodhisattva neither laughs nor cries. At any time, anywhere, the Bodhisattva is free, without constraints, without obstacles, without troubles or worries, without birth and death, without structure or purity, without increase or decrease. People who study Buddhism should apply their efforts right here.

Zen Buddhism does not use writing as its guiding principle. Why? Because they are afraid that beginners will be attached to the form of writing, which will then give rise to attachment to dharma. Anyone who has attachment to ego or dharma cannot achieve freedom. Because of afflictions and delusions that oppress their bodies and minds, they must float in the stream of birth and death, rising and falling in the ocean of suffering, forever never ending.

You should be alert to understand that human life is impermanent, impermanent ghosts will come to find us at any time. At that time, "Ten thousand states cannot pass, only karma depends on the form," everything cannot be taken away, only karma follows you. We should know that Shakyamuni Buddha also had to enter Nirvana, not that he lived forever. What's more, ordinary people like us need to be even more vigilant! Time is running out, we should make diligent efforts to study Buddha Dharma, only then can we escape the cycle of birth and death. If we don't try hard, then wait

What great eon will it take to achieve this?

We should understand a little and then do a little, don't be tempted to do things that are far from reality. We must know that: cake cannot relieve hunger. Let's return to our homeland to take care of our home, our inherent treasure. Why do we have to look outside? Everything is in the self-nature. If not losing it, then gaining it! No gain and no loss means freedom. No increase, no decrease, no coming, no going, right here it is. Therefore we do not need to look far away. As Master Vinh Gia said in the Dao Ca Ca:

Destroying dharma wealth, destroying merit

Mac is not due to self-consciousness

The meditation door of the willow gate rejects the mind and enters the power of non-birth, knowledge and understanding.

Mean:

Waste of legal resources, end of merit

Nothing more than just delusion

Therefore, meditation does not use the mind

Instantly attain enlightenment of non-birth and wisdom.

When we do not use our conscious mind, we have become one with the religion. So what's there to worry about? What's the problem?

Lecture on December 1, 1985

Good or Bad - Unmoved

People who study Buddhism should not immediately feel happy when they hear someone praise them, but whenever they hear someone say something bad about them, they become extremely upset. Through that expression, it proves that I do not have concentration. If we practice concentration, we will not be shaken by the realms of the eight winds. Saying you're good is the same, saying you're not good is the same. Regardless of whether it's good or not, it's all the same. Then am I not stupid? No! It's just because we don't distinguish whether it's good or not, nor do we distinguish between right and wrong. Someone said: "So that's not nonsense?" Then you are not confused, so do you really understand? Not sure yet! If you can deal with the immutable with the immutable, with the immovable against the immutable, always and everywhere in concentration, then you will truly understand.

People who are truly diligent will not be afraid of anything. Even if someone comes to kill me, I'm not afraid. We use our clear and righteous mind to do common work, without fear of indifferent people criticizing us for being incorrect. So it is said: "True gold is not afraid of fire, right mind is not afraid of shadow." Nowadays, there are some people who like to meddle in other people's affairs, rather than taking care of their own affairs. These behaviors are truly unacceptable. Please examine yourself and see if you have such thoughts?

Lecture on December 5, 1985

Honestly Reciting Buddha's Name

Supreme, profound, wonderful dharma,

Hundreds of thousands of lifetimes are difficult to encounter.

The golden knowledge of the text is attained and maintained,

May I explain the true meaning of the Tathagata.

“In the Dharma Ending Age, there were billions of people practicing, very rare

There is only one person who has attained enlightenment, only by reciting the Buddha's name can he be saved." In the Dharma Ending Age, even if there are hundreds of millions of people practicing, it is unlikely that even one person will attain enlightenment. Fortunately, thanks to the Buddha's Recitation method, we can escape the cycle of birth and death, attain happiness and be reborn in the Western world of Ultimate Bliss. We have the misfortune to be born in a time when demons are strong and the dharma is weak, in the time of the Dharma Ending, being separated from Buddha for too long. However, in an unfortunate situation, we are fortunate to encounter the Buddha's Recitation method. The method of reciting the Buddha's name not only saves money, but also does not cost you mentally. It is both easy and convenient. Because of reciting Buddha's name, we will become Buddha.

Why will reciting Buddha's name lead to Buddhahood? Because from countless previous lives, Amitabha Buddha made forty-eight great vows. And among those forty-eight vows, there is one vow that says: "If any sentient being recites my name, but is not born in the Pure Land, I swear I will not attain Perfect Enlightenment." Amitabha Buddha emits these vows, his vow is to take sentient beings to the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, but only on the condition that sentient beings have faith. Believe that Amitabha Buddha really exists in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, vow to be born in the Pure Land to be his disciple, and sincerely recite the name Amitabha Buddha. We must have faith, vows and actions. Once we have these three fourths, we will definitely be born in the West.

The World of Ultimate Bliss has no suffering, only enjoys happy things and does not have the three evil paths: hell, hungry ghosts, and animals. Even though there are white cranes, peacocks, flamboyant birds, relics, old calanthus, and life-giving birds; But those bird species were all transformed by Amitabha Buddha in order to spread the Dharma. This is due to changes in the realm, not that animals really exist. The world of Ultimate Bliss does not have ten thousand sufferings, many evil things, and is filled with afflictions like the Saha world.

The Pure Land preaches wonderful Dharma day and night, reciting the Buddha, reciting the Dharma, and reciting the Sangha. But if we want to be born in the Pure Land, we must sincerely recite Buddha's name. We cannot help but sincerely recite. To honestly recite is to single-mindedly recite Buddha's name, and not care about whether you will become a Buddha or not, nor care about whether you will be reborn or not be reborn, but just use the merit of reciting Buddha's name right at this moment. Reciting the Buddha's name, reciting the Buddha's name to be single-minded, mature, and single-minded is not chaotic. When we are about to die, Amitabha Buddha will definitely lead us back to His realm.

Why did Amitabha Buddha come to welcome ordinary people like us? This is very unbelievable. Not wrong! This is an unbelievable dharma. That's why no one asked, but Shakyamuni Buddha himself spoke the Amitabha Sutra. Because no one knows and no one believes in this Dharma, Shakyamuni Buddha, with his compassionate and earnest heart, told us living beings of the Dharma Ending Age to practice in a shortcut way.

Here in the Dharma Ending Age.

Honestly, reciting Buddha's name means reciting Buddha with your mouth and reciting Buddha with your mind. When we walk, stand, lie down, or sit, we all recite Amitabha Buddha. Recite Amitabha Buddha's name verbally and physically practice according to Amitabha Buddha's conduct. Why is it called happiness? Just like we are currently attending Buddha That. No matter how busy we are, we must let go to participate in Buddha's Seven, and must recite so that we can be single-minded and undisturbed. One mind without chaos means one thought follows another, continuous thought. It's not like you can recite for a while and then feel tired and want to go and rest. A person who is lazy like that cannot attain Buddha Recitation Samadhi. That's called not honestly reciting Buddha's name.

Honestly reciting Buddha's name means reciting Buddha with one mind and one thought. When reciting Buddha's name, I forget everything like eating, wearing clothes, and going to sleep. Eating, wearing clothes, sleeping are normal things, human life cannot be abandoned; Every person cannot do without those things every day. But when reciting Buddha's name, we can forget those three things, then we don't know whether we are eating, drinking, wearing clothes or sleeping at all. That is truly reciting Buddha's name. If we know when we have to go eat, that is not honestly reciting Buddha's name. Or knowing that you want to wear more clothes when it's cold, that's not honestly reciting Buddha's name. Or when we don't get enough sleep, we want to go on vacation. That's not honestly reciting Buddha's name.

To be honest, no matter what you walk, stand, lie down or sit down, you only know the six-word name "Namo Amitabha Buddha." You recite in a continuous, uninterrupted chain; Even the sound of running water is reciting “Namo Amitabha Buddha,”

The sound of the wind blowing is also the recitation of "Namo Amitabha Buddha", the sound of birds chirping is also the recitation of "Namo Amitabha Buddha." You must recite until Namo Amitabha Buddha and yourself are inseparable. Recite until there is no more self outside of "Namo Amitabha Buddha", and outside of the self there is no longer "Namo Amitabha Buddha". My chanting "Namo Amitabha Buddha" and I become one. At that time, the wind does not blow through, the rain does not penetrate, and so we achieve the Samadhi of Nembutsu. Flowing water and moving wind are all magical discourses, reciting "Namo Amitabha Buddha," that is Honest Buddha Recitation.

If water flows and knows it is flowing water, if wind moves and knows it is wind moving, or if we look sideways and up and down to see if there is any movement in any place, that means we are not honestly reciting Buddha's name. If while reciting Buddha's name, you look forward and backward as if wanting to steal something, that means you are not sincerely reciting Buddha's name.

To be honest, reciting the Buddha's name means knowing every thought, reciting the thoughts in your mind, without any false thoughts, nor thinking about eating delicious food or drinking tea, forgetting everything. There is no secret here, just control your mind to stay and not have false thoughts, then that is honestly reciting Buddha's name. If you cannot control your mind and keep worrying about delusions, then it is not sincere reciting Buddha's name. When you initiate mindfulness, that means sincerely reciting Buddha's name. If you keep thinking wildly and have evil thoughts, then you are not sincerely reciting Buddha's name. Therefore, reciting Buddha's name honestly is an unspeakable miracle. If you truly know how to recite Buddha's name, you will achieve great Freedom, no person, no self, no sentient beings, no recipient, and only the name Namo Amitabha Buddha!

Speaking is Dharma, practicing is Tao. Just talking without acting is like that

Counting other people's money doesn't benefit me at all. Today I tell you this principle. If you understand clearly, you must honestly recite Buddha's name and honestly attend Buddha's Seventh Anniversary. This is the most precious time in our lives, so don't let it pass in vain. I hope you will make an effort to recite Buddha's name, bringing all three of your minds: perseverance, sincerity, and permanence to recite Buddha's name and attend Buddha's Seventh Anniversary.

Lecture on December 16, 1985

Birth and Death Like: Sleeping, Waking - But Still Reciting Amitabha

From countless eons up to now, we are born and then die, die and then be born again, just like humans wake up and then sleep again, sleep and then wake up again. When I go to sleep at night, I feel like a dead person. When I woke up in the morning, I was like a new born person. It's just that this matter of birth and death is short, and our lifespan is a bit longer in comparison.

However, birth and death are just like sleeping and waking up. Why? Because sometimes we are confused, sometimes we are clear and bright. Clarity means birth, confusion means death. Therefore, if we have a clear thought, and with that thought we are alive; Whenever I have a confused thought, with that thought I feel like I am dead. That is a short, temporary period of birth and death. Regardless of the time of birth and death, whether short or long, it is all revolving in the cycle of birth and death, floating and sinking without rest. Sometimes we are born into a rich and wealthy family, sometimes we are born into a poor and miserable family. Sometimes we are born as a buffalo, as a horse, as an animal, sometimes as a hungry ghost, or in hell. These are all reincarnations, floating uncertainly in the sea of ​​suffering of birth and death, because this cycle of birth and death never ends, it will never end.

Buddha Shakyamuni was so pitiful to sentient beings that he could not wait any longer and "did not ask any questions." No one asked but he said this Pure Land Dharma Gate himself. The Pure Land Dharma Gate is a method method that is very easy to use. The path is very straight, we just need to recite Namo Amitabha Buddha with faith, vows and practice is enough. Therefore, faith, vows, and actions are the three sources of food, the three necessary expenses for us to be reborn in the Western Pure Land. First, we must believe in Amitabha Buddha, believe in the World of Ultimate Bliss, believe that the Buddhist recitation method can take us to the Pure Land to meet Amitabha Buddha. We must have faith. Don't say: I haven't seen it, and there's no proof, so I can't believe it. We just need to have faith, and nothing else. Next is the vow to meet Amitabha Buddha, vow to be born in the Pure Land, and vow to practice the Buddha's name. After making the vow, we must practice according to the Pure Land dharma, reciting Buddha's name, and practice. We must truly recite Buddha's name, that is, we must honestly recite Buddha's name. After reciting a lot, we can become one, undisturbed mind and achieve the Samadhi of Buddha Recitation. Thus we will definitely be reborn in the Western world of Ultimate Bliss.

The Saha world is a world surrounded by countless sufferings, filled with thousands of evil things, with plans to harm each other, and there is never a moment of peace. In the Western Pure Land, there are no troubles or problems at all. Therefore, we must wish to be born in the Pure Land, to meet Amitabha Buddha, to be reborn from the lotus flower and to achieve the state of irreversibility. Non-regression is: non-regression of taste, non-regression of thoughts and non-regression of actions. The state of non-regression is to attain the state of non-regression. Reciting without turning back is the mind reciting the Buddha, reciting the Dharma, reciting the Sangha, and at any moment the mind does not regress. Not regressing means practicing according to this method and not regressing. When you attain these three principles of non-return, you will definitely become a Buddha in the future. Once we have the three treasures: faith, vow, and practice, it is very easy for us to go on the path to meet Amitabha Buddha in the Pure Land, because that is the power of Amitabha Buddha's vow.

In the worlds of the ten directions, if there is any living being who sincerely recites the name Namo Amitabha Buddha, then at the time of his death, Amitabha Buddha will come and lead him to the Buddha realm.

When reciting Buddha's name, it's like sending a telegram to the Pure Land. If we recite Buddha's name one sentence, we will send a telegram; if we recite Buddha's name two sentences, we will send two telegrams. Every day we send telegrams to Amitabha Buddha. Amitabha Buddha in the Pure Land also has a radar and a machine to receive telegrams. So what are radar and telegram receivers? It is the seven-jeweled lotus pond. You recite the Buddha's name once, and the lotus grows a little. If you recite, all of you are Amitabha

Buddha, then the lotus will gradually grow bigger like a wheel. Wait until you are born in the Pure Land, your one spirit Buddha nature and your one spirit true nature will come to this lotus and be born. When the lotus blooms, your Buddha nature will also appear. So say:

I wish to be born in the Western Pure Land,

Nine-grade lotus flower acts as a parent,

Flowers open the Buddha's view to enlightenment without birth,

Non-retreating Bodhisattva as travel companion.

We hope to be born as parents from the highest quality lotus flower. When the lotus blooms, we see Amitabha Buddha and realize the patience of non-birth. At that time we will attain immortality, escape birth and death, and be friends with the Bodhisattvas who do not retreat. When we reach the Pure Land, our friends and relatives are all friends with the Great Bodhisattvas. That's why we preach the sutras and preach the Dharma together every day, all moving forward together.

Lecture on December 17, 1985

Seven Loves, Six Desires and Earthquakes

Buddhist scriptures often talk about great earthquakes, that is, earthquakes. So where do earthquakes come from?

Earthquakes can also be said to be human earthquakes, because causes and earthquakes are interconnected. When people move, the earth also moves. When people don't move, the earth doesn't move either. When Buddha entered Nirvana, why were there six types of shocks? Because people's hearts are so frightened and frightened, all seven emotions and six desires spew out, which is an earthquake. Therefore, when you are happy it is an earthquake, if you are angry or frustrated it is also an earthquake. Your sadness, grief, and fear are also earthquakes. When you give birth to love, it is also an earthquake. If you feel disgusted, it's still an earthquake. If you give birth to thoughts of desire, it will cause even more great earthquakes.

Because the seven emotions and six desires in the mind are vibrant, the earth will shake. Why does the world have earthquakes? Because every day people create earthquakes, they just don't know it. Especially love, love creates even bigger earthquakes. When everyone, everyone is not at peace, that is causing a great earthquake.

Mountains, forests, trees, rivers and seas are who we are. Your hair is like the mountains and forests; eyes, eyebrows, and whiskers are trees; Rivers and seas are desires that we cannot control. That caused a big earthquake.

When Buddha was about to enter Nirvana, everyone was shocked. When I didn't cry in normal times, I have to cry now. The visible earth shook, the invisible earth also shook. Because the inside shakes, the outside shakes, and the inside shakes, so the outside shakes. What is inside, is what is outside. Therefore, the inside and outside are interconnected and closely related to each other.

We humans love and love every day, so we create earthquakes every day. This is a very dangerous thing, a matter of life and death, but people still create earthquakes without knowing it. They had to wait until a tangible earthquake actually happened, then they knew they were afraid. During the invisible stage, creating an earthquake, they are not afraid. Once the cause for an earthquake is sown, there will be an earthquake. People don't know fear when they sow seeds, but when they reap the rewards, they become scared.

Today I say this, you probably won't believe it!

Lecture on June 3, 1986

Thousands of Waves Rise to Take Souls

When I was young, I specialized in treating people. Whenever someone is sick, I must treat them well to relieve their pain. Because of that, I have offended many pagan heavenly demons and cows, demons, snakes, and gods. They all have great supernatural powers and are waiting for an opportunity to attack. Whenever you open the door, they rush in to attack immediately, called: "Opening the door" means opening the door to let demons or flying stars enter your body - (Shurangama Sutra, section about the Five Skandhas). Or maybe they rush in to steal your soul, chase your soul away, and then cling to your body to talk nonsense and nonsense. At that time, I had offended many demons and devils because I had accepted a young disciple. His Dharma name is the Kingdom of Fruition, which means that his fruition will definitely be rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. This boy followed me to become a monk because he also had a predestined relationship.

One day, while meditating, I knew there would be a child who wanted to become a monk. This baby is plump, chubby, and looks very handsome. Early the next morning, I told my senior disciple: "Pay attention, today there will be a young boy coming to ask for ordination. When he comes, you must notify me immediately!" At about one o'clock in the afternoon, my senior disciple was panting and said with a Shandong accent; “Master, this morning you said that a young boy had come to ask to become a monk. Indeed, he has arrived now.”

Has it really arrived? Where?

It is in front of the kitchen.

I went out to see. It was a child dressed in rags, shaking his neck and gawking at me. Later, he became a monk with me, and every day he held a fan and looked like Venerable Te Cong. When he was five years old, this boy could treat people's illnesses. Who helps it do that? Dill is fox spirit and snake spirit. In his previous life, the boy was a psychic healer (in northern China it's called Khieu Than, in Taiwan it's called Chiem Dong). These types of bulls, demons, and snakes came to the boy when he was five years old, and they gave him the ability to cure diseases. There are diseases that the boy can cure, but there are diseases that he cannot cure. Some people call it "Little Demon Obstacle," because it has demonic energy in its body, but does not have any healing magic.

When he was twelve or thirteen years old, he also got sick. What disease is it? Stomach disease, but it cannot be cured by itself. One day, he dreamed that a fat monk came to his house and told him: "If you want to be cured of your illness, you must go to Tam Duyen Pagoda, in Hop Nhi, to become a monk and worship Dharma Master An Tu as your teacher. That way you will be cured of your illness immediately." The dream happened three times in a row and it was exactly the same, so the little boy believed it. The boy lives more than a thousand miles away from my temple. At that time, Japan had just surrendered, yet he went to Hebin alone. On the way, he saw that some Japanese weapons were still left behind in the military warehouse after surrendering. He went there and picked up two grenades, then went and played with the grenades. At night, he slept outside. At that time, dozens of wolves surrounded him and attacked him from all directions. The little boy was not afraid at all and told them: "Dear friends! You have arrived, so let me give you a few eggs to eat!" The wolves didn't want to eat the eggs (grenades), so they ran away.

Seeing the little boy like that, I asked: "Why did you come here?"

He replied: "I came to ask for ordination."

Why?

There was a fat Venerable, that is, the one sitting in the temple at the three-entrance gate. He told me in a dream to come here and find Dharma Master An Tu to ask for ordination, so that I would be cured.

You have no food to eat, no clothes to wear, no house to live in so you came here to become a monk, right?

Not so! Because the fat Venerable Master taught me three times, that's why I came here.

At that time I had a dumpling in my hand. I took a bite and chewed it thoroughly, then spit out both the cake and my saliva onto the ground and said:

- If you want to become a monk, you must first eat all these foods

Go.

It looked up at me, then lied down on the ground and picked it up to eat. I saw that the boy could still be trained, so I let him stay. Sure enough, after becoming a monk, his illness was gone.

After more than half a year, the boy really gained five eyes and six eyes, he could really see anything. The power of the heavenly eye, the power of the natural ear, the power of other minds, the power of life, and the power of divine mantras are all there. I took him everywhere to treat people's illnesses. During treatment, people relied on this little boy to find out my origin. They asked: Now do you have such great abilities? We have heard about it for a long time, but we don't know if your Master has supernatural powers or not? Everyone knows that he practices, but don't know if he has supernatural powers like Teacher? He blinked, then said in the air: Probably not! It's strange, when he finished saying that sentence, his magical powers were no longer there. It doesn't matter if he no longer has magical powers, but the relatives of the cow, ghost, and snake god enter again, causing him to become a demon based on demonic energy like before. Seeing that, I thought: "Is there such a thing! The boy has followed me to become a monk, and now the ghosts still dare to come here and bother him!" So me and them fought. For twenty-one days, during this time, I neither ate nor slept. Fighting to the end, I conquered those demons. After subduing them, I think nothing will happen again.

Then I went to Dong Tinh, this village is surrounded by mountains on all four sides, and there is only one well in the village. The house where I stopped to stay temporarily had just a fence made of forest trees outside, so it couldn't stop the wind, it couldn't stop the rain, it couldn't stop anything. One day, I took four young disciples to stay there, and everyone in that house took refuge in me. Because when I was in the Northeast, which is Manchuria, I often took care of temple work, so I had to travel here and there.

While staying there, the underwater monsters found an opportunity to drown me. From the sky it rained, below the well water rose three feet high. That means superiors and subordinates fight hand to hand. In the north, in Manchuria, people slept on brick furnace beds, that is, on the fireplace mantle. When the water rises too quickly, people have no way to escape; Someone standing on the brick kiln bed was also drowned. That time, more than thirty people drowned, and more than eight hundred houses were swept away. But the house made of fences and bamboo panels that I live in, although it cannot stop the wind and rain, in the yard the water is only one or two feet high, while outside the water is ten feet high.

I will also tell you the truth that my four little disciples all have five eyes and six eyes, so when we saw such heavy rain, we "made the precepts," so the flood water could not enter. That situation is not much different from the flooded scene at Kim Son Pagoda. That was the first time I was submerged in water, but there was no drowning.

The second time I experienced flooding was when I took a boat from Tianjin to Shanghai. The time for a normal cruise is about four or five days, but that time, the boat kept spinning around in one place on the pitch black sea, unable to move anywhere. Therefore, the boat had to stop there for more than ten days.

There were fourteen monks on the boat, but all the rice and noodles were eaten, so everyone almost starved to death. At that time, I didn't chant any mantras. I vomited everything in my stomach, even the yellow bile. I lay down on the deck and thought to myself: "I was born to dedicate myself to Buddhism. If Buddhism does not need me, then I will jump into the sea alone, without getting involved with these people. If Buddhism still needs me, I hope Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara will manifest and allow this boat to reach Shanghai safely."

I thought that if after five minutes the wind didn't stop, I would jump into the ocean. As soon as I finished speaking, the wind stopped, the rain stopped, and finally the boat arrived safely in Shanghai. The dozen people on the boat also avoided becoming sharks' prey or turning into ghosts. That was the disaster I caused, so after coming to Hong Kong, I didn't dare to interfere in other people's affairs. But if I happen to encounter it by chance, I will still intervene a little.

When I came to the United States, I put up a war exemption sign. Even if a pagan demon came to challenge me, I would bow my head, pay my respects, and repent. They see that I no longer have any strength left and I am prepared for them to come and take my life at any time. I have been in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas for ten years, and now I am stepping down and retiring. If they want to come find me again, it's okay. Besides, I don't have anything to do!

Lecture on July 1, 1986

Dharma Gate Dragon Statue Great Man

O good and knowledgeable people! Tomorrow is the 4th of July, the National Day of the United States and also the day intern Phuong Truong takes office. This new Phuong Truong is very fierce. Before he took office, he already wanted to kill a few people to sacrifice to the Dharma. Who did you kill? Kill the enemy! Those who were enemies in the past, or would be enemies in the future, all had to have their heads chopped off to be publicly shamed. When the new teacher Phuong Truong took office, he wanted to establish rules. Why haven't I established any rules until now? Because I am a slave of France, everything is OK, no problem. But this new Phuong Truong is more tyrannical, so he wants to kill the enemy, kill as many enemies as possible, called "Kill all the enemies of Buddhism, leaving only the Venerable High Monk." A La Han also translates as "Kill the enemy," so it is said: "Eliminating violence can bring peace," eliminating evil people can bring peace.

Please pay attention! Don't think that flattering the new Mr. Phuong Truong means he's a good guardian. In fact, it is you who hinder and hinder the development of Buddha Dharma. As Phuong Truong, you should not arbitrarily praise or criticize others, nor be swayed by praise or slander. If you want someone to praise you, then someone will definitely criticize you. That's just natural morality.

In the past, I let everything go, even if someone scolded me, it was fine; Someone complimented me, but I forgot about it. So now I practice being Phuong Truong, which means I have to maintain the principle of not praising or criticizing. You don't want people to praise you, so you shouldn't praise them first; If you don't want people to criticize you, then first of all you should not criticize others, which is called: "Don't push what you don't want to others." Remember, don't sow impure seeds.

The lay followers saw the new Master Phuong Truong and wanted to offer special foods, which was an act that damaged the Buddha Dharma. If they do not want to cause the decline of Buddha Dharma, they will not "embroider flowers on brocade" and embellish it like that. Mr. Phuong Truong will not starve to death. Even if he starves to death, it's worth it. Who says he doesn't care about practicing? Furthermore, if one can starve to death for the sake of Buddhism, then it would be an honor and a meritorious deity in Buddhism. So our consistent guideline is:

Cold and dead without fate.

Starving to death does not turn into fate.

Poor people die without praying for fate.

Depends on fate but does not change;

Not changing but depending on fate.

Maintain our three great principles.

Sacrifice one's life for the sake of Buddhism.

Create a network for your duty.

Right livelihood for the Sangha.

When I encounter something that makes sense,

Understand the reason for that action.

Continuing the Patriarch's heart transmission.

Who wants to make offerings to you alone, that's a predestined relationship with you to get your attention, do you know? Especially since you are young, you must understand this point very clearly. I am already old, as people say, "incompetent old man," useless old man. But young people should not let dirty things surround them. You should "Even if you freeze to death, still stand and welcome the wind. Even if you die of hunger, still hold out your chest." Be a bright torch in a strong wind, be pure gold in a big furnace, fear nothing!

Freezing to death without fate: This is the description of my life. When I was in Manchuria, in winter and summer I wore the same three layers of fabric, just one layer of fabric on the bottom, the top layer was a few patches, each patch, each patch extending upwards. Will I be cold then? It's cold! So why do I have to endure so patiently? Because I want to "freeze to death without any luck!"

Starving to death does not turn into fate: When I was in Quan Am Cave, Furong Mountain in Hong Kong, there was no food for two weeks. I then meditated in the cave to wait for death. At that time, under the mountain there was a layman named Lao Khoan Thanh, nicknamed the "Original Dharma Master" of that area. And she was warned in a dream three times in a row by Bodhisattva Vi-Da: "In Quan Am cave there is Dharma Master An Tu, you should go there and make offerings." So the next day, this layman carried more than thirty kilograms of rice and more than 70 dong to the cave to make offerings to me. Three or four months before this happened, the lay woman was bitten on the leg by a dog. Eastern and western doctors treated her for several months, but could not cure her. They also had to give up and give up. Bodhisattva Vi-Da likes to worry about other people's affairs, so he told the laywoman: "If you go make offerings to the Dharma Master at Quan Am Cave, your leg will heal immediately."

So she believed and brought rice and money to make offerings. At that time in the cave, I was prepared to starve to death. I have never said to anyone before: "Please have mercy on me, it has been many days and I have had nothing to eat!" That is "starving to death without becoming fate."

Die poor without praying for fate: When I first came to Nam Hoa Temple in Guangdong and became close to Venerable Master Hu Van, I didn't have a single coin or word on me. I don't even have the money to send poetry, but I have never gone to lay people to seek karma. Therefore, these three great directives of mine all have origins, and are not baseless. Now that the new teacher Phuong Truong has taken office, everyone should not be alone in forming feelings for him, making him have special sympathy for them. If you have the heart to make offerings, you can make offerings to the public, do not make offerings to anyone individually. Otherwise, it's really harmful to people! It's destroying harmony in Buddhism!

Monastics should not be discouraged but should embrace the above three tones. We should become a representative teacher for heaven and man, and then fight against the demons in the ten directions. Someone asked: "Isn't it true that teachers teach their disciples to use compassion, joy and forgiveness? So, why do you teach them to fight? So don't change your anger, right? If so, how can you be a teacher who represents heaven and people?" It's because we want to be teachers representing heaven and man that we have to educate the demons!

Lecture on July 3, 1986

The Truth of Life

Life is not money but a priceless treasure. We also cannot use money to buy and sell lives. However, there have been many people who sold their lives cheaply. For money, they are willing to sacrifice their lives. In society: three teachings and nine streams, five elements and eight actions, all kinds of professions, no one is willing to sell their soul or life for money.

Confucius said: "The destiny of heaven is called Nature, following Nature is called Tao, cultivating Tao is for the sake of Teaching and cannot be separated, even for a moment." If the Tao can be separated, it is not the Tao. According to the trend of the current era, we can correct it like this: "The destiny of heaven is called Money, following Money is called Tao, practicing Tao is for Money. Money cannot be separated, even for a moment." So "open the back door wide, but close the front door" is like that.

Primary school students on their way to the main hall to participate in the noon worship session.

Nowadays students and teachers are all about money. If professors feel their salaries are not enough, they will strike and not teach. This poisons students, causing them to follow the same ideological pattern, to the point of bringing society to ruin. Social corruption is the responsibility of teachers and professors! Nowadays, there are many schools that are very wild and strange, such as encouraging students to smoke, have a loose personality, and create many illegal things. This era is much more corrupt than the Spring and Autumn Warring States period in China. Indeed, today's orderly style is deteriorating day by day, people's hearts are no longer the same as before. The professors openly criticized: This Saint is not right, that hero is not good, that prime minister is also not good. In short, everyone is not right, only they are right. Why is that? It's not because of money! Assuming they are right, then any amount of money should be attributed to them.

People in this world are addicted to wealth, beauty, fame, food, and sleep without knowing that these are the five roots of hell. The first is greed for wealth, viewing wealth as life. We have just talked about this.

Second is lust. In many families, the husband has many girlfriends, and the wife also has many boyfriends. As a result, they rioted and divorced, then neglected their children, causing them to become orphans. Children see their parents being corrupt like that, so they follow suit, and the consequences are even more unimaginable.

Third is pride. Some people feel that their name is not famous enough, so they deliberately make their name famous. But when he finished making his name famous, he was dead in a flash. Take Mao Zedong for example, his name was resounding at one time. His power is comparable to that of a god. All Chinese people grabbed his book Little Red. Even the Dalai Lama's spells are not as good as yours. Although the Dalai Lama knows how to recite mantras, compared to Mao Zedong, this mantra is not effective.

The fourth desire is to eat and drink. Many people spend a lot of effort to enjoy delicious delicacies or rich, nutritious foods. Like the banquet in the Manchu Han Dynasty that had 108 dishes, it was such a waste of heaven's blessings, such a loss of blessings and loss of life.

You should be careful and understand that: "A gentleman seeks the way, not food" meaning that a gentleman seeks the Way, not food or drink.

The fifth desire is sleep. There are some people who don't like wealth, beauty, fame, or food, but they like to sleep, and no matter how much they sleep, they don't find it enough. Therefore, these five desires make human nature become confused, the soul seems lost, then confused and confused, it runs to hell.

Lecture on July 4, 1986

Bitter and Spicy -

Pink Lotus In Fire

Dear wise friends, it has been ten years since the passing of the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. During those ten years, we faced countless hardships, hardships, and endless conflicts, but I did not go to different places to find love or pray for help. I also don't try to find any tricks to connect with society, or socialize with officials, or please the nobles. Someone introduced me to meet the governor of California and the President of the United States, but I refused. I wonder if you still remember?

In 1979, when the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas held its opening ceremony, there were several hundred people from Malaysia. In addition, there were also good men and women from places such as Hong Kong, Taiwan, San Francisco, and Los Angeles also attending the Dharma conference, a total of several thousand people. That day, the first thing I said to everyone, I still remember very clearly. I said: "All my life, I have looked down on people with money. Why? Because the more money you have, the more bad karma you have." Hearing me say that, more than a hundred people from Malaysia wanted to argue with me. They said: "We came here to support you, but you still scold us. We are all people with money, if you say that, it's not right!"

They wanted to reason with me, but they didn't dare to say it publicly. They went to visit the group's leader and advisor

they are Dharma Master Bodhidharma Nanda.

After hearing the story, Dharma Master Dat Ma Nanda reprimanded them: "You have lived to be seven or eighty years old, but you still cannot distinguish between right and wrong when dealing with things like this. At that time, I was sitting next to Dharma Master Tuyen Hoa. I also heard that every word he said was the Dharma. If you want to argue with Dharma Master Tuyen Hoa, then I can't be in your group anymore. Either you go, or I go!"

Seeing their advisor react like that, they didn't come to argue with me. Dharma Master Dat Ma Nan Da attended that Dharma conference to receive an honorary Doctorate degree from Dharma Realm University.

Everyone who comes to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas should devote part of their effort to take on some responsibilities. I was originally empty-handed and poor. I went through countless hardships and hardships to found the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, but I never complained about difficulties or asked for reinforcements, nor did I go out of my way to call for donations. Now that I have abdicated and retired, Master Phuong Truong has just taken office. In the future, he will do whatever he wants, I don't care about it, because "anyone in office, no matter what is right," if he is no longer in office, he won't have to worry about government affairs.

When lay people have arrived at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, they should not seek comfort or take advantage of the temple's scenery. Or maybe we have more greed than a monk, all day we keep reciting the mantra "greed" and the mantra "struggle," then saying that the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas has no compassion for you. If you come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to be greedy and to compete, then you are looking for the wrong object.

Everyone who takes refuge in me should think to themselves: "How much will the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas give me? And how much will I contribute to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas?" Don't come here to criticize that the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas treated you badly. So how much have you contributed to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas? Once you understand this clearly, your heart will be at peace.

Lecture on July 5, 1986

Thousands of Deaths, Thousands of Lives,

Hundreds of Grinding and Practicing

"Thousands of deaths, hundreds of trainings" means: Thousands of deaths, thousands of lives, hundreds of trainings, this is a parallel sentence about my life. I went through hundreds of thousands of hardships to obtain the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, so please don't destroy it.

When I was fifteen years old, I went to school and learned how to write parallel sentences. I really like this subject. From the very beginning, I felt close to it. At that time, my entire class had over thirty students. When they couldn't come up with parallel sentences, they all sought my help. I then imitated their handwriting and made parallel sentences for them. Not only did this train my way of thinking, but it also broadened my mind.

I went to school for half a year when I was fifteen years old, then when I was sixteen or seventeen years old, I studied for two consecutive years. I studied the Four Books and the Five Classics at a private school. When I was eighteen years old, I started teaching. I alone teach more than 30 students and I share with them everything I have learned. The students are all children of poor families, so I have an obligation to teach them.

One day, in this group of more than thirty students, suddenly about twenty of them developed the disease Duong Mao Dinh, which means goat hair boils. Everyone is scared when talking about this disease. Because if you don't treat the disease promptly, you will definitely die within three days; If you know how to treat it, the disease will be cured immediately. When this disease first appears, the headache is very unpleasant. At that time, I knew how to treat this disease. I use a match stick to press right into the mouth of the boil on my chest. If it sinks down without bulging back, then I know it is goat hair boils. And immediately use an awl to stab the meat and prod it forward, then use a knife to cut off that piece of meat. We will see that there are a lot of hairs in that piece of meat, and only a little blood is oozing out from the cut area. It is certain that treatment must be followed by that method; Boils on the front of the chest are popped out seven times, boils on the back are poked out eight times. You will ask why do you have to do that? Don't ask me. I'm eager to learn, but I don't seek deep understanding. I don't know what the reason is, but once I get it out like that, the disease will completely heal.

I have a very cute student who not only knows how to keep the rules, but is also studious, smart, and knowledgeable. I chose him to be the class leader and also took care of nurturing and educating him. The boy also had this disease of goat's hair.

There is a saying: "Concern leads to chaos." When you worry too much, confusion will arise. Because I was so concerned about its condition, I became impatient. Then that afternoon, after school, I also got this disease! This disease also has demons and infectious germs. People in mountainous areas who get this disease die very quickly.

I can dissect other people's illnesses, but I cannot hold a knife to cut my own flesh. I can remove a boil on my front, but I can't do it on my back. Now what to do? My head hurt like it was about to explode. I thought to myself: "I want to dedicate myself to Buddhism, but now I have this disease, I will definitely die." That's why I started speaking demonic words, which can also be divine words or Bodhisattva words. You can think whatever you want, because it's possible that I'm talking nonsense or gossip. I thought to myself: "I dedicate myself to Buddhism. If Buddha doesn't use me, I will die; but if I can use myself, even if I can't get the boil out, this disease will still heal." Thinking that, I reluctantly fell asleep. After sleeping for a while, I suddenly woke up because I felt like I was suffocating. I slept and felt like my brain was getting bigger, and it was hard to breathe as if something was stuck in my throat. I tried my best to cough and spit out a ball of hair. After that, my warts cured without needing surgery. That was the last life-or-death moment that nearly killed me.

Today I tell you about the dependent origination of the parallel sentence "a thousand deaths, a thousand lives, a hundred grindings" as above. Now that I'm retired, if I remember anything, I'll tell you a little about it.

Lecture on July 6, 1986

How to Learn the Precepts?

Question: We hope that Master will teach us how to make the Dharma last for a long time.

Answer: If you can not fight, not be greedy, not seek, not be selfish, not take personal advantage, not lie, then you will make the Dharma stand in that world.

Question: We don't know how to learn the precepts?

Answer: The Six Great Principles of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas are the precepts. That is:

If you don't fight, you don't violate the precept of killing. Why must we kill? Because I want to compete. If you compete with me, you will commit murder and arson. If you don't fight, don't kill. This is how you keep the precept of not killing.

If you are not greedy, you will not commit the precept of stealing. Why do you want to steal? It's all because of greed. Desire for the things of one's employer. If you are not greedy, you can keep the precept of not stealing.

If you don't pray, you won't violate the precepts. A man searches for a woman, that is a bridge; A woman searching for a man is also a bridge. If you can't pray, your spirit and soul will go crazy. Even in your dreams, you will still pursue it, making your body and mind restless.

If you are not selfish, you will not violate the precepts of lying. Why lie? Because I want to protect my private interests, I deceive people and lie wherever I go.

If we are not selfish, no matter where we are, we can speak the truth and not commit any deception.

If you do not seek personal gain, you will not violate the precepts of alcohol. People who drink alcohol think that drinking alcohol can improve blood circulation, benefit the body, and will definitely keep them healthy. Like a drunk person feeling light and lightheaded as if he had become a god or an immortal. Those are all delusions of people who drink alcohol. They are being manipulated by self-interest.

Do not lie. The five things mentioned above already include false speech. However, in order to make everyone more vigilant, I especially emphasize the evil of false speech. That's why I added this reminder.

If everyone truly does not fight, is not greedy, does not seek, is not selfish, does not seek self-interest, and does not lie, then society will definitely be secure and families will definitely be happy.

If people in the world strictly observe the five precepts and do not commit acts such as: killing, stealing, adultery, lying, and alcoholism, they will have no afflictions, no worries, no worries. Therefore, it can be said that this Six Great Sects is the most wonderful Dharma method, and it can also be said that:

“The supreme and profound dharma.

Hundreds of thousands of lifetimes are difficult to encounter.

I have received and maintained the golden knowledge of the text.

May I solve the true meaning of the cause.”

That is, the wonderful Dharma is very profound and unsurpassed. It's hard to meet in hundreds of thousands of lifetimes. Now I see, hear, and accept. May I understand the true meaning of being human.

I would like to say one more sentence, as a Buddhist, the lowest level is to strictly keep these five basic precepts and practice them thoroughly, only then can we be peaceful and free. If these five precepts cannot be kept, then the 250 precepts of Bhikkhus and the 348 precepts of Bhikkhunis will be even more difficult to keep. Therefore, at the Ta-la Song Tho forest, when Buddha Shakyamuni was about to enter Nirvana, he told Venerable Ananda: "Take the precepts as your teacher." Therefore, we know how important the precepts are!

Lecture on July 7, 1986

Qiankun Transport -

Maintaining the Precepts

Even though it is currently the period of the End of Dharma, Buddhists should awaken their spirit and establish their indestructible Vajrayana vows, in order to transform the End of Dharma into the Dharma. We should be a true Buddhist. If everyone sincerely follows it, it will turn the Ending Dharma into the True Dharma. If Buddhist followers do not know how to perceive and do not sincerely practice Buddha Dharma, then even the Dharma will turn into the End of Dharma. Why is that? Because when people are right, the dharma will be right, if people are skewed, the dharma will also be skewed. A skewed person is a person who does not follow the right path. They do not keep the precepts, but instead look for loopholes in the precepts. Just like the law is to maintain security for society, but there are some people who specialize in finding loopholes in the law to do illegal things. Thus, even the law no longer exists, so the world is affected and corrupted.

As Buddhists, if we do not sincerely work and sacrifice for Buddhism, then how can Buddhism be widely promoted? We want to promote Buddhism, not learn some mantras, learn to have magical powers, learn Tantra, or learn strange and strange things, or learn about ghosts, séances, or learn to draw charms and wormwood. Therefore, the most important thing is to learn the precepts that Buddha left behind. If we can practice according to the teachings, then the Dharma will endure. If everyone does not keep the Buddha's precepts, that is the end of the Dharma. Because "It is created by the mind alone," everything is created by the mind, so the dharma is right in the human mind. Why do people go to the Dharma Ending Age? Because many people violate the precepts, few people keep the precepts; There are many people who know the precepts, but there are few who understand the precepts, which makes people confused. You say that person understands, but he doesn't completely understand. If you say he doesn't understand clearly, but he knows a little on the surface, only vaguely understanding a certain part.

What are precepts? It is "to prevent evil," that is, to stop evil and prevent mistakes, to help us not do all evil, and to prevent all mistakes. That is, "when the evil acts, the good serve," not doing evil deeds, but doing all good deeds.

Everyone understands that the Five Precepts taught by Buddha are important. Furthermore, the precepts also have a close relationship with each of us as individuals. If you keep the rules, don't be careless or lethargic, it means your self-nature is increasing in wisdom. By keeping the precepts, concentration can arise. Once concentration arises, it means having wisdom. If you don't keep the precepts, you won't have concentration, and if you don't have concentration, you won't have wisdom. Keeping the precepts is like a clear sky, ten thousand miles without a cloud. If you do not keep the precepts: Killing, stealing, adultery, false language, drinking alcohol, doing bad things and talking nonsense, it is like a dark cloud appearing in the clear sky. Once dark clouds appear, they will cover the sun, so you won't be able to see the light. Can't see the light, that's darkness; but darkness is ignorance. So much so that he lost his entire body, then crawled into the belly of a pig to become a pig, into the belly of a buffalo to become a buffalo, and into the belly of a horse to become a horse. These are all due to scientific achievements, the results of experiments in the chemical factory of human nature.

A person who keeps the precepts is a person who has pure self-nature and wipes away all darkness in self-nature. People who do not keep the precepts will have endless dark clouds. A day of not keeping the precepts is a day that gives birth to more dark clouds. People who do not keep the precepts, because of their own nature, are creating dark clouds of pollution. If you do not keep the precepts, it is not others who are injured, but your own nature that is injured. Therefore, you must strictly maintain the precepts. If you can keep the precepts, it is the Dharma; if you cannot keep the precepts, it is the end of the Dharma.

Lecture on July 9, 1986

Not Taking Credit

tieu_de: Transporting the Universe - Maintaining the Precepts / 257 Do not take credit for personal revenge /
tom_tat: In Buddhist teachings, towards people or towards things, we should rely on the Four Immeasurable Minds: Compassion, Joy and Equanimity as the basis. When dealing with anything, we can use two methods: extraction and photography. For example, a Bhikkhu…
noi_dung:
Transporting the Universe - Maintaining the Precepts / 257 Do not take credit for personal revenge /

In Buddhist teachings, towards people or towards things, we should rely on the Four Immeasurable Minds: Compassion, Joy and Equanimity as the basis. When dealing with anything, we can use two methods: extraction and photography. For example, if a Bhikkhu has a bad nature, people may hate him, ignore him, and not pay attention to him anymore. That is extremely difficult for Bhikkhus to educate. If there are some Bhikkhus who intentionally or unintentionally break the precepts and destroy the Dharma, then the Bhikkhus who uphold the precepts should help them with boundless love, compassion, joy, and equanimity. But sometimes they use the method of "control" to chase them away, such as changing places for the offender to live alone, so that he can repent and correct his mistakes and become a new person. There are also times when the "ha blame" method is used, which means scolding or reprimanding harshly. But we must not use public matters to take private revenge. We cannot, because we have a disagreement with someone, then look for faults and intentionally find fault with them. We must use integrity, not resentment, and not use a biased mind to preside over and handle public affairs. If you use public matters to take private revenge, for example, as soon as you see his face you immediately protest, that is a big mistake, extremely wrong.

For example, if you see someone you don't like, you slash him on the right, hammer him on the left, almost choking him to death, to get revenge! That's a big mistake! When we study Buddhist scriptures, we must be impartial. We are purely to help people, but we use two methods of "extracting and suppressing," either harshly scolding or using soft words to guide them. Those are all methods of helping people.

Especially when we arrive, we should not say that this person did what was wrong, and what that person did was also not right. If we say so, we have committed a cause and effect error. We should use our great kindness, impartiality, compassion, joy and forgiveness. If we know how to apply the two methods of extraction, then we are wise. If anyone doesn't know how to use it, he has evil knowledge. If you make a mistake, you'll be lost a thousand miles! Not doing wrong is legal, but doing wrong is illegal. But whenever it is illegal, it means creating criminal karma. The more crimes you create, the deeper the karma. The deeper the guilt, the more the resentment increases. For Buddhism, once one has committed resentment, there will be no escape in the future. In short, karma is tied tightly to the body. You want to practice, but evil obstacles come to you. Why? Because you are not fair. If we are fair, then everything will be good and as expected. If we are not fair, trouble will appear.

Lecture on July 20, 1986

Thien Ha Vi Cong, China town gate, San Francisco

Selfishness is a rock that blocks the feet of a cultivator

Cultivators like us easily develop a strong mind, but it is difficult to establish a will for eternity. That is to say, if you put your mind to it at the moment, anyone can do it to the fullest. But if you constantly reflect on your aspirations and goals every day to follow, that is not an easy thing to do. Because people cannot keep their minds constant and unchanging. Even though we clearly know that practicing is a good thing, after a long time we become lazy. We forget the spiritual mind, then let our selfishness take over all the power. If a cultivator can eliminate selfishness, there will be no problems and no troubles will remain. If you don't have a selfish mind, you won't fight, you won't be greedy, and you won't have expectations. You also won't have a big ego, you won't think about your own benefit, and you won't lie about anything.

Why do we have so many bad habits? It's because of that evil self-centered and selfish mind. Who is the enemy of the cultivator? In fact, the real enemy is not the Demon King, but the selfish mind. Our selfish mind is our evil knowledge. It makes us forget the spiritual mind. Once personal selfishness arises, every move, every word, every action is also selfish. That's why I don't succeed in anything I do, and everything I do is damaged. But if there is success, it is also an illusion, because that success is not achieved from wisdom and merit

true virtue.

Why do people not have true wisdom? Also because of selfishness, from beginning to end, people cannot achieve true wisdom. As time goes on, practitioners lose their minds and forget their original aspirations. That's why they keep dragging and dragging on without being completely decisive. That is the great obstacle of a cultivator. Where does that great obstacle come from? It is from selfishness that arises. If you can enlighten to the above sayings and chase away the lazy worms of leisure, then you will achieve a great harvest.

Lecture on July 28, 1986

The Identity of a Buddhist - Being Uncompromising and Non-A Dua

At the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, no one is allowed to flatter or say flattering words to others. In the past, why were some people reincarnated? Because they like to be flattered to “wear a high hat.” The monks here, including the new Phuong Truong, are all young people. If you flatter them, it means you want them to be reborn a little sooner.

At the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, we don't say anything about humanity. We absolutely only talk about Buddha Dharma, and do not bring out Buddha Dharma to give away in a worldly way, that is, to please people. I also do not allow disciples to take refuge in me, no matter how much I flatter them, let people "wear high hats" come there, that is the most evil behavior. My principle is not to praise anyone, nor to intentionally defame or criticize anyone. What I said is the truth, nothing more, nothing less. Therefore, at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, no one says "thank you" twice, it is called "The upright mind is the temple", the upright mind is that temple!

When I first bought the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, the disciples who took refuge with me were all afraid to approach me. They were afraid that I would be messy and wanted to donate money. They said: "That place is so big! It looks like within a year, he will definitely close and go bankrupt!"

However, I still cherish three great principles:

"If you're cold, you won't find fate, if you're hungry, you won't find fate, if you're poor, you'll die without finding fate."

I also don't bow my head or bow down to anyone. I tell you honestly: Not only do I not bow my head to others, but when I pay my respects to Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, I also never say: "Bodhisattvas! Please help me! This time I'm not done..." Even though it was both painful and difficult, I also shouldered the burden of overcoming it myself, without letting others know. Do I want to ask for people's pity? --- What kind of monastic person is like that! Because of this spirit, I dare to say: "San Francisco is not allowed to have an earthquake."

Lecture on July 29, 1986

Subjective Intellect

tieu_de: Selfishness is a rock that blocks the feet of a cultivator / 262 The Identity of a Buddhist - Steadfast Non-A Dua / 264 Subjective Intellect Drives Motivation /
tom_tat: The driving force behind the subjective intellect and this method of preaching the sutras has never existed before, but it cannot be said that in the future it will no longer exist. According to this method, each individual can develop his own understanding...
noi_dung:
Selfishness is a rock that blocks the feet of a cultivator / 262 The Identity of a Buddhist - Steadfast Non-A Dua / 264 Subjective Intellect Drives Motivation /

The driving force behind the subjective intellect and this method of preaching the sutras has never existed before, but it cannot be said that in the future it will no longer exist. According to this method, each individual can develop his or her own understanding, to speak his or her heart and express his or her own wisdom. I have listened to you speak the Dharma a lot. Although I cannot say that I have achieved many good things, the benefits I have received are not small.

For more than ten years, every day I have been a Buddhist monk preaching the Dharma to you. So now I am a beginner studying with you. This is truly inconceivable! Be a teacher and then a student. But if I were playing the role of a teacher, I wouldn't be able to do that. You need to pay attention to this point!
