If you don't come out to preach the Dharma, then I bow my head and pay my respects to you. If you still refuse to leave, I will kneel. Now there are many people competing to preach the sutra first. This skill cannot be achieved overnight. Listening to you preach the Dharma, I feel like I have the taste of nectar and the fullness of Dharma joy. In your lectures today, each person has their own strengths (strengths) and weaknesses (weaknesses). You should work together to complement the long and short, using the good things of others to compensate for your bad, that is, using an "eclectic" approach. If you feel that what you say is reasonable, you should encourage yourself even more. And if you don't preach as well as others, then don't be afraid to use other people's strengths to supplement your weaknesses. That is the spirit of learning so that we can develop more and more.

Most importantly, don't be complacent, brag about yourself, or become arrogant, otherwise these will become causes and conditions that hinder your path. Therefore, everyone should concentrate even more, take everyone's wisdom as their own wisdom, and everyone's understanding as their own understanding. Each individual can hear many others develop their own inherent intelligence. This method has never existed before, but who knows what the future holds.

Again, regarding how to request the Dharma, basically, no matter where we teach the Dharma, there should be someone who requests the Dharma. But nowadays there are some people who only know how to preach the Dharma, but don't know how to ask for the Dharma. Now the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas uses this method of requesting the Dharma to revive and flourish again, in order to restore the regulations set by the Buddha.

Studying the Dharma means that we should "be good at it," and if we are proficient, we want to be more proficient, and every day we should seek to make more progress. Don't find it difficult and then retreat, because if you do, we will never be able to clearly understand Buddha Dharma. Therefore, everyone has the opportunity to preach the scriptures, everyone has the opportunity to speak reasonable words of righteousness. Speaking fairly means we don't need to flatter or inflate each other, or promote or flatter each other. Otherwise, we will not be able to understand the true meaning of Buddha Dharma. Here we should be honest, we should speak the truth and talk about the truth. We should summarize, don't talk about the three kingdoms, embroidering flowers and weaving leaves. We just need to explain the true meaning of

The classics are clear, that's fine.

After listening to the sutra lecture, the male and female audience should each nominate one person to summarize and criticize. Criticism here is not with malicious intent, but with good intentions and constructive comments. If someone preaches incorrectly, you can also point it out to make it correct. That means honing, cultivating, and working together to correct incorrect understandings. Because insiders are often confused, while onlookers are often more alert. But don't flatter people or give people "high hats".

You have to "single-sword straight in," speak out bluntly and "open the gate," get right to the point. If you feel the criticism is unreasonable, you can still speak up. This is not an argument, but should be like "the first point to see the blood" is to say briefly, right to the important point to point out what is wrong. Only then can it be like forging in a big furnace to get pure gold. Just like at Shaolin Temple, practitioners must overcome the group of wooden people, where they train to achieve true kung fu. If they can't make it out of the battle, it means they have to start over from the beginning. If they can escape, that means they can ride the clouds and waves in the world to propagate Buddha Dharma. This is a good measure that can eliminate the appearance of ego. Don't think that because people criticize you, you feel ashamed, or that you point out other people's shortcomings but are afraid they won't be able to stand it. This is the truth and the truth, the truth is also the truth, it is honest and sincere, there must not be any impurity or impurity.

I believe that from ancient times to modern times, no one has preached the sutras in this way. But in the United States, it was especially opened in this formal style. America is a democratic country, so everyone should speak the truth with all their sincerity. We propagate Buddhism in the United States. Wherever we go, we should speak the truth, so that when we enter water we will not sink, when we enter fire we will not be burned, and we will not be harmed by swords and spears. Don't preach lies, don't say good things to please people, to make people sympathize with you. I speak the truth, even if you kill me, it's okay, it doesn't matter. We should have that spirit to speak the truth, even if we die, it will be a meaningful death. We should have that spirit of commenting, not worrying about what's ahead or being timid. Otherwise, we cannot understand Buddha Dharma.

“Destroying dharma wealth, destroying merit,

Mac is not due to self-consciousness."

(Edit Ca)

Harming the Dharma, destroying merit, is not due to the mind, will, or consciousness.

That means your mind, mind and consciousness will kill you.

"The mind is rejected by meditation." Through meditation, one abandons the mind. Therefore, people who meditate do not use their mind, thoughts, or consciousness. They don't think about anything, nor contemplate anything, but they often meditate with the question "Who is the one reciting Buddha's name?" This is them going upstream to return to their roots, finding their original origin, what they were originally? This is called: "Single-mindedness," concentrating to the extreme and suddenly becoming clear, enlightened, and achieving great wisdom. Nowadays, there are some people who fake enlightenment, or find people to prove that they are already enlightened. That's because everyone thinks that enlightenment is a good thing, and practitioners still haven't forgotten this good word. If you were told that an enlightened person would later turn into a dog, people probably wouldn't say they were enlightened! Claiming to be enlightened is like being ignorant to the extreme. Why do you want to advertise yourself to tell others? What does that mean? That is still to spread the fate, to bang the gong and beat the drum yourself. If we truly understand, we will not seek fame and profit, nor will we be selfish or self-seeking. Each person should work in the spirit of Buddhism, not afraid of this, afraid of that, afraid of falling leaves that will break their heads and brains.

The person who preaches the sutras should summarize it to the important points, without being confusing or confusing. The words you preach must definitely be related to the meaning of the sutra. You are not allowed to bring pre-written documents to the podium. When drawing lots (bamboo cards with registration), whoever's name is drawn, that person must definitely speak. You must not refuse, because that is against the law and does not respect the law. This is a divine mandate. Whoever's name is drawn correctly will have to speak. If you do not preach, that means you have done something against the public dharma.

No matter who you are, you must not say:

- I won't say anything today.

Anyone who behaves like that, no matter how well they preach, will not get any points. If you don't prepare, but you often lecture, then it counts. If you are prepared to give a lecture, it doesn't count. If you go to lecture and bring documents, you will not get any points. Why? Because it doesn't follow the rules! Picking up the paper and reading it is deceiving everyone and only causing more disturbance. Because you didn't pay attention to the lecture, you brought formal papers with you. Here we are not an "Open Book Test" that allows you to open a book.

When preaching: If you know, say what you know. If you don't know, don't say you know, don't pretend. If you don't know what the story is about, then why are you discussing magical theories? That's like swallowing all the books and you don't know anything, so what's the true value of saying it? So if you want to have a true mind and clear understanding, don't draw a snake with legs or do redundant things.

With this method of preaching the sutra, each person will develop their own inherent wisdom. When someone from the south side is preaching on the platform, the next person should sit under the platform to wait for his turn. The same goes for the female side. That way people won't be left thinking, "Whose turn will it be next?" If someone goes up front and waits, it will make everyone feel secure, and that person can also take this opportunity to be quiet for a moment to prepare to preach the Dharma. However, not everyone is speculating: "Whose turn will it be next?" But in the mass there are also people who are very impatient and restless.

"The world is all right, let people disturb themselves." There is nothing going on in the world, but stupid people want to find something to do. Therefore, in every situation they encounter, they are completely attached. This method of preaching the sutra is very natural, wise people see wisdom, benevolent people see benevolence, profound people see profoundness, shallow people see shallowness. Each person has their own strengths, and each person's teaching principles are also different. Now we will collect all those differences, then put them together in one furnace to refine them together, to gather the wisdom of sentient beings to form useful and profound thoughts. In this way, people without wisdom also become people with wisdom. Why? Because we have many opportunities to learn and wisdom will gradually arise. That is when everyone takes the long to make up for the short, based on logic and truth, we will very quickly penetrate the scriptures, wisdom like the sea. Once we have wisdom like the sea, no matter what problem we encounter, we can solve it as easily as splitting bamboo. Just like a mirror shows everything clearly, when things happen, they respond, when things pass, there is silence. This is very important for studying Buddhism.

One more point, when you are on the stage to practice preaching, if you have familiar speech patterns, or if you have any inappropriate gestures, you should leave them out. Here, on the one hand, we learn to preach the scriptures, and on the other hand, we learn how to lecture in front of the public. I see people making more and more progress every day, slowly walking on the right path. Again, people who don't know Chinese must speak Chinese, and people who don't know English must speak English.

There are many Westerners here. Before, they didn't know how to speak Chinese, but because they were forced to learn it, they can now. I have a disciple who loves eating candy, but he would rather not eat candy than quit learning to speak Chinese. Now he can speak. Here, Westerners should speak Chinese, Chinese people should speak English so that the East and West languages ​​can interact together as one. The minimum level you should know is two

language. If you can continue to learn a little more like Spanish, French, German, Italian..., then in the future it will be very convenient for you to go out and propagate Buddha Dharma. Please do not miss this point. I'm so ashamed that I don't know other languages. Like recently, when I went to Indonesia, because I didn't know Indonesian, I felt like I was deaf. You are young people, now you have the opportunity to practice, in the future you will be the pillars of Buddhism. That is the hope that I place on you.

Lecture on August 6, 1986

Capable of Maintaining Precepts

Cultivating Self-Nature

Once we have received the precepts, we need to keep them. Precepts mean: Evil people act, good people obey, meaning: Do not do bad deeds and do all good deeds. Precepts are also: Only prevent evil, meaning: stop, stop doing evil deeds and avoid making mistakes. After receiving the precepts, we must follow the basis: "Only evil prevents evil, evil acts and good beings serve" and follow, that is, we are keeping the precepts. From our thoughts to our actions, we should all try our best to stop doing bad things, and also do our best to do good things to help people. In every moment, you should guard against your own unreasonable and illegal thoughts and behaviors. That is the meaning of precepts. Buddhists who keep the precepts should pay attention to this point. So can you follow it?

After taking refuge in the Three Jewels, you should always maintain reverence for the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. Because everything is created by the mind, if the mind often respects the Three Jewels, over time it will naturally merge with the Three Jewels into Buddha, Dharma, Sangha and Precepts. If you have taken refuge in Buddha, when you see a Buddha statue, you should respect and worship it. Buddhist scriptures should also be kept above secular books and placed in a sacred place. It is best for Buddhist scriptures to be placed neatly and respectfully, not left on stairs or in the path of passersby, but should be left in a clean place. At all times, we should respect Buddha, Dharma, Sangha and Precepts, especially in our hearts, we should not have any contempt or contempt.

Maintaining the precepts means purifying one's own nature, it means sweeping away all the dark clouds in one's self-nature; Not keeping the precepts means endless dark clouds. If we don't keep the precepts, there will be more and more dark clouds, just like dark clouds in the sky. People who do not keep the precepts are creating black clouds of pollution in their own nature. If we don't keep the precepts, then it's not someone else who gets hurt, it's us who gets hurt, our own nature gets hurt. So we need to strictly keep the precepts. Maintaining the precepts is the Dharma; not maintaining the precepts is the end of the Dharma.

When listening to Buddhist teachings, we don't need to listen too much. The important thing is just to stop doing evil things, avoid sins, know and act often. “Do not do evil deeds, do good deeds,” is enough.

When the Buddha was about to enter Nirvana, Venerable Ananda asked the Buddha four questions. There was one thing that he asked such as: When Buddha was still alive, we worshiped Buddha as our teacher, but after Buddha entered Nirvana, who should we take as our teacher? At that time, Buddha spoke solemnly to his monastic and lay disciples: "Take the precepts as your teacher." So when we recite refuge, it is also the mindfulness of refuge in precepts, that is, taking precepts as our teacher.

If you want to truly study Buddhism, you must take precepts as your teacher, not saying precepts, precepts, precepts on your tongue, but precepts must be right in your heart. A person who does not violate the five precepts will have a bright and clear mind. As for people who violate the precepts, when you hear them talk, you know they have demons inside them, making it impossible for them to show their face and speak eloquently and with reason. Behind them there must be a string to pull, like a devil is pulling their tail, making them afraid!

No matter where I go, I don't understand why, even though I don't have any guns or weapons on my body, whenever people with evil principles and evil spirits see me, they are afraid. They were so scared that they were trembling and nervous, not even daring to speak, not even daring to look at my face. Today I tell you why! Because they don't keep the precepts and stay in the dark clouds all day, hiding in darkness and darkness, that's why they can't see the light. Not keeping the precepts is a sign of the End of Dharma. If you want to uphold the Dharma, you must keep the precepts. Keeping the precepts is not about telling others to keep them, but keeping them yourself. If you do not keep the precepts, your self-nature will be injured, and whenever your self-nature is injured, it is contaminated and dark, like a mirror covered with a lot of dust, so it cannot illuminate anyone.

Our self-nature is like a clear mirror. At our origin, we all have the Great Perfect Wisdom, the Wisdom of Creation, the Wisdom of Wonderful Observation, and the Wisdom of Equal Nature. Self-nature is immeasurable light, immeasurable clarity, but because of not keeping the precepts, the light cannot appear. So our memories are not good, everything is not good. Why are people stupid? Because of not keeping the precepts. Nowadays, there are still children with weak minds and low abilities. That's because they didn't keep the precepts in their previous lives, so they're as stupid as horses and buffaloes. Although they have a human body, they don't have a human mind.

Stupid and crazy people.

Just like today, someone came to ask me: What earth level is he a Bodhisattva? Right at the edge of the Bodhisattva, he couldn't even touch it, yet he still asked what level of Bodhisattva level he was? Would you say it's pitiful or not? People like that don't keep the precepts, so their nerves go crazy.

Buddha is a person of great wisdom, whoever has great wisdom will be exactly like Buddha. If we cannot become a Buddha, it is because we do not keep the precepts. Buddha always kept the precepts for all eternity, even as small as a thread, he did not violate them. Because of that, he attained the Buddha body, having Three Bodies, Four Wisdoms, Five Eyes, and Six Wisdoms. If everyone can "not do evil deeds and do all good deeds," then that means keeping the precepts.

Lecture on September 3, 1986

tieu_de: Precepts Have the Ability to Cultivate Self-nature / 274 Should Comment Fairly /
tom_tat: “Among all kinds of alms, Dharma almsgiving is the best.” That is the greatest kind of almsgiving, because it can achieve the Dharmakaya of Wisdom and Life for people, just like lighting a bright lamp in front of people. Therefore, the Buddha in…
noi_dung:
Precepts Have the Ability to Cultivate Self-nature / 274 Should Comment Fairly /

“Among all kinds of alms, Dharma almsgiving is the best.” That is the greatest kind of almsgiving, because it can achieve the Dharmakaya of Wisdom and Life for people, just like lighting a bright lamp in front of people. Therefore, throughout his life, Buddha did not do anything else, but only worried about preaching the Sutras and preaching the Dharma. We are disciples of Buddha, if we do not learn to preach the Sutras and preach the Dharma, if we do not learn to speak the truth, then what do we follow Buddha to learn?

Now, every evening when the sutras are lectured, everyone takes turns speaking, and at the end, there are people who give general comments. So this is more than giving Dharma in the ways of giving Dharma. For those who have not been on the right path, you should also slowly guide and help them get back on the right path. Therefore, commenting like this means you are practicing a part of the Bodhisattva path.

If you truly want to help others, truly want others to achieve success and practice Dharma giving, you should not be indifferent or not care about anyone; If not, then you are not a true practitioner. Remember that in the beginning, no one wanted to lecture, but now you understand everything. When you preach, don't be afraid, because no one will beat or kill you. Even when I criticize, it is with good intentions, not with malice. Like: “I feel like that person is not right so I have to overpower him.” On the contrary, we should support them, because we cannot bear to let them fall. Don't be like: you look at me, I look at you, then everyone is afraid to comment and criticize. Even if your comments are not correct, everyone can still hear your views and opinions. We should be "pure and pure," meaning that we are already pure but still want to be more pure, so that not a single residue remains, just like refining pure gold in a large furnace, it must be pure and not mixed with other impurities.

Right now you feel this is not important, but in the future when you go out to spread the Dharma, then you will know its importance. If you preach a little wrong, it can cause people to lose their Bodhi mind. If you preach correctly, you will make people develop Bodhi mind. So now we should practice honestly. We should not spin around the bush, or talk about it like writing literature. We just need to be able to explain the important meaning of the scriptures.

Lecture on September 28, 1986

Intellectual Training

In this Dharma conference, everyone has the opportunity to preach, so each person's wisdom is revealed, and each person's ignorance is also revealed. People who truly have wisdom, even if they want to hide it, won't hide it for long. At first they can hide for about five or three days, but over time they can no longer hide. And vice versa, stupid people want to pretend that they are smart, then pretend to be smart. But no matter how hard they try to study, it doesn't come naturally. This is the real survey! Now we add the last comment section again. If you talk nonsense, there will still be people who criticize you. But the person commenting must not be indifferent and should speak longer than the person giving the Dharma lecture.

Let's see, the ancients commented on literature like "drawing a dragon with its eyes", they only used a few simple but complete words, vast and vast. So we don't need to "draw snakes seriously", that is, draw snakes with legs, or pretend to "appear human but still have guts".

Everyone should consider carefully: Is that person's criticism accurate? Is that person's opinion true or false? Is that person the right person to show the way? But is he right or not right?

We train every day in the fiery furnace, so that not even a bit of dregs, a bit of dirty thread remains. If we are dedicated to studying Buddhism, no matter what other people say is correct or incorrect, we must listen attentively. Anyone who doesn't pay attention will fall asleep. This is a test, a challenge, whether true or false, all are trained to reveal everything.

Lecture on October 5, 1986

Attitude of Buddhist Students

Buddhism is a teaching from the world, so we do not criticize good or bad politics, or this or that party, because the Dharma is like that, the world's trend is like that. All things, all things, are speaking the Dharma. We can say: Everything is "cause and effect". From countless eons up to now, this cause has been sown, so it must produce that result, which is called: "like the visionary, the cause will be the result," that is, whatever you sow will reap the fruit, and there is not the slightest mistake. But according to the understanding of ordinary people, there is a distinction between right and wrong. We should not pay attention to the matter of "right or wrong," because that is the distinction that people themselves make. Therefore, we study the Buddha Dharma completely. because we want to study the ethics of Confucius, Lao Tzu and Buddhism. We do not discuss the actions of any political party, because we do not do politics. We also do not borrow from Buddhism to air our grievances.

To study Buddhism, first of all we must calm our grievances. We are not left-leaning, but we are not right-leaning either. That is our principle when teaching the Dharma.

Also, I don't like to be flattered, nor do I want anyone to praise me. I'm happy when people slander me, but I'm most bored when someone praises me in front of me. I don't want to deify myself, I am inherently like nothingness, no form, no form, no image, no east, west, south, north, no person, no self, no sentient beings, no recipient. So why is there a "self"? If I had a "self" I would not come to the United States. I didn't come here to dig for gold. In San Francisco, although it is called Cuu Kim Son (old gold mountain), I don't even want gold powder. I don't know how to speak English, I don't understand a word a, b, c. Then what did I come here for? Because I want to develop new land here, in order to spread Buddhism to the whole world. That is my will.

No matter where I am, I don't want to promote my status, nor do I want to stand out. I don't feel that I am taller than others, better than others, or more intelligent than others. If I think like that, I'm complacent, I'm done. Because a complacent person will definitely not achieve anything. People should be like “yes as well as nothing, real as well as unreal.” People who have morality are like people without morality, people who have wisdom are like people without wisdom, especially they should not be complacent.

Once people become complacent, they will become arrogant, and being arrogant becomes like the word "xu" which means stinking (the word "xu" is Chinese and includes the word "tu" and the word "dai" which means stinking). Therefore, we should all try our best to learn the Six Great Principles: Don't fight, don't be greedy, don't seek, don't be selfish, don't seek personal gain, and don't lie. We must do our best to follow these six principles. If you cannot practice these Six Great Principles, no matter what talent you have, you will not have true wisdom. Even if your tongue is as fluent as running water and your eloquence is flawless, I am not interested. I am someone who only knows honest people, but not cunning people. In the future, no matter who you are, you must be honest and don't think that you have anything outstanding. Or even if you are extraordinary and outstanding, you don't need to show off or show off that you are the best and second to none. That kind of person will not be able to exist in Buddhism, sooner or later they will fail. Therefore, I often tell you that in Buddhism, if you want to create merit, you must definitely learn the attitudes of the great virtuous people of ancient times: do not fight, do not seek, do not be greedy, do not be selfish, do not take personal advantage, do not lie, this is true to the status of a true student of the Buddha Dharma. Otherwise, no matter how well you preach, it won't be of any benefit.

You can only lie for a while, but you can't lie for a long time. So it is said: Long distance knows the horse's strength, long time knows the heart of the person. Cultivating the Way means cultivating what? It means focusing on one's own virtue.

Lecture on October 18, 1986

tieu_de: Cultivating Wisdom / 280 Attitudes of Buddhist Students / 282 What is the First Mindfulness?/
tom_tat: The Venerable replied: - That is, one original thought, without thinking, without using the mind, mind, or consciousness to understand clearly. All thoughts are of the human mind, not the Dao mind. The first thought is the first...
noi_dung:
Cultivating Wisdom / 280 Attitudes of Buddhist Students / 282 What is the First Mindfulness?/

The disciple asked: - What is the first thought?

The Venerable replied: - That is, one original thought, without thinking, without using the mind, mind, or consciousness to understand clearly. All thoughts are of the human mind, not the Dao mind. The first thought is the first truth, not falling into the second or third.

The disciple asked: - Normally, when we see delicious food, the first thought is to eat it; Or when we see a beautiful object, we immediately think of wanting it. Is that also the first emperor of righteousness?

The Venerable replied: - No! Don't make a mistake, it is called the First Remembrance because it is the opening of our original knowledge, it is revealed from our true mind, it is the Original Face of the Future. The idea of ​​greed for food and beauty belongs to the false mind and greedy mind, not the true mind. For example, if we are here studying the truth, that aspect belongs to yang. As for the mind of greed for food and beauty, it belongs to the yin aspect, so it cannot be called the first truth. The mind needs to follow the direction of truth and light, then it counts. The key is whether the upper reaches advancement or the lower reaches decline. We should know that people fall into hell because of the first thought, but that thought belongs to the evil, to the negative, to the lower world, so it can gradually push us step by step to hell. Therefore, we must clearly distinguish basic issues, and not discuss them in a chaotic general way.

The disciple asked: - Someone asked: "Buddhism says: The human body is difficult to gain, once the human body is lost, it will never be restored." So why is the world's population increasing so strongly today? It is clear that the number of people born is greater than the number of deaths, so how does Buddhism explain this?

The Venerable replied: - Currently, the population proliferation rate is high, but how do you know that the number of deaths of sentient beings is not more than the number of living people? There is no way to count this total accurately, nor can it be scientifically proven. That can only be said by example. When the Buddha was in this world, he once grabbed a handful of earth and said: Gaining a human body is like the soil in the palm of your hand, losing a human body is like the soil on this great earth. The number of people living in this world seems to be immeasurable, but how do you know that the number of people who are lost is not more than the number of people who are born?

The disciple asked: - Nowadays, an atomic bomb explosion can kill tens of thousands of people. So in the end, is there any way to calculate the death toll?

The Venerable replied: - In the past, the number of deaths was not as high as today. Nowadays, deaths from wind and fire accidents, car accidents, airplane accidents, wars and bombs cannot be counted. Furthermore, those who die, after losing their human bodies, most likely will not become human again. Or maybe they are reborn as ants, mosquitoes, or ferocious animals. How can science provide this quantity as evidence?

Parents give birth to a child, but why does the child suddenly become sentient? This is the most basic issue, but ordinary people carelessly ignore it and never research it. Although it is said that the current human population has increased dramatically, the number of sentient beings who have lost their human bodies is higher than before. In the past, there weren't many ants, mosquitoes and other harmful insects like this. How do you know that low-born, transformed or ovum-born beings are not deformed from humans?

After a person has lost his body, his spiritual nature will dissipate. A person's soul can transform into many animals, even into eighty-four thousand mosquitoes. Because that person's wisdom has been scattered, it becomes dull. If you want to restore your human body, it means they have to be re-refined in a "chemical factory," so it may take a long time.

Another point is that people who marry many times, after death their souls are divided into many pieces. For example, no matter how many times a woman marries a man, when she dies, an electric saw will cut her soul into so many pieces, to be divided among that many men. If a boy marries many girls, the retribution will be the same. There is also another big problem: abortion. Abortion is the loss of a human body. Currently, the number of deaths due to abortion is higher than the number of living people.

As for sentient beings, can their spiritual nature be restored? It's possible! If they meet someone who preaches the Dharma to them in a suitable way such as:

“The merit of preaching the Dharma,

The first point of the jade stone,”

That is, the Venerable Master Sanh preached the Dharma, even the stones nodded. That is, they can also restore their spiritual nature, but they must meet a Saint or Arhat to have such an opportunity.

Lecture on November 10, 1986

Purpose of Establishing a School

The school at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas has three levels: Duc Luong Primary School, Virtue Cultivation Secondary School and Dharma Realm University.

Duc Luong Primary School: - Is to educate students to become talented and outstanding pillars of society, to become honest and outstanding people of the country, but also to educate them to become outstanding elites of humanity, so it is called "Duc Luong."

Virtue Cultivation High School: - Because of our inherent human nature, we cannot say we do not have it, but it is not certain that we have it fully. Therefore, we need to cultivate blessings, cultivate wisdom, and cultivate virtue.

As there is a saying: "The act of filial piety is immortal," among all virtues, the act of filial piety is the most important. Therefore, Duc Luong Primary School promotes filial piety to parents, while Secondary School focuses on loyalty to the nation. We teach our children to first be filial to their family, and to go one step further to care for and protect the nation, so that they can prepare to serve the nation in the future. So now you need to establish virtue to become a person with good character. That's why it's called "Buddhist Virtue" High School.

Dharma Realm Buddhist University: - When virtue has been fully cultivated, then students enter university, and are educated at Dharma Realm University. I'm just afraid that you don't have the skills. If you are talented and capable, you can reach out to all humanity in the world to help and benefit all people. That is the founding principle of our school.

Lecture on January 15, 1987

The Foundations of Great Men

Dear young people, you should imitate the saints; the sages of previous generations, the great men with their heads held high and their feet on the ground; imitate great heroes of the past at home and abroad; the greatest leaders in the world, to pursue happiness for humanity. Therefore, when talking, you should be in high spirits, not be moody and not at all excited. The pride must be sky-high, always maintaining the spirit of a great hero. Now is the time for you to lay the foundation, you should start building your personality base well, so that in the future, you will serve all humanity in the world and bring benefits to all people.

If you want to set such a goal, you should not resign yourself to it - you are like trash. When you go up to preach, you should have an enthusiastic attitude, don't be shy, don't think that you speak well or not well. Whether it's good or not, it doesn't matter. Just say what you want to say in your heart, "The direct mind is the path," which also means you're speaking the truth. Don't say lies, don't say things to make people like you. You should say the words you want to say, don't say the words you don't want to say. So it should be: "Rich and noble people are not capable of lust," rich but not infatuated. Even in the future, when you become rich, you must maintain rules and order and not commit adultery.

And “I can't be poor,” meaning that no matter how poor my circumstances are, I will not change my spirit, or let my mission and goals waver.

"Impossible to subdue" means not to be subdued by any oppressive or seductive power. You should maintain your human attitude with strong, resilient will.

Now you should build the foundation of your personality, so that in the future you can become a great and heroic figure in the world. Now you should always keep this wish, in the future you will definitely have a vast and vast future, called: "Thousand miles of Peng", like a Peng bird soaring thousands of miles away!

Lecture on January 16, 1987

Students of Cultivation High School, City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, on the occasion of Respecting the Elderly at Gold Mountain Monastery.

tieu_de: The Purpose of Establishing a School / 289 Institutions of Great Men / 291 Setting out to do great things /
tom_tat: Our body, mind and work should also have a legitimate goal. The right goal is how we can help humanity in the future, to benefit the people, not telling people to come and benefit...
noi_dung:
The Purpose of Establishing a School / 289 Institutions of Great Men / 291 Setting out to do great things /

Our body, mind and work should also have a legitimate goal. The right goal is how we can help humanity in the future, to benefit the people, not to ask people to benefit us. If you ask others to benefit you, then you are a waste, a useless object, a person without ambition, hesitant and less decisive, a moody and moody person without excitement. Don't be like that, you should set goals on how to be a human being.

While in class, students should concentrate on studying and learning. You have to put in all your effort to learn English, and you have to put in the effort to learn Chinese. Don't let precious time pass by. Teenagers are the golden age, this is the time to set legitimate goals, in the future you will definitely become great people in the world. If you set lowly low-class goals, like wanting to become a doctor in the future to earn more money and enjoy yourself, then that is a misconception. Or if you decide that in the future you will become a scientist and research a bunch of monsters to control the world, that is also wrong knowledge and wrong views.

In short, no matter what you study, such as studying to be a doctor or studying science, it can help people and you need to use what you have learned to benefit people. Doctors should consider treating people's illnesses as their main goal, and not think making money is the priority. Scientists should research to invent new things that are beneficial to the world's people without causing harm. You should not just aim for money or personal enjoyment, because those are very vile thoughts!

People should have great thoughts and make great aspirations, not only know how to make money. You should know that the two words "fame and profit" have killed so many people in the world. Why is the world at war? Also because of this benefit and reputation. Why do people kill me, why do I kill people? Also because of this fame and benefit. It is true that the two words fame and fortune are influencing people to the point of confusion and insanity. Therefore, while studying, we must focus on "clarity" which means we must be clear about all principles; As for ethics and how to treat people, we must also be clear and transparent. (The Chinese words for wisdom and fame and fortune have the same pronunciation.)

People in the past did not go to school for fame and fortune, but today people go to school for fame and fortune. I passed the "doctor" degree, that is a "name"; we can earn a lot of money, that is a "benefit"; It all comes from those two names, fame and profit. The reason this world is corrupt is because of the corruption based on the word profit and fame. People live like they're drunk and die like they're dreaming because they seek fame and fortune. That's why the ancients said: "In this world there are only two types of people: one is seeking fame, the other is seeking profit." We remember not to follow those two types of people in search of fame and profit. No matter what, we remember the benefit of all humanity. You are still young today, if you can preserve the mindset of not seeking fame or profit, then the whole world will definitely benefit in the future.

Lecture on January 16, 1987

Knife of Blessings and Virtues Cuts the Hair of Troubles

Blessings and virtues cause afflictions to arise,

Wisdom seeks to defeat love.

Tung Kim emerges from the hammock of reincarnation,

Directly beast the supreme Bodhi.

Mean:

Dao of merit and virtue shaves the hair of afflictions

The sword of wisdom cuts the thread of love.

From now on, escape the net of samsara.

Straight to the unsurpassed Mahabodhi.

Today is the day to celebrate Amitabha Buddha's birth. We should know - Why do we have to hold an inauguration ceremony?

Because Amitabha Buddha has great kindness towards us sentient beings. He saves us from the sea of ​​suffering, He leads us to the Western world of Ultimate Bliss, which is a place where "there is no suffering, one receives all pleasures," there is no suffering, only enjoyment. If we could recite one hundred thousand Buddha names every day, then every day we would celebrate Buddha's birthday. At the time of death, the body is not sick or suffering, the mind is not attached, the mind is not crazy, like entering meditation, reborn in Ultimate Bliss.

Today there are people who have become monks, so I read the above verse to encourage them. Now I would like to briefly explain the meaning of the verse to you.

Knife of merit to shave hair of troubles: This knife can shave off the hair of a person who will become a monk, it must be blessed. Because monastics also need to have full virtue to be able to shave their hair. Therefore, people have virtue, but knives also have blessings. So from now on, this knife will be retired. We no longer use it for other things, but we should put it away carefully. In the future, when you build a stupa, you can bring these knives into the stupa and make offerings, considering them as Dharma treasures. Why do you have afflictions? Some people say: "I don't have any worries!" So unless your head has no hair, you won't be able to stop suffering. If you can cut your hair a little early, your afflictions will slowly be eliminated. Of course, it cannot be stopped immediately. If you say you can cut it off immediately, that's deceiving people. Affliction must be gradually stopped.

The sword of wisdom cuts the thread of love: The sword of wisdom must be used to cut the thread of love. What is love? That means missing your parents, missing your siblings, missing your children, missing the east, missing the west, missing the south, missing the north, all of these are love at work. If we can cut off love, we will have no obstacles, no terror, and no delusions. We don't even have dreams, so our spirit will be pure. But ordinary people are like lotus roots. Even though the roots are broken, the vine still lingers and never leaves.

Love is like that! For example, when a girl gets married, she will not be able to let go of her husband. But after giving birth, she could not leave her children, but on the contrary, she sometimes forgot her husband, and she did not even need her husband anymore. That's all just trouble. If we have no love, no closeness, no nearness or distance, then the world will unite into one great mass.

From now on, we must escape the net of samsara: From now on we must escape the six paths of samsara, and not be bound anymore.

Straight to Supreme Bodhi: Mahabodhi means Buddhahood.

The meaning of these four verses is not just to say to those who have just become monks today. Because if you can reflect and reconsider this meaning, you will also have a place to use it.

Lecture on January 18, 1987

Don't Go to the Road of Death

Today I will tell you a few short words, but they contain a lot of meaning. We all know that when people are born, they are forced to be born by their parents, and when they die, they are also forced to die by their parents. I believe that when everyone hears these words, they will be terrified. That's right, people are born from their parents, but they die from old age and illness. Then why did Master say death was forced by parents?

Correct! Your parents gave birth to you, but every day they urge you to get married. They say: "Older boys get married, older girls get married," so that means they force you into the path of death and nothing more. Parents have gone down the road of death themselves, and now they want their children to go down the same road of death as themselves. Parents first want to have children, and then they will tell their children: "Not having children is a big mistake." They want their children to also give birth to children, from this life to the next, continuously without interruption. When you give birth to a child, you also tell your child to die - because every time there is birth, there must be death. But the ultimate goal of studying Buddhism is to escape birth and death.

I have a disciple whose parents keep urging her to get married, but she refuses to be fooled. If I say this principle, you probably have never heard it or seen it before. Parents often tell their children: "The big story of your life is not over yet." What is called the big story of life? It tells you to go to the road of death. Parents go down this road of death themselves, and then want to force their children to follow in their footsteps. Because of this reason, the sky tilted and the earth collapsed, the world was in chaos.

Buddha Shakyamuni practiced for three great aeons, and finally he understood what things were like. That is, "Birth" is not a good thing, "Death" is also not a good thing. That's why Buddha wanted no birth and no death. But his father, King Tinh Phan, was an old fool who insisted on getting Buddha married. Although Buddha had a wife when he was crown prince, he did not get married. Someone asked: So why does He have children? I have no way to tell you this argument.

Prince Siddhartha was fed up with living in the palace, so one night, he rode away on horseback. The four Heavenly Kings each lifted the Crown Prince's horse's hooves so that he could ride high in the air. Arriving at Tuyet Son, the Buddha practiced asceticism for six years there. In Tuyet Son it is very cold, there is no heating or hot water. That place is not as comfortable as we are now, where we can shower every day. At Tuyet Son, Buddha ate only one sesame seed and one barley grain every day and practiced single-mindedly. And so he diligently practiced asceticism for six years. Then he went to the Bodhi tree to meditate for forty-nine days. One night, he saw a bright star and realized the Way.

Buddha's enlightenment was that he did not want to die confused. So He left behind this path and allowed people to become monks, so as not to be forced by their parents to follow the path of death. Therefore, those who become monks learn to follow the path of success that Buddha took.

Today is December 8th, usually

We have the custom of eating "Lap bowl chuc," which means milk porridge. Because on this very day, Buddha also started drinking milk porridge. However, according to the customs of Tung Lam pagodas in China, it is the day that they eat "eight treasures porridge". I don't know how many ingredients they use to cook this dish. Because I don't have enough merit, I haven't eaten yet. If you follow me, you should not eat either. It's just that eating porridge or not eating porridge is not a big issue, it's mainly a matter of Buddha's teachings. People are greedy, Buddha is not greedy, people like beautiful things, Buddha does not like beautiful things. Buddha is a person who has gone astray and knows how to turn back, let go of everything, abandon all delusion and retain the truth. Therefore, he attained enlightenment, clearly understood all the appearances of the world, and the dharma was like that. Today, those who come to celebrate Buddha's enlightenment day should take Buddha's wish as their own wish. Let's find a way out of birth and death, not on the path of death.

Lecture on February 7, 1987

Lectures and Commentaries -

Don't Talk About Your Lover's Face

Here, preaching the sutras and preaching the Dharma is done by drawing lots using bamboo cards with names already written on them. Whoever's name is drawn, that person should quickly go to the stage first to prepare. Don't wait for the previous person to finish speaking before you go up, because that will waste all your time. Even if you don't know how to preach, just go up and say a few quick sentences, then quickly go down to take someone else's turn to preach. You can study little by little like that.

If anyone preaches wrongly, everyone should correct it.

Don't think:

- I'm afraid to say people's faults because I'm afraid they won't be happy.

Here, anyone who preaches wrongly and has someone point it out to correct him or her should happily accept it. Everyone should encourage each other and help each other.

Here we are not talking about love and face, and we are also not talking about feelings or respect for anyone. Even if someone says something wrong, everyone can go up to correct it, don't be too attached to the matter of face. We should help each other speak the truth. Don't be like other places where you flatter me, I flatter you, but lie to each other.

When it comes time to criticize, you should speak the truth, not just because you want to please everyone but say good things. No matter who they are, if they only like to hear good words, that person is done with it.

Because he will not make progress, he will not be able to learn anything anymore, and the Bodhi tree will also wither. Therefore, we should accept criticism from others, so we can improve every day.

Lecture on March 30, 1987

Young people should develop the mind to save the world

The Venerable Master gave a lecture at the research department at the University of Oregon.

Dear intellectuals, professors and students:

Today, everyone has the good fortune to gather together in the same lecture hall to discuss the topic "What are the necessities of human life?" Why did we come to this world? Do we come to this world simply to eat, to wear, to sleep, or to enjoy it? If we don't pay attention, these issues seem very simple, but if we study them carefully, they are not that simple. So what is our saving work to this world? What is the responsibility? Each person should seriously discuss clearly. If you don't realize it clearly, then this human life has no meaning or value. Therefore, we need to know clearly how to fulfill our responsibilities and how to complete our tasks well.

First, we must learn how to fulfill our innate vocation and human duties. Newly born babies only know how to cry and eat. They don't know what their future mission is. Then over time, days pass and they mature. Parents send them to school to learn about human responsibilities, to prepare them for what they will do in the future

Complete your duties diligently.

Regarding learning, each person has many aspirations. Some people study for "reason" to understand morality; There are people who study for "fame and profit", so that in the future they can show off their talents and gain a good reputation (ming li and fame and fortune are pronounced the same in Chinese, both are "ming li", but the writing is different); Some people study so that they can become rich in the future and gain great benefits. They don't care about understanding or not understanding morality, legality or illegality. They don't care about tricks as long as they can make money and maintain power. There are people who want to be leaders, want to be leaders too. But first you must know how to be a human being. Ask yourself, are you qualified to be human? As a matter of fact, I already know clearly how to be a human being, which means I can be a role model for others, and in the future I will not be ashamed to be a leader. If you still have the mind of competition, greed, pursuit, selfishness, self-interest, lying, always looking outward in pursuit, wanting to be a leader only to seek blessings for yourself, but not for the happiness of others, then you are on the wrong path. To be a leader, one must be "unselfish in treating others," condescending to entertain others, or "unselfishly treating others," which means looking down on oneself, but treating others kindly, for the benefit of all humanity.

What is human responsibility? I should contribute, help the whole world and benefit everyone in the world. That is the responsibility of each of us to be righteous people. But we don't just want to eat well, dress beautifully, or live in a luxurious home.

Throughout the world, if there are people who don't have food to eat, no

I have clothes to wear, so I feel sorry for that person, because I didn't dedicate myself to helping that person. The true responsibility of being a human being is to be truly for the benefit of others. If we want to have merit in life and benefit the people, we should shoulder responsibility and not push others. If everyone had that kind of mind, the world would definitely be peaceful and war-free.

First of all, we should be good teachers and role models and not compete with others. Why is this world corrupt? Because people compete for power, profit, and fame. We should give good things to others, and we should accept things they don't want, and we shouldn't compete with anyone. If everyone did not fight, the world would definitely be peaceful. Ordinary people are greedy, but we are not greedy. Don't follow the crazy trends of the world. Be a strong torch in a strong wind. Be like pure gold in a fiery furnace. Depending on fate but not changing; does not change but depends on fate; maintain your principles, secretly change to influence everyone to obey, not to fight, not to be greedy, not to seek, not to be selfish, not to benefit, and not to lie. If you can do that, the world will definitely be peaceful.

The starting point is self-cultivation. When you don't fight with yourself inside, then all the crazy delusions don't arise. Peace and quiet are true pleasure. By being calm and happy yourself, you can influence those around you to be calm and happy as well. When everyone lives together peacefully, the world will no longer have war. Why is the world at war? Because in the human heart there is struggle. If the human mind is at peace, the world will be at peace. If people's minds are dissatisfied, the world will not be peaceful. We, young and old, after knowing this principle, we will not gamble, get addicted, set fires, rob, or rape. If you want the world to be good, you must start with yourself first. If we are not good, how can the world be good? We should not expertly point the finger at others, saying: Why don't they keep rules and regulations? We should ask ourselves first: "Do I keep the rules?" Young people should take on this responsibility. If young people don't do well, how can the world be good?

Young people learn from the teachings of professors and teachers to follow the right path. But if they encounter a bad teacher who only teaches the children wrong knowledge and wrong views, then the young people will also learn badly. As the saying goes: "Close to ink, it's black, close to the light, it's bright", so choosing friends and finding teachers are extremely important issues. Young people with ability and achievements should be clearly aware of their responsibilities, not be selfish people who only care about themselves. The responsibility of being a human being is to contribute to life, to be beneficial to the people, and to benefit all humanity. I originally wanted to shoulder the responsibility of saving lives, to help all humanity in the world achieve success, but I am old and do not have enough strength. Therefore, I send this hope to capable young men, that you should develop the mind to save lives, and seek happiness for all humanity.

Hello talented young people! We should sincerely make great vows and great powers to help all humanity be happy. Help those who are in floods and fires so that they can leave suffering and be happy. First, you should learn yourself: don't smoke, don't drink alcohol, don't get angry, don't kill, don't steal, don't commit adultery, don't lie, don't eat meat, don't gamble, don't smoke drugs. You should learn to do righteous things. If you can do so, humanity throughout the world will be saved. Wherever I go, I call, exhort, and hope that young people will be enlightened, develop great compassion, great joy, great renunciation, and imitate the ambition to save the world like that of Jesus Christ, Shakyamuni Buddha, and all the Saints. If so, even if the world is not peaceful, it will still be peaceful.

You can study what I said today. Whether it's true or not, I don't know. But I am a person who deeply desires and wishes for world peace, and hopes that humanity in the world will not suffer. But if you want to fulfill this ideal, you must have wisdom to be able to do it.

Lecture on April 4, 1987

Cause and Effect Retribution -

To Hao Not Wrong

Venerable Master Tuyen Hoa gave a lecture at the University of Oregon

Namo reaches the end of space and transforms the dharma realms of the ten directions, three worlds, and immeasurable, endless Buddhas.

Namo ends the void and transforms the dharma realms of the ten directions and three worlds, which are immeasurable and endless, all respecting the Dharma.

Namo reaches the end of space and transforms the dharma realms of the ten directions and three worlds forever, immeasurable and boundless, all Sages and Monks.

Namo ends the void and transforms the dharma realms of the ten directions, three worlds, and always abides immeasurably and endlessly.

Namo Tathagata: Offering Offerings, Perfectly Enlightened Knowledge, Complete Wisdom and Conduct, Good Oath, Understanding the World, Supreme Being, Regulating Men, Master of Heaven and Man, Buddha, World-Honored One.

Buddhism focuses on cause and effect, because the cycle of retribution does not deviate by an inch. Whatever you sow, you will reap. Planting good causes brings good results, planting evil causes brings bad results. If we sow the cause of scolding others, we will be beaten by others. If we sow the cause of hitting others, in the future we will reap the retribution of being killed. The ancients said: "If you kill your father, you will kill your father; if you kill your brother, you will kill your brother." Whatever the cause, whatever the effect. Sentient beings like us are afraid of results, not of causes. When we sow the seeds, we are not careful. Only when we reap the rewards do we become worried and restless. On the contrary, Bodhisattvas fear the cause, not the effect. Bodhisattvas are very careful when sowing causes, so when the retribution comes, the Bodhisattva voluntarily accepts that retribution, not avoiding it. The difference between the thoughts of living beings and Bodhisattvas lies in this.

If a person's heart is generous, the blessings will be generous, but if the heart is narrow, the blessings will be small. Generosity means the nucleus is great, the future results will be great. We should know that: "Everything is created by the mind." The ancients said the word "Mind" as follows:

"Three points are like a star cluster, The sentence is like a moon, The flying fox tries to start, The Buddha's work is like a constellation of stars, The hook is curved like a crescent moon, Wearing a fur coat is from here, Becoming a Buddha is also because of it.

Therefore we should not do evil things, but do all good deeds. Becoming a Buddha is also due to a single thought in the mind. However, humans cannot control their own minds. Even though the mind is inside, it often runs outside. Delusional thoughts can take us as far as heaven or hell, or as close as New York or San Francisco. Ultimately, we cannot control our own minds. Cultivating the Way means cultivating one thought in one's own mind. If we can bring a single thought to one place and focus on it, then it's okay, and there's no need to discuss it anymore.

Lecture on May 3, 1987

tom_tat: People in life always look for the fake, but not the real. They all want to be deceived. If you want to tell the truth, people won't believe you. For example, there are people who specialize in talking about the way to get rich, they claim that anyone who comes to listen...
noi_dung:
Dao of Blessings and Virtues to Cut Off the Hair of Troubles / 295 Don't Go to the Road of Death / 298 Lecture Sutras and Commentaries Don't Talk About Personality and Personality / 301 Young People Should Develop the Heart of Salvation / 303 Karma and Retribution - Su Hao Is Not Wrong / 308 The Way to Generate Wealth /

People in life always look for the fake, but not the real. They all want to be deceived. If you want to tell the truth, people won't believe you. For example, there are people who specialize in talking about the Dharma to get rich, they claim that whoever comes to listen to that Dharma to get rich will become rich. So the people who came to listen didn't know how much it was. But if you speak the true Dharma, no one will listen, because listening cannot make you rich. If you tell lies to deceive people, you will make a fortune. So how to get rich?

It's so simple, even if I say it, I can't describe this miracle. Like all those who came to listen to the Dharma to get rich, first each person took out a hundred dollars, then they visualized this hundred turning into a hundred thousand, thousands, thousands, thousands of thousands - the more the better - until this hundred dollars radiated out and they became rich. People who learn this magic must first hand over one hundred dollars.

Think about it, who will get rich as a result? Of course, those who preach the Dharma will make a fortune. If one thousand people come to listen to the Dharma, that means they will collect one hundred thousand dollars. But in the end, it's not you who gets rich, but the one who deceives others who gets rich. That's why it's miserable! That's called accepting the fake, but not accepting the real. Think about it, in the end, who gets rich?

Just look at this world, although the number of people coming to worship in churches is not small, it is not the same as in cinemas, dance clubs and gambling places, where the number of people there is always larger. Think about it, what is the morality? That's because people accept the fake but not the real. They view fake stories as important, on the contrary, they don't pay attention to real stories. It is also due to greed, competitiveness, in the heart there is desire, selfishness, self-interest, the mind that likes to lie is doing mischief. So they keep following those unrighteous paths.

Lecture on May 5, 198

The Path of Mindfulness & Right View at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas

tieu_de: People Are Inherently Intellectual /
tom_tat: Only people with wisdom have true pleasure. People without wisdom cannot achieve true happiness. A wise person can clearly distinguish between right and left, and will not get confused between black and white. Have…
noi_dung:
People Are Inherently Intellectual /

Only people with wisdom have true pleasure. People without wisdom cannot achieve true happiness. A wise person can clearly distinguish between right and left, and will not get confused between black and white. If you have wisdom, you will not be stupid. If we know how to apply effort, we can turn ignorance into wisdom; If we don't know, we will turn our wisdom into ignorance. That's a very simple argument, as easy as turning a finger. If you recognize the three sufferings, know the eight sufferings and immeasurable sufferings, then you will be wise and not be surrounded by suffering. All religions teach us to destroy attachments to generate wisdom. The concept of true religions and scholars is not to make sectarian, racial, nationalistic, black or white, or right or wrong beliefs. They are outstanding people, outstanding with great vows, great virtues, great wisdom, great compassion, great joy and great forgiveness. That's why their spirit can soar into the void and spread throughout the dharma world. Buddha Shakyamuni said: "All living beings have Buddha nature and can become Buddhas." All sentient beings have wisdom, can achieve their inherent wisdom, and all have great wisdom, endlessly deep and wide, immeasurable and boundless, just like Buddha. Buddha never said, only He can become a Buddha, only He can have wisdom. On the contrary, he said that if you are a living being, you are qualified to become a Buddha.

Living beings are not simply human beings, but also include all fetuses, ovum beings, lower beings, transformed beings, including animals that can fly, dive, walk and have blood, all of which can become Buddhas. Some people say: "I don't want to become a Buddha." However, when you become a Buddha, you must also become one, unless you are not a living being. Buddhism is extremely vast and extremely sophisticated, there is no self, no people, no sentient beings, no followers, and no concepts of nationality, religion or faction. And that's not to say that if you don't believe in Buddha, you can't become a Buddha. No matter whether you believe or not, you can become a Buddha. As long as you practice, do nothing evil, do all good deeds, return to your origin, you will become a person of great wisdom and great wisdom. Speaking of which, I have a very simple verse, now I would like to read it to you:

The Dharma Realm is microscopic and exists outside,

Nothingness is used without tolerance,

All things are equal and separate from each other,

One thought, no birth, no speech.

Mean:

The Dharma Realm is the substance, what else is there?

Nothing is intolerant of nothingness.

All things are equal without distinction,

Not a single thought arises, no words.

The Dharma Realm is a microcosm of existence: There are ten Dharma Realms, including the Four Saints: Buddha, Bodhisattva, Pratyekabuddha, Sravaka and Luc Pham: Heaven, Human, Asura, Hell, Hungry Ghosts, Animals. These ten dharma realms include both sentient and inanimate and all have the same full wisdom and can all become Buddhas. Taking the Dharma Realm as the essence, then what else is there outside the Dharma Realm? Therefore, it is said: "The outside world" means what else is outside?

The use of nothingness has no use: It means that nothingness is of great use, you should not think that nothingness is useless. All mountains, rivers, land, houses, rooms, flowers, trees, forests, all living things exist in the void. If there was no emptiness, then there would be a vacuum, no people, no living beings - all of it would be endless. The reason humans exist is because there is nothingness. Emptiness is our best food, it provides nutrients and promotes our growth, no sentient being lives outside the void.

All things are equal without distinction: All things are inherently equal. Whoever does good deeds has merit that will go up, whoever does bad karma will inevitably go down, this is very fair. So we should not use our delusional minds to differentiate. If we don't have true wisdom, we won't be able to distinguish clearly when facing things. For example, learning a foreign language, if you don't have intelligence, you will learn this but forget that. But, is that why I don't want to study anymore? That's not the case, we should learn how to get rid of false thoughts, we must use our true mind to learn; Don't use hope to find hope. We must clearly understand the truth, only then will it have value. We should not let our lives pass in a confused manner.

One thought does not arise, absolutely no words: When you can not give birth to a single thought, your true mind will appear immediately, and absolutely cannot be described using your mind or language. Just like: "The mouth wants to speak but the words disappear, the mind wants the relationship but thinks it is lost."

Lecture on May 8, 1987

How To Be Free From Birth And Death?

Most of us are born into this world, not knowing what to do; We are born confused, then we die confused. During the period of birth and death, we go crazy for fame, go crazy for profit, go crazy for beauty, go crazy for good food, go crazy for enjoyment. Why are we crazy? Because we are not aware of our duties as human beings, suddenly we are born in heaven and suddenly go to hell. From birth until death, we never think about praying to know the truth, to clearly understand the basic meaning of being human. But we run after sound, chase after form, and then let ourselves wander in sound, form, fame, and profit. We only know how to earn money every day to maintain life, but we do not fully understand what we live for. If it's simply for the sake of eating, dressing, and sleeping like that, then what value does living have? Because everyone does not bring this issue out to clarify, they live confused, then die confused. At the time of death, people are still attached to this and that, their sons and daughters, and their property is left for nothing. But, even if they can't let go, they can't do anything. When you die, you must die!

Studying Buddhism is to understand clearly the process of birth and death, and then we practice to liberate birth and death. If we don't clearly understand the matter of life and death, nothing we do will have any meaning. Therefore, as students of Buddhism, you should first clearly understand this basic issue. You must clearly understand how to live, how to die, and clearly understand your duties as a human being. If you understand these tasks clearly, you will not be confused. The ancients said:

A time of joy, a time of sorrow,

Not in the human world, running away for a while,

Never come back, never go away,

The heron has no joy, the heron has no compassion.

Mean:

Coming is happy, leaving is sad,

It's not enough to walk through life, It's better to not come or go, To be neither happy nor sad.

A time of joy: When a child is born, in any family, everyone is very happy. Past times of sadness: When someone dies, everyone in the family is very sad and cries loudly. When it's time to laugh, when it's time to leave, it's time to cry. But when the child was born he cried, and when he left he did not forget to cry. We are happy when we see children being born. When we see people die, we cry. When a baby dies, we also cry. When an old person dies, we also cry. When a middle-aged person dies, we also cry. When the wife dies, the husband cries. When the husband dies, the wife cries. After all, what is the point of crying? That's called a map.

It's not because the world is fleeting: In this life, we don't understand anything. When we come we don't, when we leave we don't, we either don't gain any more profit or lose any capital. What capital loss is this? People who live in this world and do good deeds will be promoted, but if they create bad karma, they will be demoted. People who do not do good deeds, or do not cause bad karma, will neither go up nor down. They will not go to heaven, nor will they go to hell, but they will still continue to rotate in the chemical factory of the human world.

We humans are a small chemical factory. When we put a little more in our thoughts, that little bit will turn into documents. If we increase our good merits, we will ascend to heaven to become a heavenly person, or become a human being in the human world, or become an Asura. If we commit evil karma, we must fall into hell as a hungry ghost or an animal. If I neither go to heaven nor go to hell, then I will live a normal life on earth. In this life, we eat a lot, wear a lot, sleep a lot, so in the end, what do we get? It's still the same as coming empty-handed and leaving empty-handed. Therefore, the verse says: After a lifetime, there is nothing.

Never come back, never go away: For such a life, what is the meaning of our living in the end? It doesn't make any sense. Therefore: "If you don't come, don't go."

Heron without joy, heron without sorrow: If we had not come, there would have been no joy, nor sorrow. Isn't that so peaceful? But people are not willing to endure silence. There's nothing going on, people are still trying to find something to do. Therefore, everyone remains in the six realms of samsara, moving back and forth, birth and death, death and birth again, and staying there becomes a confused person. You say they understand. But what do they understand? I don't believe they understand. They only understand the illusion and impermanence of the world, so their minds are often depressed and often not happy. Please tell me, what is the purpose of living like that? If we can understand that being human has no meaning, then we should find the true meaning of what being human is.

Personally, I feel: "Human life is as impermanent as breathing in and out." Once upon a time there were three old men. One is ninety years old, one is eighty years old and one is seventy years old. Three old men gathered together to have fun at the party. The seventy-year-old man said: "This year, everyone will be at the banquet table. I wonder who will be missing next year?" He said that this year the three of us will happily eat and drink together, but we don't know who will be absent next year. The eighty-year-old said: "What you are talking about is so far-fetched! Today I can take off my shoes and socks, I wonder if I can put them on tomorrow?" That means I took off my shoes and socks tonight, but it's not certain that I can still wear them tomorrow. The ninety year old man said: "You're talking too far away. I don't know if the breath I just exhaled will come back or not!" I can say that because this man is already ninety years old. Let us each meditate on the discussions of these three old men. Can we be sure that we will not die?

There was a middle-aged man who, after his death, came to see the King of Hell and said: "I'm still young and in good health, so why did you call me down here? I can still do a lot of things. Why did you call me down here without giving me any prior notice? Either you sent me a telegram or wrote me a letter so I could prepare. Now you're asking me to come here, it's unreasonable!"

The King of Hell then said: "I have sent you letters several times, but you have neglected to pay attention to them."

The middle-aged man asked: "When did you send me the letter?"

The King of Hell replied: "I sent you the first letter when your neighbor just gave birth, but two days later the baby died. Do you think you will die too?"

The middle-aged man replied: "Ah! Is that letter addressed to me? I don't recognize words like that, and I also don't know how to read poetry. What about the second letter?"

The King of Hell said: "You have seen many people your age die, that is the second poem."

"But I never thought I would die too. What about the third letter?"

King of Hell continued: "You have seen old people with deaf ears and lost teeth, so why aren't you a little more careful? Do you think that in the future it will also be your turn?"

After listening, the middle-aged man bowed his head sadly and did not say a word.

Each of us will eventually receive these letters, but everyone doesn't pay attention. If you pay attention, what is the benefit? Do we have any method? We should try to study Buddha and learn to escape birth and death. Regarding birth and death, we must be sure that we will be free to live and die. Many people talk about freedom, but that is fake freedom. As for birth and death, freedom means you can live as long as you want; If I want to die, I will die at any time. If you say it, you will come, if you say it, you will go. I know where I come from; Wherever I go, I'm fine. We study Buddhism because we want to be able to move freely - life and death are up to us, even the King of Hell cannot control us. No matter how many telegrams and letters he sends, I don't care. If we want to be free from birth and death, where should we start? This is very simple, but nothing magical. We also don't need to recite many mantras every day to send to the King of Hell. Here I have Luc Dai Tong Chi. If you take these six great teachings as a basis and train your body and mind, you will be free from birth and death.

Luc Dai Tong Chi means:

1 - Not fighting: Not fighting means not even getting angry. A little anger is not okay. I don't get angry with anyone. If you don't get angry, sadness and ignorance will also decrease. When afflictions end, wisdom will arise, and we treat everyone with compassion.

2 - Not greedy: Not greedy for wealth or beauty; I'm not greedy for fame or profit, I'm not greedy for anything. But you should: Whatever you need, I will give it to you.

3 - Don't seek: Don't pursue outside things, you absolutely don't need things that you shouldn't have.

4 - Not being selfish: The reason we cannot become Buddha and fall into the three evil paths is also because of selfishness. If we don't have selfishness, then there won't be any karma.

5 - No self-interest: We should not seek personal gain

but regardless of tricks to do many illegal things, or do things that harm others.

6 - Do not lie: That is, tell the truth. We never lie to others, or say things that sound true but are false.

I also said the Six Great Tongs of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas for the sake of the two masters, Three Steps and One Bow. But until today, even though they have stopped the Three Steps One Bow, they still haven't practiced much. At the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, everyone talks about this Six Great Tongs. Whoever can practice fully will leave the three realms and become a Buddha. If you cannot practice on your own, you should not blame others for not helping you. My understanding is in this Six Great Tong Chi. No matter what you do, if you can keep according to the Six Great Principles, you will not create karma. That is the most basic condition to become a Buddha. If we can do this, the world will be at peace. When people and people don't fight with each other, how can this world not be peaceful? There is no greed between people, like I don't want what's yours, nor am I greedy for improper possessions, then everyone will live together in peace. Once everyone is not greedy, not seeking, not fighting, not selfish, not self-seeking, not lying, then the natural world will be peaceful and there will forever be no conflict. Those of you who study Buddhism should first be clearly aware of these basic conditions. Only then will you receive many great benefits from studying Buddhism.

Lecture on June 13, 1987
