tom_tat: Some people want to know about my past life, so now I will outline a few points for you to understand. I was born in the Northeast and became a monk from there. Then I was blown by the wind of karma to Tianjin, then blew...
noi_dung:
How To Be Free From Birth And Death? / 315 Monks in the Grave /

Some people want to know about my past life, so now I will outline a few points for you to understand. I was born in the Northeast and became a monk from there. After that, I was blown by the wind of karma to Tianjin, then blown to Wuhan, Hubei, Putuo Mountain, and Suzhou Lingyan Mountain. Then it brought me to Guangdong to Nam Hoa Temple, and to be close to Venerable Master Hu Yun.

In 1950, I went to Hong Kong again. And in Hong Kong, I had a relationship that was neither big nor small. During my time in seclusion there, I had very little contact with outsiders. In 1962, I went to the United States alone again.

When I first arrived in San Francisco, USA, life there was very miserable. I live in a basement room. In this cellar there is a door, but no window, so sunlight cannot penetrate. Besides, that place was very damp, just like a grave. Therefore, I gave myself the name "Mo Trung Tang," which means Master in the Tomb. Even though I'm still alive, I'm like a dead person, which means I don't dispute with anyone. Whatever people like to do, I won't fight and just let them do it. I collect things that people don't like, or things that are not good, just like picking up trash.

I stayed in that "grave" for six years. By the summer of 1968, the fate of achievement was that from the Seattle area, thirty or forty students with all degrees: doctors, masters, scholars, invited me to lecture on the Shurangama Sutra. So I crawled out of the grave to begin spreading Buddhism in the West.

I would also like to say more about my aspirations and implementation of translating the scriptures. I am a talented, uneducated person who only attended school for two and a half years in my entire life. I entered school at the age of fifteen, but dropped out of school at the age of seventeen.

When I was fifteen years old, I started going to school. When I was sixteen or seventeen years old, I joined the Ethical Society. At the age of sixteen, I preached the Six Patriarchs Platform Sutra. If an uneducated and unskilled person like me knows how to preach sutras, do you think it's funny or not?

When I was in the Northeast, I often observed how other religions spread their teachings. For example, Catholicism and Protestantism, I see that their teachings are widely spread and have many followers. The main reason is because they translated the Bible into many languages ​​around the world and disseminated it widely. The writing and doctrine in the Bible are concise, clear, and easy to understand. Furthermore, their entire teachings have been condensed and condensed into one Bible, without any frills, making it easy for many people to accept. That is a big factor why Catholicism and Protestantism are so popular. There is another big factor that also helps them succeed: they promote education. They established many schools to spread the teachings, so it had a very widespread influence.

Through this consideration, I decided that: If we want to revive the Buddha Dharma, we must start from two aspects such as: self-propagating and promoting the sutras and promoting education. Because of that, I soon made a vow to translate the Tripitaka into foreign languages, in order to spread it to the whole world.

Translating the Tripitaka is a very difficult task. In the past, this was all due to the dedicated support of the King and his mandarins, not the ability of a few common people. I am a person who does not measure myself. As for me, I don't understand a single foreign language, yet I want to take on this great responsibility. Since I don't understand foreign languages, how can I translate? I then went to scholars who knew foreign languages ​​to bow or pay their respects. Seeing me being so solemn, they were all honored. Therefore, although translating the classics is a very difficult job, they still do it wholeheartedly.

From 1968 until now, our association has published more than a hundred classics that have been translated into Western languages. Those scriptures have been circulated throughout all countries, and are considered very important by people of all countries. Although the translation work cannot be said to be perfect, it is true that it has awakened many people who were dreaming, causing them to have true faith in the Buddha Dharma. Furthermore, through this method of testing, it has the same effect as when we throw away a stone to gain access to a precious pearl.

We hope that in the future, people will do the translation work more deeply and reach a more complete level.

Until today, I still carry in my heart the ambition to translate classics and organize education. If I can't do it, I won't close my eyes when I die.

Lecture on June 15, 1987

Studying Buddhism -

Focus on Practice

When studying Buddha Dharma, we should focus on practice. If we just talk and don't practice, even if we speak so well that it grows branches, leaves, and flowers, it still belongs to illusion. So it's like only talking about food but not eating it, like counting treasures for others, having no benefit for yourself, is deceiving yourself and deceiving others. We should ask ourselves: "How should I be a monk? How should I be a lay person? What should I be like as a Buddhist?" Don't just worry about washing other people's clothes, to the point where you work hard and sweat, and your clothes are still dirty.

When studying the scriptures, we should bring the scriptures into harmony with our own body, mind, and life and ask ourselves: "Can I follow this Dharma? Can I practice with an upright mind and a true mind? Am I just a lazy person, wasting time in Buddhist teachings? Am I a person with a head as hard as a rock, a person who often talks but never does anything?" We should reflect back, examine ourselves and ask ourselves: "In the end, what kind of Buddhist do I want to be?"

As a true Buddhist, you will not be afraid of anyone talking about your mistakes. When we are at fault and someone points it out, we should accept it. Regardless of whether the critic is more or less intellectual than us, older or younger than us, male or female, we should all accept it, not argue or argue for ourselves. Knowing that you are wrong but not willing to correct it is a mistake. That's why it is said: "If you have a mistake, you can correct it. It's considered nothing. If you hide it, the crime will increase." If you keep making excuses to hide your mistakes, that will only increase your karma.

When seeing a person breaking the precepts or breaking the law, Bhikkhus who keep the precepts can expel or reprimand that person. But if the person is not at fault, and you keep saying that he or she is at fault, that is not right. Or someone accidentally makes a mistake, you shouldn't pick on that person's bad habits. You should also not say what is right in front of you, but say what is wrong behind your back; Or in front of people, they say there's no problem, but behind their backs, they say a lot of nonsense. There are some people who don't know themselves and think they are very good. They like to show off their talents to make a name for themselves, make friends, form parties, and interact closely with people. Such people will not be allowed in Buddhism.

People who practice Buddhism need to maintain their spiritual mind and practice mind every day. If we deceive others or lie to ourselves, we are at fault with others, but also with ourselves and are the ones creating sinful karma in Buddhism.

Lecture on June 16, 1987

noi_dung:
Studying Buddhism - Focusing on Practice / 326 Bodhicitta is the True Mind /

What is Bodhi mind? Bodhi is a Sanskrit noun, translated as "Enlightenment," meaning the path to enlightenment. Bodhi mind is the fundamental true mind, which is also the mind without confusion. A confused mind is a mind that creates karma, a mind that is not enlightened. Therefore, we must know clearly whether this path is easy or difficult to follow. Knowing the route clearly then we can reach the goal. Furthermore, Bodhi mind means that when we walk, stand, lie, or sit, we all adhere to the law, and that law is precepts. Simply put: "Where evil acts, good acts serve."

Evil actions are precepts. There are five Precepts: Killing, Dao, Lust, Hope, and Alcohol. Doing good deeds means practicing the ten good deeds. Our body, speech, and mind have a total of ten evils. The body commits murder, morality, and lust; Verbal offenses include: false language, false language, evil language, double tongue; Violations of the mind: greed, anger, ignorance. If we don't do these ten evil things, then we have already practiced the ten good things. Let me now briefly explain as follows:

The body has three evils: Killing, religion, and lust. In fact, there are many people who do not know good and evil, but they know and still try to commit crimes. Regarding killing, most people know that killing living beings is not right, but they still violate the precept of killing.

Stealing means taking something that is not given to you, knowing clearly that stealing is not good, but they still steal. Adultery is lust for the flesh, it is an illusion of pleasure, not real. Because this type of pleasure is fake, people can easily become infatuated and forget true pleasure. This is a common disease of people. No one recognizes the real thing, but everyone rushes after the fake one.

That's why it is said: "If you can sell a thousand counterfeits in one day, you can sell ten thousand times, you can sell a thousand fakes in a day, but it's difficult to sell a real one in ten days." People are so strange like that!

Our mental karma commits three evil things such as: Greed, anger and ignorance. Greed is an insatiable greed. Some people keep thinking: "If I had a million, I would be very satisfied." But when he got one million, he thought about ten million, even ten billion. No amount of money can satisfy that greed.

There are verses as follows:

Chung Nhat Mang Mang Chi Vi Co, Dac Willow Storm Phan Huu Tu Y,

Both food and drink are abundant

It's a shame to think of a tall and beautiful wife,

Thu Ha Kieu's wife is pure and beautiful,

Entering and exiting a small boat and plane,

Rotating aircraft and equipment,

Huu is an official who is taken advantage of,

Five products, four products, minor concerns,

Three products, two products, wild hysteria,

The first rank is equivalent to slapping the Prime Minister,

The male front of the throne ascended the throne,

One day, the throne sits on the throne,

Huu thought of becoming a fairyland.

Mean:

Busy all day just because of hunger,

Having enough food to think about clothes,

When both food and clothing are enough,

So I thought I wanted a tall house and a beautiful wife.

Marry a beautiful wife, a pretty concubine,

There are still a few ships and planes missing.

When purchasing enough ships, boats and aircraft,

Not yet my position is despised by others,

Five products Four products criticized as small,

Third grade and second grade are still low,

Appointed Prime Minister of the First Dynasty,

I want to wear the crown to the throne,

One day on the throne,

I want to play chess with Tien again.

People are busy all day just because they worry about filling their stomachs. When the stomach is full, people think about beautiful clothes, wear straight Western clothes and like to associate with high-class officials in society. When it's enough to eat well and dress well, people think about marrying a beautiful wife or getting a handsome husband. When they have a beautiful wife, a pretty concubine, or a handsome husband, they think about carriages, buying a famous car, and even want to have a plane to go there and here. When they have enough planes and cars, they think that if they don't have a mandarin position, they will be looked down upon. So they went to the official's school again. Being an official of 5th grade, 4th grade, up to 3rd grade, 2nd grade, they still criticize him as small. Finally, they reach the rank of First Rank, which is Prime Minister or Minister of State. But that's not enough, they still want to be President or Emperor. Once they are promoted to the palace as Emperor, they want to become Immortals, live forever and be immortal and play chess with the Immortals.

That is the image of our human's bottomless greed. Even though he has a fortune of thousands, he wants to take full control of the national economy. Once you grasp the national economy, you even want to grasp the economic network of the entire world. In short, there are two types of people in the world, one is greedy for fame, the other is greedy for profit. People who are greedy for fame try to use thousands of methods to make their reputation bigger. People who are greedy for profit are devoted to finding every scheme to earn more and more money. It's all caused by greed.

There is also anger in the heart. Anger means an angry mind, burning with anger, called: "Deficiency in virtue, loss of virtue" means lack of virtue is like a head covered in smoke. People with intense heat are as if their heads were covered in smoke all day long, with hot air rushing up. That is a sign of lack of virtue.

Truly noble people do not get angry. If they have a hot nature, they must definitely restrain themselves, subdue, and regulate their body and mind to be calm and know how to turn anger into gentleness, knives and knives into jade and silk.

The three poisons of greed, anger, and ignorance are interconnected. All human sorrows come from desire. When we have desires, we look outside to find what we need. When we see something nice, we want to take it as our own. If we can't take it, we get angry. Once angry, our minds become dark and confused, then become stupid. This stupidity does not refer to the stupidity of white elephants, but refers to people who do not know reason and are confused about the law of cause and effect, because the cognitive ability of the mind has been obscured. These three poisons are the root of all afflictions. To eliminate afflictions, we must first cut off the roots of the three poisons of greed, anger, and ignorance.

Our speech karma can easily commit four mistakes such as: false language, false speech, bad speech and double tongue. Idiot speech is speaking nonsense, untruthful words, or saying improper words, causing the listener to have impure delusions. False speech is untruthful, deceitful speech. Evil speech is using cruel words to scold someone, making it impossible for the listener to bear it. Bilingualism means talking about right and wrong, inciting the two sides to separate, like a two-headed snake.

Above is a brief explanation of the ten evils of body, speech, and mind. If we can turn the ten evils into ten good things, carefully guarding them so as not to violate them, that means keeping the precepts. Bodhicitta is a nickname for the precepts. Precepts teach us to be enlightened. Bodhi mind is the seed of goodness inherent in everyone's mind. If we do not forget the Bodhi mind, our good roots will not be interrupted. Not being confused means Bodhi mind. Let us try to cultivate the Bodhi seeds to grow, and head straight on the path to Buddhahood.

Lecture on June 18, 1987

O Many Buddhas -

Frequently Encounter Good Things

Every year at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, the Buddha Bathing Ceremony is held outdoors. It was so hot today, some people waited outside for a long time, exposed to the sun and sweating. Actually, the sunshine is also a test to see if you sincerely come here to bathe the Buddha or not. Even if you have a sincere heart and are exposed to a little bit of sunlight, you won't feel miserable. If you are not sincere, you will not be able to bear it. However, there are some people who can't stand it anymore. So in the future we may change the method of bathing the Buddha for the better. Coming out of the main hall, the crowd can walk a little further, then walk around to bathe the Buddha and return to the main hall. This way people will not have to wait long outside.

The method of bathing the Buddha here is called "two dragons and water," which is like two dragons spraying water. People came out from both sides of the main hall, looking like two dragons coming together to bathe the Buddha.

Among the people attending the meeting today, some are sick or have encountered miserable things. Each person's situation is different. But because everyone is so sincere, I believe that the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will be very happy and say: "Good men and good women! You can endure such heat to come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to attend the Buddha Bathing Ceremony. Then all the things you desire, you will be satisfied and satisfied!" So people with illnesses will get better, people with dangerous situations will become auspicious, and all invisible disasters will be eliminated.

You sincerely develop Bodhi mind to believe in Buddha, this cannot be bought even if you use money. So today, I would like to pray for everyone. I hope everything goes as you wish, and you always diligently walk the Bodhi path and soon attain Buddhahood.

When you come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, do you notice how this place is different from other places? Let me tell you that here when we eat, we don't talk, it's a place that's different from other places. If we don't talk, food will digest more easily. If we talk too much, it will be difficult to digest, and will cause many strange diseases. Because the Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas wants to save all humanity, we must first help everyone stay healthy. If my body is not healthy, how can I help others? Therefore, our learning is wisdom, our focus is a healthy body.

While eating, we should focus on eating, not choosing. Even if the food isn't delicious, I should still eat a little. If we chase away the demons of greed, laziness, and sleepiness, then everything will be good. This philosophy contains very rich truths. As long as you understand how to eat, how to dress, and how to sleep, you will definitely become rich. Why don't people get rich? Because they are so lazy!

Therefore, it is said: "Thrifty rules the family, the family is prosperous, and the family is rich

Teacher, noble son." So we don't need to buy any stocks or shares to get rich. If you want to make more money, you just need to bow to Buddha more.

Someone said: "I spend all day worrying about buying stocks, why do you say such inauspicious words? So I definitely won't make money." If you want to make money, then bow to Buddha a little more. Dear Buddha, it's even better than buying stocks.

In the future, if you have friends coming to attend the Buddha's Birthday ceremony, you should inform them in advance that you will not eat meat, drink alcohol, smoke marijuana or drugs, or dance here. This place is not an entertainment viewing area, nor is it like the gambling center in RENO. You should tell people that here we only focus on keeping the body healthy and cultivating the mind. Therefore, we should not be greedy for pleasures, such as luxury cars and beautiful clothes, because that is a waste of money. Money is like dung and soil, just see if you know how to use it or not. Like manure, it can be used as fertilizer for rice seedlings, but cannot be eaten. Similar to the above reason, money must also be used to be true to its meaning.

Lecture on June 23, 1987

tieu_de: Many Praises to Buddha - Often Encounter Good Things / 333 Five Demons Destroying Houses /

noi_dung:
Many Praises to Buddha - Often Encounter Good Things / 333 Five Demons Destroying Houses /

"Impermanent ghosts" are not just one type, but have at least five types: Blue, yellow, red, white, black (Blue, Yellow, Pink, White, Black). Based on the theory that the five elements coordinate with the five organs in the human body and also correspond to the five colors, five seasons, five seasons and five directions. Below is a summary, if explained in detail its reasoning would be endless.

- Can - wood - winter - spring - youth.

- Heart - fire - south - lower - red.

- Lung - metal - western - autumn - white.

- Spleen - earth - middle - long lower - yellow.

- Kidney - water - north - east - black.

The Five Elements have the logic of "mutual generation and mutual interference." The five types of impermanent demons are also based on the principle of the five elements being mutually exclusive, and can cause our five internal organs to develop many related diseases.

- Black Demons are impermanent - For example, people with kidney disease. And the kidney belongs to water and is black in color. Because water overcomes fire, it affects the heart and causes illness.

- Hoang Quy is impermanent - The spleen belongs to the earth, yellow color. The spleen is diseased because earth overcomes water, so it in turn affects the kidneys.

- Thanh Quy is impermanent - Liver belongs to wood, green color. Liver disease is caused by wood overcoming earth, then it will affect the spleen and become sick.

- The White Ghost is impermanent - The lungs are metallic and white in color. Metal overcomes wood, causing lung disease, which also affects the liver.

- Red Devils are impermanent - Heart belongs to fire, red color. Heart disease is caused by fire overcoming metal. So when the heart is sick, it can also affect the function of the lungs.

Thus, the five elements are mutually exclusive, and the diseases of the five internal organs are also born according to the cyclic evil nature of a certain law.

One impermanent demon can gather into five impermanent demons. This is enough to see that human life is impermanent, just in the space of breathing in and out. People can die, people can also live again. These five impermanent demons have a tremendous influence on human physiology and psychology. But they don't come naturally. It's not an overnight thing. But because during the time people grow from childhood to adulthood, they accumulate little by little, until eventually it causes a situation where they cannot collect anymore. Research on the causes, all kinds of evil diseases, even birth and death, come from "ignorance". If ignorance is destroyed, all diseases and all impermanent demons will no longer exist. Ignorance is the root of all evil, afflictions, illness, suffering, and even birth and death. People should learn how to expand their wisdom. When we have wisdom, we will be able to operate the five elements, turning the principles of "interdependence" into "mutual birth," as we can do: metal gives birth to water, water gives birth to wood, wood gives birth to fire, fire gives birth to earth, earth gives birth to metal. "Mutual birth" means helping and guiding each other, being able to transform knives and spears into jade and silk.

Therefore, we must destroy ignorance to gain wisdom. Having wisdom means we will be able to destroy all attachments. Why do people have attachments? Because ignorance is a monster. Ignorance is the root of crime and disaster. Therefore, practitioners must definitely destroy ignorance. Once the basic problem has been eliminated, other problems will be easily resolved.

So say:

Having attained one's true purpose, one is saddened by the end of the world, Like a pure lapis lazuli that holds the moon, The ability to solve the test is like a pearl of will, Self-benefit and others are inexhaustible.

Mean:

Just take the roots, don't worry about the tips,

Like a pure mirror containing the moon's treasure, Having understood this wish-fulfilling gem,

Benefiting yourself and others will never end.

Illness is caused by bad karma and evil spirits. We also cannot use our physical eyes to observe disease phenomena in such a simple way. Because the patient has bad karma, there are many ghosts and ghosts who follow him to collect debts and cause trouble for the patient. Therefore, depending on the condition of the disease, simply relying on medicine for treatment is not enough. The patient must also clearly understand their own karmic causes and karma. Adding Buddha Dharma mantras will make the treatment more effective, so "when the medicine comes, the disease will be eliminated" has immediate results. Therefore, in ancient times there were physicians who were honored as "miracle physicians".

like Hua Tuo of the Eastern Han Dynasty, Ton Tu Mac of the Tang Dynasty. As for their virtue in treating illness, it is inconceivable. Those people all believe in Buddha, it's just that their medical records are not recorded.

There are a number of patients whose therapists have had results. However, there are also patients who have been cured by doctors for one disease, but another disease develops. As soon as this disease is cured, another new disease appears. Sometimes they suffer from two or three such illnesses in a row, also because karma keeps bothering them behind them. Just like the Doctor has beaten back the demon that causes the disease, this demon will go find another demon to help, then they will return to attack another grave of the sick person. Demons also often act collectively in groups and groups.

There is a Chinese proverb: "The disease has entered the high wilderness," the disease has entered the heart, indicating that the disease is serious and cannot be cured.

In the Tale of the Ten Years of Success, it is recorded as follows: Tan Canh Cong was sick, Tan Ba ​​invited Cao Hoan to treat him. While Cao Hoan had not yet arrived, Tan Canh Cong had a dream about two villains.

One said: "Ah! The doctor is so good, I'm afraid he will hurt me. What should I do?"

The other said: We live above in a desolate place, below in a high place, so what can we do? (The place below the heart is called Cao, Hoang is the place below the heart above the diaphragm).

Then the doctor came and said: There is nothing that can be done about this disease. Above Hoang, below Cao, the work cannot be done, and the circulation cannot come. The medicine doesn't penetrate and can't cure it.

Tan Canh Cong said: Physician! Hoang is the diaphragm, Cao is the tong cach.

Thanks to a dream, Tan Canh Cong knew the location of the two little devils who had crawled into his body. After that, he invited the Qin physician Cao Huan to come and treat him. Cao Hoan was originally a good student of physician Bien Thuoc, a famous physician at that time, but he had no way to save Tan Canh Cong's illness. Because the upper part is wild and the lower part is high, no amount of acupuncture treatment can clear it. Therefore, later generations, taking advantage of this story, created the idiom "Sickness of entering Cao Hoang" to describe an incurable disease that cannot be cured.

In the world, there are hundreds of thousands of strange diseases, all of which are called: "Multiple complications," incurable diseases that are difficult to treat, causing even doctors to give up. But these miscellaneous and strange diseases are not recorded even in medical books.

When I first became a monk, I often treated people's illnesses. But I do not write prescriptions for patients, nor do I use any surgery or acupuncture procedures. I only rely on my sincerity to recite Buddhist mantras. That sincere will is to save people. At that time, I didn't know anything about saving demons and ghosts. In my mind, I only had the thought of saving people, so I made the demons unhappy. Because when you heal people, the demons think you want to oppose them, so their anger spreads to the healer.

When I was still in the Northeast, there were countless mountain monsters and water monsters coming from all directions, day and night, six times a day, they were watching me and waiting for an opportunity to take revenge. If there is a slight opening, they will take the opportunity to rush in. It's true that I can't take precautions, so I often suffer losses. Either I'm the only one who's at a disadvantage, or it's causing the people around me to suffer as well. Most people there knew absolutely nothing about the situation inside. One time, water flooded Dong Tinh village, drowning thirty people in just four hours, and washing away more than eight hundred roofs. The flood came very quickly, and the person standing on the furnace bed (the sleeping place above the fireplace lid) also drowned. That number of disadvantaged victims is also my fault. The devils and demons wanted to flood the water to drown me, but in the end I did not drown, but involved many people. To this day, I still feel uneasy about that incident and feel very sorry for those who died.

Lecture on July 26, 1987

Summary of Venerable Master Hsuan Hua

! ! ! ! !

Venerable Tuyen Hoa's family name is Bach, his real name is An Tu, his name is Do Luan. He is from Songcheng district, Songjiang province in Northeast China, that is, Manchuria. His father's name was Phu Hai, specializing in farming. Her mother's family name was Ho, and she gave birth to eight children, five boys and three girls, and he was the youngest.

He respectfully took care of his parents as if he were Buddha. Soon, rumors about His filial piety spread throughout all four directions. At that time, everyone called him Bach Hieu Tu (filial son of the Bach family).

When he was 19 years old, his mother passed away; At that time, he said goodbye to his relatives and went to the temple to worship Venerable Thuong Tri as his teacher and took refuge, officially becoming a monk and receiving ordination. After that, he returned to his mother's grave to pay filial piety for three years. During that time, he lived in a small thatched hut, meditated every day, recited Mahayana sutras and recited Amitabha Buddha's name. Many times he sat in meditation and then entered concentration, continuously for many weeks without leaving the meditation bed.

After World War II, he traveled everywhere. Finally, after traveling more than three thousand miles, he arrived at Nam Hoa Pagoda and paid homage to the Great Wise One of that time, Elder Venerable Hu Van. The Venerable was 109 years old at that time. As soon as he saw Him, the Venerable immediately recognized His enlightenment. At that time, the Venerable said: "Like this, like like!" and He also replied: “As it is, as it is!” At that time, the Elder Venerable confirmed his attainment and he officially became the ninth Patriarch of the Quy Ngoc dharma lineage.

After that, the Venerable Master taught him to stay at the temple and take on the role of Head of the Institute of Precepts of Nam Hoa Temple.

In 1950, he left the temple and left for Huong ûng. Here, he lives in an isolated cave, with nothing to do with worldly dust or worldly affairs. Soon, countless Chinese and Mainland monks came to Hong Kong as refugees and they needed his support. Finally, according to destiny, he left the cave, established a lecture hall and two pagodas, and assisted him in building many other ashrams.

In 1962, he came to San Francisco, USA. Here, in a small warehouse, he persistently practiced in silence, waiting for the opportunity to propagate the Dharma to ripen. At that time, he called himself "Mo Trung Tang" (the monk in the grave), he was Hoat Tu Nhan (the one who died but was still alive). The disciples who understood his true practice were very moved and respectfully supported and made offerings to him.

In 1968, he knew the opportunity had come, he said: "A rush of flowers will bloom with five petals." That summer, he presided over the Shurangama Sutra teaching conference for 96 days. When the Dharma ended, indeed, the first five Americans asked to join him.

From then on, he continued to preside over many Dharma conferences and lecture on sutras such as: Heart Sutra, Ksitigarbha Sutra, Dharma Sutra, Dharma Jewel Platform Sutra, etc. In 1971, He preached the supreme collection of Mahayana, which is the Avatamsaka Sutra.

Along with preaching the Sutras and preaching the Dharma, he also made countless other merits of saving sentient beings. In 1976, he established the Holy City of Buddha as a base to propagate Dharma in the United States. At the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, he built a monastic system, trained monks and nuns, studied them, and created outstanding grace for true practice.

tom_tat: Buddha's Preaching of the Amitabha Sutra - Unlike other sutras, because this is a sutra that no one asked for, but Buddha preached it himself. This sutra was summarized by the Venerable Master Hsuan Hua, explaining the meaning and method of practice, so that we can…
noi_dung:
Summary of Venerable Master Hsuan Hua / 342 Introduction to the Sutras /

Online Catalog: http://bttsonline.org

Buddha's Preaching of the Amitabha Sutra - Unlike other sutras, because this is a sutra that no one asked for, but Buddha preached it himself. This sutra was summarized by Venerable Hsuan Hua's meaning and method of practice, so that we can better understand the function and value of the Amitabha Sutra. The content refers to life and is interspersed with interesting stories about Buddha's great disciples. The book has additional comments and many basic Buddhist nouns.

Diamond Sutra - The entire sutra's name is called the Diamond Prajnaparamita Sutra. The use of the sutra is to destroy all attachments and entanglements about appearances: self, person, sentient beings, and recipient. For example, when a Bodhisattva practices giving alms, he still believes that he is the one giving alms and that there are people receiving alms, that means he is not a Bodhisattva. Therefore, the Buddha said: Bodhisattvas should not rely on form to give alms. In the Dharma Ending Age, if someone hears the Diamond Sutra and immediately has faith, understands it, accepts it, and upholds it, it is truly rare, because people in the world often have a mind that clings to self and the Dharma.

Khai Thi - Includes teachings of H.T. Tuyen Hoa on basic ethics such as: human dignity for family, society and humanity in the world. With practical examples, H.T. only shows the noble virtues of the ancient Sages so that everyone can follow them. Along with these short sermons, H.T. always earnestly calls for us to value morality and morality and remember to keep a peaceful mind in daily activities. Because that is also one of the righteous weapons that help make the world peaceful.

Mahayana Commentary on 100 Dharmas of Minh Mon - This treatise from the beginning had up to 84,000 dharmas. Because living beings are naturally confused, Bodhisattva Maitreya shortened it into the Yogacara Master Grounds, which includes 600 dharmas. But there is still much left for the future sentient beings. Bodhisattva Thien Than then briefly summarized it into 100 dharmas. This Treatise is simple and easy to understand, a shortcut leading us to the door of Buddhism, very suitable for those with Mahayana nature.

Vinh Gia Trinh Dao Song - A song of enlightenment that was passed down during the life of Great Master Vinh Gia Huyen Giac, Tang Dynasty. And he is a monk who has been in the temple since childhood. The great master was intelligent and well-educated and knew how to practice diligently, so he soon became enlightened. By reading the Vimalakirti Sutra, his mind glowed and was confirmed by the Sixth Patriarch. Master Vinh Gia wrote a song explaining the experiences of someone who has realized the true nature and understood the principles of Zen. He used his singing voice to let everyone see the true, unborn and immortal nature that is available to him. If we understand and practice according to this song, we can also attain enlightenment like Great Master Vinh Gia.

Dharma Lotus Sutra, Pham Pho Mon - The most familiar sutra is Am Pho Mon, often recited by monks and lay people. The content of book h is explained by Venerable Hsuan Hua about the compassionate virtues and miraculous uses of Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara while saving sentient beings.

Master Bodhidharma - Is the 28th Patriarch in India but in China he is considered the Patriarch. Because he considered that the Mahayana nature in China was ripe, he did not go there with difficulty and difficulty to propagate Buddhism. But when he arrived in China, no one recognized him, not even King Luong Vo did not respect him. Then again, out of jealousy and hatred, someone tried to poison the Patriarch again. Even though he encountered many obstacles, he remained calm and unharmed. Knowing that his fate had not yet come, he meditated at Hung Nhi mountain for 9 years facing the wall of time. At that time, Dharma Master Than Quang also knelt in front of the mountain cave for 9 years to pray to the First Patriarch. To prove his sincerity in seeking the Dharma, Lord Than Quang cut off his own hand, causing blood to fall and dye the white snow red. As a result, Sr. Bodhisattva found someone to transmit the initiation. Than Quang became the Second Patriarch Hui Kha to continue spreading the lineage of Buddhism. The book is accompanied by images depicting a very vivid story about Bodhisattva.

According to tradition, every year on the occasion of Buddha's Birthday, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas and the Dharma Realm Holy City hold a course to celebrate the Thousand Buddhas Repentance. This is a good fate for everyone to gather to worship Buddha together. At the same time, it is also an opportunity for everyone to focus on worshiping 10,000 times within 3 weeks, hoping to eliminate their sins. The sutra consists of Chinese characters, with notes and Vietnamese characters attached. Very convenient for participants in the Dharma conference, medium

catch up with the masses and understand the meaning of the sutras while worshiping.

LU Luc - This book is an excerpt and compilation of the profound teachings and recommendations of Venerable Master Tuyen Hoa, the founder of Ten Thousand Buddhas Thanh ønh Pagoda. The content of the book is words that explain how to raise the spirit of religion and awaken the ignorant sentient beings. Many times the Venerable Master's words were very brief and seemed very strict, but if anyone realized it and knew how to practice it, they would benefit immensely.

This Vajra Shout: - Record the questions and answers of the Venerable Master and his disciples and people during the Venerable Master's trips to propagate the Dharma in Taiwan. The Venerable Master's answers are aimed at correcting wrong views and superstitions and awakening confused souls. Sometimes He just gave a simple, short answer that contained a very reasonable meaning. Sometimes He mixes it up with a bit of humor

but imbued with morality, making the listener attentively pay attention and accept his teachings with joy. While watching the questions and answers, we can feel like the Venerable Master is directly answering our own questions.

Buddhist Sutra Forty-Two Chapters - This is the sutra translated into Chinese for the first time when Buddhism was transmitted from India to China. This sutra includes 42 chapters of Buddhist teachings, which are also 42 paragraphs, or 42 teachings preached by the Buddha on methods of practice. People who practice religion must be determined to eliminate desires and attachments and know how to let go. But mainly, the practitioner needs to know how to control himself to subdue his mind, only then can he achieve results. This sutra is not only very beneficial for monastics, but also lay people can study and practice.

Tam Bo Nhat Bai - Diary recounting the pilgrimage over a thousand miles of two American monks, disciples of Venerable Master Tuyen Hoa. With a journey lasting more than 10 months, the two monks sincerely bowed every three steps from San Francisco to Marblemount, Washington state to pray for world peace. Tam Bo Nhat Bai raised a sincere wish for all humanity, a rare noble act that actually happened right on American soil.

Phap Nhu Tham An - Commemorating the late Venerable Master Tuyen Hoa's Ten Years of Nirvana

It is a collection of a number of writings by monastic and lay disciples from China, America, Canada, Vietnam, Singapore, Malaysia... to commemorate the revered teacher. They expressed their deep gratitude for the valuable experiences they learned with Venerable Master Tuyen Hoa. Although the revered teacher is now absent, his valuable memories and lessons will forever be engraved in the hearts of many disciples. Through these articles, with the stories told, readers will have the opportunity to learn more about the special, skillful but very practical teachings that the Venerable Master has guided, depending on the nature of each disciple.

Essay on Developing Bodhi Mind - Through the article, Great Master Am Province urgently advised us to urgently develop Bodhi mind. He also clearly explained the reasons as well as clearly analyzed why we must develop Bodhi mind. This Bodhi mind is very important and essential in our practice, and is also the main factor to become Buddha. We should learn from the Great Master to develop Bodhi mind and establish Bodhisattva conduct to escape the cycle of birth and death. Therefore, this article on Encouraging the Development of Bodhi Mind occupies an extremely important position in Buddhism.

The Sixth Patriarch's Platform Sutra - The content of the sutra recounts the life and process of attaining the Dharma of the Sixth Patriarch. During his life of practicing Buddhism, he spread the Dharma teachings everywhere so that people who study the religion can receive their original mind and see their original nature. The Sixth Patriarch's Dharma Jewel Platform Sutra includes the sermons of the Sixth Patriarch Huineng copied for transmission. The Patriarch was originally illiterate, but when he heard someone chanting the Vajra Sutra to the words: "Without a place of residence, the mind is born," he suddenly became enlightened. Afterwards, he received the seal of approval from the Fifth Patriarch Hoang Nhan and passed down his bowl and robe and became the sixth Patriarch.

Eight Rules

of the Institute of Classical Translation

Translators must free themselves from the motive of pursuing fame and profit.

Translators must cultivate their minds and cultivate their nature and get rid of the habit of arrogance.

Translators must control themselves and not praise themselves and then criticize others.

Translators must not consider themselves the standard, the measure, and then degrade others by finding mistakes in their work.

The translator must take Buddha's mind as his own mind.

The translator must use Trach Phap Nhan to judge what is the truth.

The translator must respectfully request Cao Sangha and Dai Duc in the ten directions to prove his translation.

Translators must happily spread Buddhist teachings by printing Sutras, Vinaya, and Treatises once their translation is proven to be correct.
